aUSAPICA.meaning: API Cushing crude oil number — industry-source weekly stocks at Cushing OK.
aUSAPICA.how_to_use: Released Tuesday evening before Wednesday's EIA report. Often moves prices on the prior-day Asia/Europe overnight session.

aUSOIAIA.meaning: API weekly crude oil imports — industry source for US crude imports, released Tuesday evening. Cross-check against EIA's official Wednesday release.
aUSOIAIA.how_to_use: Useful for forward-looking trade — API can drive overnight oil price moves before EIA confirms next morning. API methodology is voluntary reporting from refiners; EIA samples the full set, so discrepancies are usually resolved within 2-4 weeks of revisions.

aUSOIARA.meaning: API weekly crude oil runs (refinery throughput) — same conceptual measure as aUSEIACR but industry-sourced. Total crude processed in US refineries per day.
aUSOIARA.how_to_use: Drives demand for crude. Pair with utilization for tight-vs-loose signal. Hurricane season (Aug-Oct) on Gulf Coast can drop runs by 1-2mb/d for 2-3 weeks; major maintenance windows in spring and fall similarly reduce throughput.

aUSOIACA.meaning: API weekly crude oil stocks (industry inventory) — total US commercial crude inventory excluding SPR. Industry-sourced; released Tuesday evenings, one day before EIA.
aUSOIACA.how_to_use: Cross-check with EIA's official numbers. API often differs by 1-2 million barrels — a draw vs build divergence drives short-term oil-price moves. Markets initially trade API release; EIA next morning often confirms or reverses.

aUSOIADA.meaning: API weekly distillate (diesel + heating oil) inventories — total US distillate stocks. Q4 inventory builds for winter heating; Q2 builds for trucking demand.
aUSOIADA.how_to_use: More volatile than gasoline because two demand drivers: trucking (year-round, GDP-correlated) and heating (Q4-Q1, weather-correlated). Tight distillate stocks 2022-23 drove distillate crack spreads to record highs.

aUSOIAGA.meaning: API weekly gasoline inventories — total US gasoline stocks. Driving-season seasonality: drawdowns May-Aug as Memorial Day to Labor Day demand peaks.
aUSOIAGA.how_to_use: Cross-check with EIA gasoline stocks. Below 220M barrels = tight; above 245M = loose for the typical year. Inventories swing crack spreads (gasoline vs crude price differential).

aUSOIAHA.meaning: API weekly heating oil inventories — subset of distillate stocks (~25-30% of distillate). Q4 demand-driven for Northeast heating.
aUSOIAHA.how_to_use: Cross-check vs EIA heating oil stocks. Track heating-degree days (HDD) for demand pulse. Mild winters depress demand and build inventories; cold snaps drive draws and price spikes.

aUSOIAPA.meaning: API weekly product imports — refined product imports (gasoline, diesel, heating oil, jet fuel). Track for product-vs-crude import mix.
aUSOIAPA.how_to_use: US imports refined products mainly from Caribbean refineries (Trinidad, Curacao) and Europe. Falls when domestic refineries run higher; rises during US refinery outages.

aUSESECOP.description: United States, EMISSIONS - CARBON DIOXIDE, Volume, Commodity Fundamentals, Annual, British Petroleum
aUSESECOP.how_to_use: Annual EIA. Tracks US progress on emissions reductions. Has trended down post-2007.

aUSEIACI.meaning: EIA crude oil imports — official measure. Halved post-shale (2007 ~10mb/d → 2024 ~6mb/d) as US production rose from ~5mb/d to ~13mb/d.
aUSEIACI.how_to_use: Cross-check with API (aUSOIAIA). Track Saudi/OPEC+ vs Canadian share for geopolitical exposure: Canada is now the dominant US crude supplier (~60% of imports). Pipeline disruptions (Keystone, Enbridge) drive short-term spikes.

aUSEIAPI.meaning: EIA weekly petroleum products imports — official EIA measure of refined-products imports. Cross-check against API.
aUSEIAPI.how_to_use: Track for US refining-deficit signals: when product imports are persistently elevated, US refineries can't meet domestic demand. Used in trade-balance and consumer-fuel-price analyses.

aUSOIPIA.meaning: Imports, petroleum products, absolute change — week-over-week change in product imports.
aUSOIPIA.how_to_use: Volatility signal. Spikes during refinery outages or supply disruptions (Colonial Pipeline 2021, Hurricane Harvey 2017). Smooths to ~2-3 million bpd in normal weeks.

aUSNGIFA.meaning: Natural Gas Implied Flow (EIA) — backed-out demand calculated from production minus storage change. Captures total domestic + export demand for nat gas.
aUSNGIFA.how_to_use: Important for nat-gas storage and pricing. LNG exports have surged post-2016 (Sabine Pass, Cameron, Calcasieu Pass) — implied demand now includes ~14 Bcf/d of LNG exports. Track for cold-snap demand spikes (heating) and cooling-degree-day demand (electricity for AC).

aUSOICRA.description: Production, Crude Oil Inputs into Refineries, Absolute change
aUSOICRA.meaning: Crude oil inputs into refineries, absolute change (weekly) — pace of refinery throughput change.
aUSOICRA.how_to_use: Captures refinery activity changes. Maintenance turnarounds (spring + fall) drop runs by 1-2 mb/d temporarily; hurricanes (Aug-Oct Gulf Coast) similar magnitude. Watch for unscheduled drops as supply-disruption signal.

aUSOIDOA.meaning: Distillate production, absolute change (weekly) — pace of diesel + heating oil output change.
aUSOIDOA.how_to_use: Track for distillate-supply tightness signals. Elevated demand + flat production = tightening market. Diesel demand correlates with trucking/freight (real-economy proxy).

aUSPCOAL.how_to_use: Long-term decline. Down >50% from 2008 peak. Replaced by gas + renewables.

aUSEIACR.description: Production, EIA, Crude Oil Inputs into Refineries
aUSEIACR.meaning: EIA weekly crude oil inputs into refineries — refinery throughput. Largest single use of US crude. Demand pulse for crude-oil markets.
aUSEIACR.how_to_use: Tracks domestic crude demand at the refinery gate. Seasonal: peaks in summer driving season, troughs in fall maintenance turnarounds. Compare to refinery capacity utilization for slack-vs-tightness signal. Cross-check against API weekly numbers (aUSOIARA).

aUSEIADP.meaning: EIA weekly distillate fuel oil production — diesel + heating oil output from US refineries. Released in EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report each Wednesday.
aUSEIADP.how_to_use: Diesel demand is freight-driven (trucking + rail), a real-economy proxy. Heating oil demand is winter-weather-driven (Northeast US). Tight diesel supply in 2022 drove crack spreads to record highs — track distillate inventories alongside.

aUSEIAGP.how_to_use: Gasoline output — pairs with stocks for refining-margin analysis.

aUSEIAPRU.meaning: EIA Refinery Capacity Utilization. 85-95% normal range.
aUSEIAPRU.how_to_use: Drops sharply during hurricane season (Gulf shut-ins) and spring/fall maintenance (turnarounds). Pair refinery inputs with crude imports + crude production for fundamental balance. Below 85% = excess capacity, weak crack spreads.

aUSOIGOA.meaning: Gasoline production, absolute change (weekly) — pace of gasoline output change. Tracks driving-season supply response.
aUSOIGOA.how_to_use: Refineries shift product slate seasonally — more gasoline in summer, more distillate in winter. Watch for unusual divergences from seasonal pattern.

aUSOIRUA.description: Production, Refinery Capacity Utilization, Absolute change
aUSOIRUA.meaning: Refinery capacity utilization, weekly absolute change — pace of refinery slack tightening or loosening. EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report.
aUSOIRUA.how_to_use: Refinery utilization ~85-95% in normal operation. Hurricanes (Gulf Coast) and maintenance turnarounds drive temporary drops. Sustained sub-85% suggests demand softness or capacity loss; sustained 95%+ flags capacity constraint and crack-spread expansion.

aUSOICCA.description: Stock Levels, Cushing, Oklahoma Crude Oil excluding SPR, Absolute change
aUSOICCA.meaning: Cushing OK crude oil stocks ex-SPR, absolute change WoW.
aUSOICCA.how_to_use: WTI futures-deliverable supply. Below 25M bbl = tank tops empty risk.

aUSOILHA.description: Stock Levels, Distillate over 500 ppm sulfur, Absolute change
aUSOILHA.meaning: Stock levels, distillate over 500ppm sulfur, absolute change — high-sulfur distillate inventory pace of change.
aUSOILHA.how_to_use: Smaller specialty market. Track for bunker fuel and non-road diesel supply dynamics. Mainstream ULSD inventory (aUSOILDA) is the meaningful market gauge.

aUSOICIA.description: Stock Levels, EIA Weekly Crude Imports
aUSOICIA.meaning: EIA weekly crude oil imports stock levels — companion to import flow (aUSEIACI). Tracks aggregate US-bound crude inventory.
aUSOICIA.how_to_use: Use the flow series (aUSEIACI) for high-frequency tracking. Levels reflect logistics pipeline (in-transit cargoes plus port stocks).

aUSSCCO.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Cushing, Oklahoma Crude Oil excluding SPR
aUSSCCO.meaning: Cushing OK crude oil stocks ex-SPR — WTI futures delivery point. The most-watched single inventory location.
aUSSCCO.how_to_use: Below 25M bbl = tank tops empty risk; above 80M = oversupply. WTI-Brent spread widens (WTI discount) when Cushing is full; narrows when low.

aUSEIADS500.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Distillate over 500 ppm sulfur
aUSEIADS500.meaning: EIA weekly distillate stocks (>500ppm sulfur) — non-ULSD high-sulfur distillate. Used in non-road/marine fuel and some heating applications.
aUSEIADS500.how_to_use: Smaller pool than ULSD (the dominant US diesel grade). Track for non-road fuel market dynamics. Mostly relevant to specialty-fuel markets and bunker-fuel applications.

aUSEIAGS.meaning: Total US Gasoline Stocks. Released weekly with EIA petroleum status report.
aUSEIAGS.how_to_use: Builds during winter (low driving demand), draws during summer (peak driving). Below 5-year range = bullish gasoline cracks. Pre-Memorial Day stock builds often signal weak demand or oversupply.

aUSEIAPADD1.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1 (East Coast) — distillate inventories in PADD 1 (Northeast US). Heating-oil-heavy due to NE residential heating demand.
aUSEIAPADD1.how_to_use: Most weather-sensitive PADD for distillate. Cold winter draws drive product imports from Europe. PADD 1 supply matters for Northeast heating-oil prices and fuel-oil markets.

aUSEIAPADDA.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1A (New England) — sub-region of PADD 1. Highest heating-oil exposure (Maine through Connecticut).
aUSEIAPADDA.how_to_use: Most weather-driven inventory in US. Mild winters → builds; cold snaps → severe draws. Heating-oil dealer inventory turnover is key real-time indicator.

aUSEIAPADDB.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1B (Mid-Atlantic) — NY, NJ, PA, DE, MD region. Mix of heating and trucking demand.
aUSEIAPADDB.how_to_use: More commercial/trucking-driven than PADD 1A. Pipeline-supplied (Colonial Pipeline). Watch for major pipeline disruptions impacting Mid-Atlantic supply.

aUSEIAPADDC.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 1C (Lower Atlantic) — VA through FL. Less heating exposure than upper PADD 1; more trucking/agricultural demand.
aUSEIAPADDC.how_to_use: Pipeline + local refinery supplied. Hurricane-season disruptions (Aug-Oct) can sharply tighten regional supply.

aUSEIAPADD2.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 2 (Midwest) — Midwest US distillate inventory. Trucking/agriculture-heavy demand profile.
aUSEIAPADD2.how_to_use: Pipeline-supplied from Gulf Coast. Watch for tightness during ag-harvest periods (Sep-Nov) when farm diesel demand surges.

aUSEIAPADD3.how_to_use: Largest refining region. Gulf Coast crack spreads pricing reference.

aUSEIAPADD4.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 4 (Rocky Mountains) — small-volume PADD with limited refining capacity. Mostly truck/rail-supplied.
aUSEIAPADD4.how_to_use: Smallest PADD by distillate inventory. Local supply tightness can drive regional price spikes (Western Slope CO, MT, WY). Less liquid market than coastal PADDs.

aUSEIAPADD5.meaning: EIA distillate stocks, PADD 5 (West Coast) — West Coast US distillate inventory. CARB-spec fuel requirements complicate cross-PADD product transfers.
aUSEIAPADD5.how_to_use: Insulated from other PADDs by quality requirements. CARB diesel standards mean West Coast inventory is functionally separate market. Watch for CA-specific supply/demand events.

aUSEIAREF.how_to_use: RBOB grade — summer-spec gasoline. Tightens approaching summer driving.

aUSEIAHOS.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Strategic Petroleum Reserve
aUSEIAHOS.meaning: Strategic Petroleum Reserve stocks. Drained ~200M bbl in 2022 (Russia/Ukraine response under Biden admin). Refilling has been slow.
aUSEIAHOS.how_to_use: Below 350M bbl is historically low. Refill pace (target $67-72/bbl) tested by oil price moves. SPR can release ~1M bbl/day for sustained periods.

aUSEIACS.description: Stock Levels, EIA, Total Crude Oil excluding SPR
aUSEIACS.meaning: Total US Crude Oil Stocks excluding SPR — EIA weekly Wednesday release. The single most market-watched US oil-inventory series.
aUSEIACS.how_to_use: Big surprises vs API/consensus drive WTI intraday by 2-5%. Cushing-specific stocks (aUSSCCO) matter most for WTI futures (delivery point). Below 25M bbl Cushing = tank-tops empty risk; above 80M = oversupply pressure.

aUSEIADS.meaning: Total US Distillate Stocks (diesel + heating oil). Industrial + freight + winter heating demand.
aUSEIADS.how_to_use: Winter heating-oil cushion gauge — heavily watched in Q4. Distillate cracks often diverge from gasoline cracks based on freight cycle (diesel) vs travel cycle (gasoline).

aUSOILGA.meaning: Gasoline stock levels, absolute change (weekly) — pace of gasoline-inventory change.
aUSOILGA.how_to_use: Negative readings (draws) common in summer driving season; positive (builds) in winter. Below seasonal norm = tight market = price-supportive. Pair with refining margins for crack-spread direction.

aUSOILNA.description: Stock Levels, Natural Gas in Underground Storage, Lower 48 States, Absolute change
aUSOILNA.meaning: Natural gas in underground storage, Lower 48, absolute change.
aUSOILNA.how_to_use: Weekly NG storage change. Inverse of demand minus production.

aUSOILRA.description: Stock Levels, Reformulated Gasoline, Absolute change
aUSOILRA.meaning: Reformulated gasoline (RFG) stock levels, absolute change — RFG is used in major metro areas (CA, NY, NJ, etc.) for clean-air requirements.
aUSOILRA.how_to_use: Smaller stock pool than conventional gasoline. Track for regional supply tightness in metro markets. Subject to specific summer-blend mandates (RVP rules) that drive seasonal shifts.

aUSOILCA.description: Stock Levels, Total Crude Oil excluding SPR, Absolute change
aUSOILCA.meaning: Total Crude Oil stock levels (excluding SPR), absolute change — week-over-week change in commercial crude inventory.
aUSOILCA.how_to_use: Build vs draw is the key oil-price-driving signal. Builds = bearish (oversupply); draws = bullish (tightness). Winter: typically builds; spring: typically draws. Seasonality matters.

aUSOILDA.description: Stock Levels, Total Distillate, Absolute change
aUSOILDA.meaning: Total Distillate stock levels, absolute change — week-over-week change in diesel + heating oil inventory.
aUSOILDA.how_to_use: Build/draw signal for distillate market. Trucking-demand-driven year-round + heating-demand seasonal Q4. Watch for tight readings as diesel-crack-spread expansion signal.

aUSWSETHES.description: Weekly U.S. Ending Stocks of Fuel Ethanol, Commodity Fundamentals, Weekly, EIA - Energy Information Administration, United States
aUSWSETHES.meaning: US ending stocks of fuel ethanol — weekly.
aUSWSETHES.how_to_use: Ethanol blendstock. Tied to gasoline demand and corn prices.

aUSWPETHES.description: Weekly U.S. Oxygenate Plant Production of Fuel Ethanol, Commodity Fundamentals, Weekly, EIA - Energy Information Administration, United States
aUSWPETHES.meaning: Weekly US oxygenate plant production of fuel ethanol — domestic ethanol production for gasoline blending (E10, E15, E85).
aUSWPETHES.how_to_use: RFS (Renewable Fuel Standard) mandates drive ~13B gallons/year. Corn-price-sensitive on input side. Track for ag-policy implications: corn demand for ethanol affects food prices.

aUSOESNA.how_to_use: Weekly USDA Export Sales report. Drives soyoil futures.

aUSINTCONB/A.description: Interest Paid by Persons, Total excluding mortgage
aUSINTCONB/A.meaning: Total interest paid by persons (households + nonprofits) excluding mortgage interest. From BEA Personal Income & Outlays.
aUSINTCONB/A.how_to_use: Cyclical: rises with consumer credit balances and effective rates. Pair with consumer credit outstanding to see whether the burden is balance-driven or rate-driven. Heavy in late-cycle when revolving balances peak.

aUSMOV659A.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score 620-659
aUSMOV659A.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 620-659 — subprime band. NY Fed Household Debt and Credit Report quarterly. Sensitive to lending-standard shifts.
aUSMOV659A.how_to_use: Volumes rise when banks ease standards (cycle peaks) and collapse in tightening cycles. As a share of total originations, this band fell from 15-20% pre-2008 to 5-8% post-Dodd-Frank — a structural shift toward higher-quality lending.

aUSMOV719A.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score 660-719
aUSMOV719A.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 660-719 — near-prime/middle band. The pre-2008 mainstream borrower segment, now a smaller share given migration toward higher scores post-crisis.
aUSMOV719A.how_to_use: Watch share vs prime (720-759) as a cycle indicator: rising near-prime share indicates lender willingness to extend credit further. Falling share signals tightening — a leading indicator of housing slowdowns.

aUSMOV759A.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score 720-759
aUSMOV759A.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 720-759 — prime band. Largest single share of originations historically. Standard conforming-loan borrower.
aUSMOV759A.how_to_use: Most stable band through cycles. Fell ~70% from 2021 peak as rate hikes killed refinance volumes. Use as the 'baseline mortgage market' gauge — purchase originations in this band track home-sales volume.

aUSMOV620A.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score <620
aUSMOV620A.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score below 620 — deep subprime band. Very small post-2008 (banks largely don't lend here; FHA dominates this credit-quality segment).
aUSMOV620A.how_to_use: Monitor for any uptick as a sign of loosening credit standards. Pre-2008, this band exceeded $50B/quarter. Post-Dodd-Frank QM rules effectively shut down deep-subprime conventional lending; FHA fills the gap with explicit federal guarantee.

aUSMOV760A.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score >760
aUSMOV760A.meaning: Mortgage originations with risk score 760+ — super-prime band. Largest dollar volume share (highest credit-quality borrowers tend to take larger loans for higher-priced homes).
aUSMOV760A.how_to_use: The 'jumbo + prime conforming' segment. Most resilient to rate shocks because these borrowers have alternatives (cash, equity). Useful for tracking high-end housing demand separately from broader market.

aUSMOVZERA.description: Households, Mortgage Origination Volume, Risk Score Zero
aUSMOVZERA.meaning: Mortgage originations with zero risk score — borrowers who lack credit-bureau histories (typically immigrants, young first-time buyers). Niche segment.
aUSMOVZERA.how_to_use: Very small share. Useful only for tracking unusual lending patterns. Major spike would indicate credit-extension to non-traditional borrowers (concerning) — currently flat.

aUSMOVTOTA.meaning: Total mortgage originations — sum of all credit-quality bands. NY Fed quarterly Household Debt and Credit Report. Includes both purchase and refinance originations.
aUSMOVTOTA.how_to_use: Headline mortgage finance volume. Collapsed from ~$1.2T quarterly peak in 2021 to ~$400B in 2023-24 as rate hikes killed refinance demand. Track purchase-origination share separately for housing-market signal.

aUSMEMSLA.meaning: Total student loans outstanding (memo to consumer credit) — ~$1.7T. Mostly federal direct loans; private student loans <$150B. Cumulative balance reflecting decades of borrowing minus repayments.
aUSMEMSLA.how_to_use: Major household balance sheet item. Repayment obligations resumed Oct 2023 after pandemic forbearance; consumption headwind for borrowers. Forgiveness programs (PSLF, IDR) periodically reduce balances; track flow vs stock for cleaner signal.

aUSCRDTLQ.meaning: Total consumer credit MoM% change, annualized — Fed G.19 high-frequency credit-growth signal. Captures revolving (cards) + nonrevolving (auto + student + personal) flows.
aUSCRDTLQ.how_to_use: Watch for sharp decelerations as consumer-stress signal. 2008 crisis saw -5% annualized; 2020 COVID saw -10% (credit-card payoffs from stimulus). Revolving accelerating + nonrevolving decelerating = households leaning on cards (late-cycle stress).

aUSCRDTLAB.meaning: Consumer credit, monthly absolute change — net credit creation flow. Fed G.19 release ~5th business day of each month, two-month lag.
aUSCRDTLAB.how_to_use: Decompose into revolving (cards) and nonrevolving (auto/student) for cleaner signal. Auto loan flows track auto sales; revolving flows show whether households are running balances or paying down. Stress shows up in revolving first.

aUSCRDEPNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at depository institutions — banks' auto loan + personal loan book (excludes mortgages, excludes credit cards). About half of all bank consumer lending by stock.
aUSCRDEPNA.how_to_use: Compare to total nonrevolving (G.19) for bank vs nonbank share. Auto loan share of bank lending has fallen as captive finance (GM Financial, Ford Credit, Toyota Financial) gained share — a structural shift in auto financing.

aUSCRDEPFA.meaning: Consumer credit at depository institutions, flows — net new bank consumer credit creation per period. Bank-channel credit-creation flow.
aUSCRDEPFA.how_to_use: Decompose vs nonbank flows (credit unions, finance companies) to see channel mix. Banks are ~50% of consumer credit; share has been falling as fintechs and captive auto finance grow.

aUSCRDNVFB/A.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, flows — auto + student + personal loan flows. Excludes credit cards (revolving).
aUSCRDNVFB/A.how_to_use: Auto loans dominate (~60% of nonrevolving flows). Student loans flat post-2020 forbearance/forgiveness. Track auto-loan flows for auto-sales pulse — they correlate ~0.8.

aUSCREDAB.description: Consumer credit - Actual, Absolute change, USD
aUSCREDAB.meaning: Consumer credit, absolute change in USD — total monthly net change in outstanding consumer credit. Same as aUSCRDTLAB at different release.
aUSCREDAB.how_to_use: Watch for sharp decelerations as consumer-stress signal. 2008 crisis saw monthly contractions of $20-30B; 2020 COVID saw similar drops driven by credit-card paydowns from stimulus.

aUSMEMMVA.description: Consumer credit memo, motor vehicle loans
aUSMEMMVA.how_to_use: ~$1.6T outstanding. Rate-sensitive; new vs used split matters for credit risk.

aUSFMEMMVA.description: Consumer credit memo, motor vehicle loans, flows
aUSFMEMMVA.meaning: Consumer credit memo: motor vehicle loans, flows — net new auto-loan creation per period. Tracks auto-finance volume.
aUSFMEMMVA.how_to_use: Correlates with auto sales (~0.8). Track auto-loan-flow growth vs sales growth: when loans grow faster than sales, average loan-to-value rising (subprime expansion); when slower, customers paying cash.

aUSCREDITI/A.meaning: Consumer credit outstanding (alternate framing) — same conceptual measure as aUSCRDOUTA. Total household nonmortgage debt.
aUSCREDITI/A.how_to_use: Cross-check vs aUSCRDOUTA. Total ~$5T as of 2024 (revolving ~$1.3T, nonrevolving ~$3.7T). Track YoY growth rate as consumer-leverage signal.

aUSCRDOUTA.meaning: Consumer Credit Outstanding total — Federal Reserve G.19 monthly. Credit cards + auto + student + personal. ~$5T total.
aUSCRDOUTA.how_to_use: Watch growth rate alongside delinquencies (aUSBDLCOCQ/A) to gauge consumer balance-sheet stress. Composition: revolving (cards) + non-revolving (auto, student, personal). Excludes mortgage debt.

aUSNCHCINB/A.meaning: Consumer credit outstanding, net change (annualized rate) — annualized version of monthly absolute change. Smoothed credit-creation pace.
aUSNCHCINB/A.how_to_use: Annualized rate makes monthly volatility comparable to year-over-year stock change. Useful for comparing fast-growing vs slow-growing periods. Pre-COVID norm ~5%/year; post-COVID swings have been much larger.

aUSTUCICA.how_to_use: Credit unions ~12% of consumer credit. Member-owned, often cheaper rates.

aUSTUCICFA.meaning: Consumer credit at credit unions, flows — net new credit-union consumer credit creation. Credit unions are ~12% of consumer credit market.
aUSTUCICFA.how_to_use: Credit unions tend to lend to higher-credit-quality borrowers and have lower charge-off rates. Growing share post-2008 (banks tightened, CUs filled gap). Track for member-base growth and lending standards.

aUSFCCICA.how_to_use: Captive finance arms (Ford Motor Credit, GM Financial). Auto-heavy.

aUSFCCICFA.meaning: Consumer credit, finance companies, flows — net new credit creation by finance companies (Ford Motor Credit, GM Financial, Toyota Financial, etc.).
aUSFCCICFA.how_to_use: Captive auto finance dominates this category. Flows correlate with auto sales but with higher beta because captives often offer subsidized financing to support sales.

aUSCRDTLFA.meaning: Total consumer credit flows — net new credit creation across all channels (banks, credit unions, finance companies, nonfinancial business, federal government).
aUSCRDTLFA.how_to_use: Aggregate flow measure. Decompose by channel for source of growth. Federal government student loans are a major share post-2010. Falling flows = consumer-credit cycle turning.

aUSBSCICA.meaning: Consumer credit, nonfinancial business — credit extended directly by retailers (store credit cards, layaway, etc.). Smaller channel.
aUSBSCICA.how_to_use: Niche category but cyclical. Retailer-direct credit grew during pandemic for buy-now-pay-later programs. Track for retailer-credit-program expansion.

aUSBSCICFA.meaning: Consumer credit, nonfinancial business, flows — net new credit creation by retailers/nonfinancial businesses.
aUSBSCICFA.how_to_use: Track for BNPL (buy-now-pay-later) ecosystem growth. Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay programs partially captured here. Volatile due to small base.

aUSCUCIFNA.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving credit unions, flows
aUSCUCIFNA.meaning: Consumer credit, nonrevolving at credit unions, flows — net new credit-union nonrevolving (auto + personal) lending.
aUSCUCIFNA.how_to_use: CUs growing share post-2008. Watch for member-base growth and lending standards. Auto lending is dominant within CU nonrevolving.

aUSCRDPFNA.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving depository institutions, flows
aUSCRDPFNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at depository institutions, flows — net new bank nonrevolving (auto + personal) lending.
aUSCRDPFNA.how_to_use: Bank-share gauge for nonrevolving lending. Bank share has fallen as captive finance grew (auto OEMs offer subsidized rates). Watch for share recovery if captives retreat.

aUSSMCIFNA.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving federal government & Sallie Mae, flows
aUSSMCIFNA.meaning: Federal government & Sallie Mae, nonrevolving credit, flows.
aUSSMCIFNA.how_to_use: Federal student loan flow. Large negative flows during pause years.

aUSFFCCFNA.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving finance companies, flows
aUSFFCCFNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, finance companies, flows — net new finance-company nonrevolving lending. Mostly auto captives.
aUSFFCCFNA.how_to_use: Auto-loan flow proxy. Highly sensitive to auto-sales pace. Captives use 0% promo financing to drive volume — watch promo-financing share for auto-incentive cycle.

aUSBSCIFNA.description: Consumer credit, nonrevolving nonfinancial business, flows
aUSBSCIFNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, nonfinancial business, flows — retailer-direct nonrevolving lending. Smaller niche.
aUSBSCIFNA.how_to_use: Track for installment-credit programs. BNPL ecosystem partially flows here. Volatile due to small base.

aUSCRCDACR.description: Consumer credit, terms of credit - comm bks interest, credit card, all account
aUSCRCDACR.meaning: Credit Card APR at commercial banks, all accounts (G.19 quarterly). ~22% in 2024 — record high.
aUSCRCDACR.how_to_use: Spread to fed funds widened sharply post-COVID (banks raised more than rate hikes warranted). Average APR for accounts ASSESSED interest (those carrying a balance) is even higher (~24%).

aUSCREDITIN/A.meaning: Non-revolving consumer credit — auto + student + personal loans. Larger than revolving; student loans dominate.
aUSCREDITIN/A.how_to_use: Auto charge-offs spiking (subprime auto stress). Student loans frozen during pandemic; payments resumed October 2023. PSLF/IDR program shifts move totals around.

aUSCREDITIR/A.meaning: Revolving consumer credit (credit cards). Hit ~$1.2T+ in 2024 — a record high.
aUSCREDITIR/A.how_to_use: Watch nominal growth rate (~8%/yr trend, faster recently). 90+ delinquency rate (aUSBDLCOCQ/A) is now elevated, especially subprime card. Card APR (aUSCRCDACR) at ~22% is record high.

aUSCRDTNQ.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, monthly percent change (annualized) — pace of nonrevolving (auto + student) credit growth.
aUSCRDTNQ.how_to_use: Smoother than revolving (cards). Auto-loan-driven cyclically; student-loan flows depend on policy (forgiveness, forbearance). Recent: weakened with auto-sales pullback.

aUSCRDTNAB.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, monthly absolute change — net new nonrevolving lending per month.
aUSCRDTNAB.how_to_use: Decompose vs revolving for cycle signal. Nonrevolving cycle lags consumer-spending cycle by 1-2 months (loans booked after purchase decisions).

aUSCICNRVA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit outstanding — total stock of nonrevolving credit (auto + student + personal). ~$3.7T.
aUSCICNRVA.how_to_use: Largest share of consumer credit (~75%). Student loans alone are ~$1.7T. Watch alongside revolving (cards) outstanding for total-leverage picture.

aUSCUCICNA.description: Nonrevolving consumer credit at credit unions
aUSCUCICNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at credit unions — CU nonrevolving lending stock. ~$400B.
aUSCUCICNA.how_to_use: Auto-loan-heavy. CUs gaining share post-2008. Track for member-base growth and average loan size.

aUSFCCICNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit at finance companies — captive auto finance + personal-loan finance companies. ~$700B.
aUSFCCICNA.how_to_use: Auto OEM captives dominate. Watch for share trends vs banks; captives gain share when promotional financing aggressive.

aUSCICNFNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, total flows — aggregate of all-channel nonrevolving lending creation.
aUSCICNFNA.how_to_use: Sum of bank + CU + finance company + nonfin business + federal government nonrevolving flows. Federal government (student loans) is variable based on policy.

aUSBSCICOA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, nonfinancial business — retailer-direct installment credit stock.
aUSBSCICOA.how_to_use: Niche category. Includes retailer financing programs and BNPL providers. Track for ecosystem growth.

aUSFICICNA.description: Nonrevolving consumer credit, pool of securitized assets
aUSFICICNA.meaning: Nonrevolving consumer credit, pool of securitized assets — auto-loan ABS and other consumer-credit-backed securities.
aUSFICICNA.how_to_use: Tracks securitized funding of consumer credit. ABS issuance is the supply side; investor demand drives pricing of subprime auto deals. Watch for ABS-spread changes as credit-cycle indicator.

aUSFORIDB/A.how_to_use: Broader than DSR — includes rent, auto leases, property tax, insurance. Better gauge for renters.

aUSDSPIDB/A.meaning: Household debt service ratio (DSR) — debt payments / disposable income.
aUSDSPIDB/A.how_to_use: Master household-leverage gauge. ~10% currently — well below 2008 peak (~13%).

aUSPCEMAR.description: Core PCE price index- Actual, Chg P/P
aUSPCEMAR.meaning: Core PCE price index, month-over-month change — the Fed's PREFERRED inflation gauge against which the 2% target is officially measured. Released with BEA Personal Income & Outlays, ~2 weeks after CPI.
aUSPCEMAR.how_to_use: Annualize the 6-month rate when reading FOMC commentary. ~0.17%/mo (~2% annualized) is target-consistent; sustained 0.3%+ prints are hawkish. Differs from core CPI in basket (less shelter weight, more healthcare) and chain-weighting.

aUSCPIWFA.how_to_use: Sub-component or variant within Consumer Prices / Inflation. No standard practitioner usage notes have been written for this specific RIC — consult the upstream source publication (BEA, BLS, Federal Reserve, Census, USDA, EIA, or the relevant industry survey) for the formal definition before using it.

aUSCPTANIFR.description: CPI - All Urban Sample: All Items - Annual Inflation Rate
aUSCPTANIFR.meaning: Year-over-year change in headline CPI — the most-watched US consumer-price inflation gauge.
aUSCPTANIFR.how_to_use: Most-watched US inflation gauge. Compare against the Fed 2% target and consensus (surprises move short-end rates). Decompose by component (shelter, energy, food, services). For Fed policy reads, prefer Core PCE — the Fed's actual target.

aUSCPI/A.meaning: Level of the Consumer Price Index — the BLS monthly measure of average prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.

aUSCPI.meaning: Headline Consumer Price Index — level. The BLS basket-weighted average price for urban consumers across food, energy, shelter, transportation, medical care, and services. Released ~mid-month, lagged one month.
aUSCPI.how_to_use: Use the YoY change (aUSCPIYYR) for inflation reads; use the level for cross-series comparisons or splicing onto historical data. The index level itself is rarely market-moving — the YoY change is. Headline includes volatile food + energy; pair with core (aUSCPIXFE/A) to filter noise.

aUSCPIXFE/A.description: CPI, All items less food and energy
aUSCPIXFE/A.meaning: Core CPI level — All items excluding food and energy. Strips out the two most volatile components, giving the cleanest read on underlying inflation pressure.
aUSCPIXFE/A.how_to_use: Watch the YoY (aUSCPFYAR) for trend. Within core: shelter is ~40% of the index and the stickiest component; if shelter inflation slows, core decelerates with a lag. Used by analysts to call the Fed reaction function alongside core PCE.

aUSCPIXFE.description: CPI, All items less food and energy
aUSCPIXFE.meaning: Level of the Core CPI (consumer prices excluding food and energy) — the BLS measure of underlying inflation, stripped of the two most volatile components.
aUSCPIXFE.how_to_use: Cleaner inflation signal than headline CPI (strips out volatile food + energy). When core stays sticky while headline falls, inflation is broadening into services/shelter — harder to dislodge. The Fed monitors core CPI but officially targets core PCE; gaps between the two reflect basket weights (shelter is heavier in CPI).

aUSCWXFF/C.description: CPI, All items less food, U.S. city average
aUSCWXFF/C.meaning: Level of the Consumer Price Index — the BLS monthly measure of average prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.
aUSCWXFF/C.how_to_use: Most-watched US inflation gauge. Compare against the Fed 2% target and consensus (surprises move short-end rates). Decompose by component (shelter, energy, food, services). For Fed policy reads, prefer Core PCE — the Fed's actual target.

aUSCPIW.description: Consumer price index, CPI, All items
aUSCPIW.meaning: Index of the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
aUSCPIW.how_to_use: Most-watched US inflation gauge. Compare against the Fed 2% target and consensus (surprises move short-end rates). Decompose by component (shelter, energy, food, services). For Fed policy reads, prefer Core PCE — the Fed's actual target.

aUSCPFAR.meaning: Month-over-month change in Core CPI — short-term underlying-inflation pulse.
aUSCPFAR.how_to_use: Cleaner inflation signal than headline CPI (strips out volatile food + energy). When core stays sticky while headline falls, inflation is broadening into services/shelter — harder to dislodge. The Fed monitors core CPI but officially targets core PCE; gaps between the two reflect basket weights (shelter is heavier in CPI).

aUSCPFYAR.meaning: Year-over-year change in Core CPI. Most-watched non-Fed-target inflation gauge: market reads first, Fed officials cross-reference with core PCE.
aUSCPFYAR.how_to_use: Compare against Fed's 2% PCE target (CPI typically runs 30-50bp above PCE). >3% YoY is hot; <2.5% suggests Fed can ease. Decompose by shelter vs core services ex-shelter ('supercore') vs core goods to read the next move.

aUSPPTYAF.description: PPI ex Food/Energy/Tr YY, Chg Y/Y
aUSPPTYAF.meaning: Year-over-year change in PPI — early signal of pipeline inflation pressures.
aUSPPTYAF.how_to_use: Leads CPI for goods inflation. Watch core PPI (ex food/energy/trade) for the cleanest underlying signal. Final-demand services PPI is the input to core PCE.

aUSPPETA.description: PPI ex Food/Energy/Trade MM, Chg P/P
aUSPPETA.how_to_use: Leads CPI for goods inflation. Watch core PPI (ex food/energy/trade) for the cleanest underlying signal. Final-demand services PPI is the input to core PCE.

aUSPFGAR.description: Producer Prices, Final demand less foods and energy, Chg P/P
aUSPFGAR.meaning: Month-over-month change in PPI Final Demand — short-term producer-price pulse.
aUSPFGAR.how_to_use: Leads CPI by 1-3 months for goods inflation. Final-demand services PPI feeds directly into core PCE via the BEA's mapping. PPI spikes without CPI follow-through implies margin compression on producers.

aUSPFDGAR.description: Producer Prices, Final demand less foods and energy, Chg Y/Y
aUSPFDGAR.meaning: Core PPI YoY — Producer Prices Final Demand less foods and energy. The producer-side equivalent of core CPI.
aUSPFDGAR.how_to_use: Cleaner pipeline-inflation signal than headline PPI. Tracks Core PCE goods inflation closely. Watch alongside USD trade-weighted: stronger USD lowers imported intermediate input costs.

No standard practitioner usage notes have been written for this specific RIC — consult the upstream source publication (BEA, BLS, Federal Reserve, Census, USDA, EIA, or the relevant industry survey) for the formal definition before using it.

aUSPPIAAR.meaning: Level of the Consumer Price Index — the BLS monthly measure of average prices paid by urban consumers for a fixed basket of goods and services.

aUSCCIPSOR.description: LSEG / Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index (PCSI)
aUSCCIPSOR.how_to_use: Alternative consumer sentiment gauge. Less market-watched than UMich/CB.

aUSOCS005Q/A.meaning: Composite Consumer Confidence Indicator (OECD-standardized) — averages multiple confidence gauges into one international-comparison number.
aUSOCS005Q/A.how_to_use: Use for cross-country comparisons. US-domestic analysts use UMich (aUSCSIUM) and Conference Board (aUSCONCF/A) directly. OECD composite smooths divergences between national surveys.

aUSHAI.meaning: National Housing Affordability Index — composite. NAR.
aUSHAI.how_to_use: 100 = median family can afford median home. Below 100 = affordability stress. Hit ~95 in 2023 — record low.

aUSHOIMED.description: National, Housing Affordability Index, median family income
aUSHOIMED.meaning: National Housing Affordability Index — median family income input. The denominator that scales the affordability calculation.
aUSHOIMED.how_to_use: Used to compute aUSHAI (affordability index = 100 means median family can afford median home). Tracks median family income trend; rises with NFP wages and demographic shifts.

aUSMSNPAH.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, Reuters
aUSMSNPAH.meaning: Mislabeled volume index — Reuters consumer surveys.

aUSMSNEAH.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, Reuters
aUSMSNEAH.meaning: Mislabeled volume index — Reuters consumer surveys.

aUSMSNAH.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, Reuters
aUSMSNAH.meaning: Mislabeled volume index — Reuters consumer surveys.

aUSIPSOAR.description: Reuters poll: TR US IPSOS - Actual
aUSIPSOAR.meaning: Reuters/Ipsos US Consumer Index — alternative consumer-mood gauge. Smaller-sample monthly survey by Ipsos.
aUSIPSOAR.how_to_use: Tertiary cross-check vs UMich and Conference Board. Less market-moving on release. Useful when major confidence gauges diverge — provides third opinion.

aUSIBDECOP.meaning: RCM/TIPP Economic Optimism Index — monthly investor and consumer optimism gauge published by Investor's Business Daily and TechnoMetrica. Combines six-month outlook, personal financial outlook, and confidence in federal economic policies.
aUSIBDECOP.how_to_use: Smaller-sample alternative to UMich and Conference Board surveys. Use as a tertiary cross-check — when all three confidence gauges move in the same direction, the signal is robust; divergences are usually noise.

aUSBCIACEBC.description: Average consumer expectations, business & economic conditions
aUSBCIACEBC.meaning: Conference Board: average consumer expectations for business and economic conditions — composite expectations gauge from CB survey.
aUSBCIACEBC.how_to_use: Captures the forward-looking aggregate of CB consumer survey. More predictive than CB Present Situation. Pair with CB Expectations sub-index for full forward-look picture.

aUSCONCF/A.meaning: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index — survey of ~3,000 US households on present situation and future expectations. Released last Tuesday of each month.
aUSCONCF/A.how_to_use: Pair with UMich sentiment — they sometimes diverge (CB more labor-market sensitive, UMich more inflation/wealth sensitive). The Expectations sub-index leads recessions: a >20pt YoY drop is a historical warning. Less market-moving on release than NFP/CPI.

aUSCONCE/A.meaning: Conference Board Consumer Confidence — Expectations sub-index. The forward-looking component, sub-80 typically signals recession.
aUSCONCE/A.how_to_use: More predictive than the headline. >20pt YoY drop is recession-warning. Historically the cleaner of the two CB sub-indices for cycle calls.

aUSCONCFP/A.description: Conference Board, Consumer confidence, present situation
aUSCONCFP/A.meaning: Conference Board Consumer Confidence — Present Situation sub-index. Current-conditions assessment.
aUSCONCFP/A.how_to_use: Lags Expectations in turning points. Stays elevated longer at cycle peaks. Use the spread (Present − Expectations) as a recession-risk signal: when Present is high but Expectations falling fast, the cycle is rolling over.

aUSFBUSCB/A.description: Conference Board, Future business conditions, better
aUSFBUSCB/A.meaning: Conference Board: future business conditions, % of respondents saying 'better'. Bullish-expectations percentage.
aUSFBUSCB/A.how_to_use: Forward-looking optimism share. Pair with 'worse' (aUSFBUSCW/A) for the diffusion (better − worse) used in net-confidence calculations. Falling 'better' share is recession-leading.

aUSFBUSCS/A.description: Conference Board, Future business conditions, same
aUSFBUSCS/A.meaning: Conference Board: future business conditions, % saying 'same'. Neutral/ambivalent percentage.
aUSFBUSCS/A.how_to_use: Track for indecision share — typically the largest bucket. Stable at ~50-60% in normal times. Spikes during turning-point ambiguity.

aUSFBUSCW/A.description: Conference Board, Future business conditions, worse
aUSFBUSCW/A.how_to_use: Bearish-expectations percentage. Sustained rises signal recession risk.

aUSFUEMPFJ/A.description: Conference Board, Future employment, fewer jobs
aUSFUEMPFJ/A.meaning: Conference Board: future employment, % expecting fewer jobs. Bearish labor-outlook percentage.
aUSFUEMPFJ/A.how_to_use: Rises sharply ahead of recessions — one of CB's most reliable recession-leading sub-indices. Sustained >25% has preceded every recession since the survey began.

aUSFUEMPMJ/A.description: Conference Board, Future employment, more jobs
aUSFUEMPMJ/A.meaning: Conference Board: future employment, % expecting more jobs. Bullish labor-outlook percentage.
aUSFUEMPMJ/A.how_to_use: Falling 'more jobs' share is recession-leading. Compute (more − fewer) for the labor-expectations diffusion — historically a reliable cycle signal.

aUSCONEMS/A.meaning: Conference Board: future employment, % expecting same number of jobs. Stability/uncertainty percentage.
aUSCONEMS/A.how_to_use: Largest bucket typically. Useful for tracking expectations volatility — when this share falls, respondents are taking strong views (bullish or bearish).

aUSFUIDECR/A.meaning: Conference Board: future income, % expecting decrease. Pessimistic income-outlook share.
aUSFUIDECR/A.how_to_use: Income-expectations are the cleanest predictor of consumption. Rising 'decrease' share precedes consumption slowdowns. Track alongside real wage growth (aUSEARNW/CA).

aUSCONFUIR/A.meaning: Conference Board: future income, % expecting increase. Optimistic income-outlook share.
aUSCONFUIR/A.how_to_use: Falling income-optimism share is consumption-leading. The (increase − decrease) diffusion is the meaningful signal for forward consumption.

aUSCONFUIS/A.meaning: Conference Board: future income, % expecting same. Stability share — neutral income outlook.
aUSCONFUIS/A.how_to_use: Largest bucket typically. Useful for tracking respondent confidence in projections.

aUSCBCLM.description: Conference Board, Plans to buy car within six months, yes
aUSCBCLM.meaning: Conference Board: plans to buy car within 6 months. Forward-looking auto-demand indicator from household survey.
aUSCBCLM.how_to_use: Leads auto sales by 1-3 months. Sustained drops below 4% historically signal slowing auto demand. Pair with aUSMAPPL6 (appliances) for big-ticket-durables outlook.

aUSMAPPL6.description: Conference Board, Plans to buy major appliances within six months
aUSMAPPL6.meaning: Conference Board: plans to buy major appliances within 6 months. Forward-looking durable-goods demand indicator.
aUSMAPPL6.how_to_use: Big-ticket appliance demand follows housing-purchase activity. Falls when housing slows. Useful as a cross-check for retail sales of furniture/appliances (aUSRSLSHF/A).

aUSPBCBAD/A.description: Conference Board, Present business conditions, bad
aUSPBCBAD/A.meaning: Conference Board: present business conditions, % saying 'bad'. Pessimistic share for current-state assessment.
aUSPBCBAD/A.how_to_use: Tracks present-conditions worry. Stays low in expansions; rises sharply at recession onset. (Good − bad) diffusion is the headline 'present situation' input.

aUSPBCGUD/A.description: Conference Board, Present business conditions, good
aUSPBCGUD/A.meaning: Conference Board: present business conditions, % saying 'good'. Optimistic share for current state.
aUSPBCGUD/A.how_to_use: Stays elevated in expansions, drops sharply at recession onset. The (good − bad) diffusion is the CB Present Situation input. Falling 'good' share with rising 'bad' is a turning-point signal.

aUSPBCNOR/A.description: Conference Board, Present business conditions, normal
aUSPBCNOR/A.meaning: Conference Board: present business conditions, % saying 'normal'. Neutral share — middle of the distribution.
aUSPBCNOR/A.how_to_use: Largest bucket. Tracks 'how typical' respondents see conditions. Movements between 'normal' and 'good'/'bad' show inflection-point dynamics.

aUSPEMPHG/A.description: Conference Board, Present employment, jobs hard to get
aUSPEMPHG/A.meaning: CB present employment, % saying jobs hard to get.
aUSPEMPHG/A.how_to_use: Cleanest household-survey labor read. Rising = labor market loosening.

aUSPEMPNSP/A.description: Conference Board, Present employment, jobs not so plentiful
aUSPEMPNSP/A.meaning: Conference Board: present employment, % saying 'jobs not so plentiful'. Middle-position labor-market view.
aUSPEMPNSP/A.how_to_use: Tracks ambiguity in labor-market perception. Pair with 'jobs plentiful' and 'jobs hard to get' for full Conference Board labor differential calculation.

aUSPEMPJOP/A.description: Conference Board, Present employment, jobs plentiful
aUSPEMPJOP/A.meaning: Conference Board: present employment, % saying 'jobs plentiful'. Bullish labor-market view.
aUSPEMPJOP/A.how_to_use: Used in 'labor-market differential' calculation: (jobs plentiful − jobs hard to get). One of the most predictive labor-market indicators — leads the unemployment rate by 1-2 months.

aUSCONCAQ/C.meaning: Consumer confidence (standardized) — OECD-comparable consumer confidence framing. Aggregates multiple US confidence series.
aUSCONCAQ/C.how_to_use: Use for cross-country comparisons. Domestic analysts use UMich/Conference Board directly. The standardization aligns with OECD methodology.

aUSUMERAPH.how_to_use: UMich forward-looking sub-index. Most market-relevant of UMich subseries.

aUSUMSRAPH.how_to_use: UMich headline sentiment. More inflation-sensitive than Conference Board.

aUSUMCRAPH.meaning: UMich Current Economic Conditions Index — present-state component of UMich monthly sentiment survey. Reflects current finances and buying-conditions assessments.
aUSUMCRAPH.how_to_use: Pair with UMich Expectations (aUSCONCFEX) for the headline sentiment. Current Conditions tends to lag Expectations at turning points; the gap (Conditions − Expectations) is a useful cycle indicator.

aUSUMCPAPH.meaning: UMich Current Economic Conditions — preliminary release (mid-month). Final release follows 2 weeks later.
aUSUMCPAPH.how_to_use: Markets trade the preliminary release. ~80% of months see no revision; large revisions (>3 points) signal late-month news (gas-price moves, geopolitical events).

aUSUM1PAPR.description: Total-prelim, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers

aUSUMEPAPH.description: Total-prelim, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers

aUSUMSPAPH.description: Total-prelim, Volume Index, Consumer Surveys, Monthly, University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers

aUSUM1FRA.how_to_use: Most-watched short-term inflation gauge. Fed monitors closely.

aUSUM5FRA.description: U Mich 5-Yr Inf Final, Chg Y/Y
aUSUM5FRA.how_to_use: Long-term anchor. Sub-3% = anchored; spikes signal Fed credibility risk.

aUSUM5PRA.description: U Mich 5-Yr Inf Prelim, Chg Y/Y
aUSUM5PRA.meaning: UMich 5-10 year median inflation expectations, preliminary release. Same conceptual measure as aUSINFEXM5Y at preliminary frequency.
aUSUM5PRA.how_to_use: Markets watch the preliminary release for any change in long-term anchored expectations. Sustained moves above 3.5% in this preliminary print historically draw Fed attention; revisions in the final release can move markets if direction reverses.

aUSINFEXM1Y.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, 1 Year Inflation Expectations (median)
aUSINFEXM1Y.meaning: University of Michigan 1-year-ahead median inflation expectation — household survey response to 'how much do you expect prices to go up over the next 12 months?' One of the Fed's most-watched short-horizon expectations measures.
aUSINFEXM1Y.how_to_use: Spikes when gasoline prices move (households over-weight what they see at the pump). The Fed cares about whether expectations stay 'anchored' — sustained moves above 4-5% raise concerns about a wage-price spiral. Cross-check against TIPS breakevens and NY Fed SCE.

aUSINFEXM5Y.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, 5 Year Inflation Expectations (median)
aUSINFEXM5Y.meaning: University of Michigan 5-10 year median inflation expectation — household long-horizon expectation. The Fed's primary anchored-expectations gauge from the household side.
aUSINFEXM5Y.how_to_use: More stable than the 1Y series — typically pinned in a 2.5-3.5% band. Sustained moves above 3.5% are taken seriously by the FOMC; Powell has cited this series specifically in press conferences. Compare to 5Y5Y forward TIPS breakevens for a market-vs-survey read.

aUSCONCFEX.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, Consumer Expectations Index
aUSCONCFEX.meaning: UMich Consumer Expectations sub-index — forward-looking component of UMich sentiment.
aUSCONCFEX.how_to_use: Pair with Conf Board Expectations (aUSCONCE/A). When both are falling together, recession risk is meaningful. UMich expectations weighed heavily by inflation; CB expectations weighed by labor market.

aUSCSIUM.description: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, University of Michigan, Consumer Sentiment Index
aUSCSIUM.meaning: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index — headline. More inflation-sensitive than Conference Board. Twice-monthly release: preliminary mid-month, final end of month.
aUSCSIUM.how_to_use: The 1Y and 5-10Y inflation expectations sub-questions are Fed-monitored. UMich sentiment correlated with retail spending leads by 1-2 months. UMich + Conf Board divergences usually resolve toward UMich within 2-3 months.

aUSPCEYAR.description: PCE Price Index- Actual, Chg Y/Y
aUSPCEYAR.meaning: Headline PCE price index, year-over-year change. Released with the BEA Personal Income & Outlays report, ~2 weeks after CPI. Uses chain-weighting and a broader basket than CPI.
aUSPCEYAR.how_to_use: Cross-check against headline CPI. Diverges from CPI primarily because of (a) lower shelter weight, (b) inclusion of employer-paid health insurance, (c) chain-weighting. Persistent CPI > PCE gap is normal — typically 30-50 bps.

aUSNC0BJN/C.description: PCE price index, other goods & services
aUSNC0BJN/C.meaning: Index of the headline PCE price index.
aUSNC0BJN/C.how_to_use: Cross-check against headline CPI. PCE differs in basket composition (broader, captures substitution behavior) and weighting (chain-weighted, services-heavier). CPI > PCE divergence is normal — usually 30-50bp wider in CPI.

aUSNXN2QZ/C.meaning: Year-over-year change in the headline PCE price index — released alongside personal income and consumption.
aUSNXN2QZ/C.how_to_use: Cross-check against headline CPI. PCE differs in basket composition (broader, captures substitution behavior) and weighting (chain-weighted, services-heavier). CPI > PCE divergence is normal — usually 30-50bp wider in CPI.

aUSNZXA49.meaning: Level of the headline PCE price index (Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, all items).
aUSNZXA49.how_to_use: Cross-check against headline CPI. PCE differs in basket composition (broader, captures substitution behavior) and weighting (chain-weighted, services-heavier). CPI > PCE divergence is normal — usually 30-50bp wider in CPI.

aUSGPC/CA.description: Personal Consumption Expenditure, Constant Prices, Consumption, Monthly, BEA - Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. Department of Commerce
aUSGPC/CA.meaning: Real Personal Consumption Expenditures level (chained dollars). The largest component of GDP at ~70%, the dominant cyclical driver of US economic activity.
aUSGPC/CA.how_to_use: Watch the MoM growth in real terms (aUSGPCSAR) — that directly feeds GDP. Decompose by durables/non-durables/services: durables most cyclical, services most stable. Real PCE deceleration is the leading edge of recession risk.

aUSCONSRVD/CA.how_to_use: Cross-check against headline CPI. PCE differs in basket composition (broader, captures substitution behavior) and weighting (chain-weighted, services-heavier). CPI > PCE divergence is normal — usually 30-50bp wider in CPI.

aUSMPATX.meaning: Manufacturing corporations after-tax profits — Census Quarterly Financial Report (QFR). Covers all manufacturing.
aUSMPATX.how_to_use: Pair with industrial production and ISM Manufacturing for the full mfg cycle picture. Profit margins (profits/sales) here lead capex decisions. Look at YoY change rather than level.

aUSMPDMF.description: Manufacturing corporations, after-tax profits, all durable manufacturing
aUSMPDMF.meaning: After-tax profits for durable-goods manufacturing (autos, machinery, electronics, fab metals). QFR.
aUSMPDMF.how_to_use: Durables are the cyclical heart of mfg — leads the broader cycle. Pair with new orders for durable goods to gauge order-book to bottom-line transmission.

aUSMPNDMF.description: Manufacturing corporations, after-tax profits, all nondurable manufacturing
aUSMPNDMF.meaning: After-tax profits for nondurable-goods manufacturing (food, chemicals, petroleum, textiles, paper). QFR.
aUSMPNDMF.how_to_use: Less cyclical than durables; more sensitive to commodity input costs. Petroleum sub-component swings the headline — strip it out for trend.

aUSRPROFITA.description: Retail trade corporations, income (or loss) after income taxes
aUSRPROFITA.meaning: Retail trade corporations, after-tax income or loss. QFR.
aUSRPROFITA.how_to_use: Cross-check with retail sales: persistent retail sales growth without profit growth implies margin compression (most likely from labor/rent). Useful for sector valuation context.

aUSRTOPIN.description: Retail trade corporations, income (or loss) from operations
aUSRTOPIN.meaning: Retail trade corporations, income or loss from operations (pre-tax operating income).
aUSRTOPIN.how_to_use: Pre-tax operating proxy for the retail sector — strips out tax effects and one-offs. Use the after-tax line for valuation, this for operational health.

aUSRTSRNOPR.description: Retail trade corporations, net sales, receipts and operating revenues
aUSRTSRNOPR.meaning: Retail trade corporations, net sales, receipts and operating revenues. The top line of QFR retail.
aUSRTSRNOPR.how_to_use: Differs from BLS retail sales: QFR is corporation-level (excludes sole proprietors), quarterly, more volatile. Use BLS retail sales for the headline; this for sector earnings context.

aUSBNQB11P.how_to_use: Reorganization filings. Big-cap Ch.11 cases (large notional debt) more market-relevant than counts.

aUSBNQ11P.meaning: Total Chapter 11 bankruptcy filings — corporate reorganizations under federal bankruptcy code. Companies filing here aim to restructure debt while continuing operations (vs Ch 7 liquidation).
aUSBNQ11P.how_to_use: Cyclical late-cycle stress signal — peaks 6-12 months after recession start. Major filings (Hertz 2020, JCPenney 2020, SVB 2023) drive headline numbers but small-business filings give cleaner cycle signal. Pre-2008 norm ~3,000/quarter; post-2010 ~2,000/quarter.

aUSBFILB.description: Bankruptcy filings (12 months ending), business, total
aUSBFILB.meaning: Total business bankruptcy filings, rolling 12-month — Chapter 7 (liquidation) + Chapter 11 (reorg) + Chapter 13 + Chapter 12 (farm). Smoother than quarterly; better for cycle reads.
aUSBFILB.how_to_use: 12-month rolling smooths volatility. Track YoY change for cycle signal: rising YoY indicates corporate stress accumulating. SBA-loan defaults flow into this stat with 6-9 month lag.

aUSBFILNB.description: Bankruptcy filings (12 months ending), non-business, total
aUSBFILNB.meaning: Total non-business (consumer/personal) bankruptcy filings, rolling 12-month — Chapter 7 + Chapter 13 personal filings. Larger volume than business filings (~400-500K/year vs ~25K/year).
aUSBFILNB.how_to_use: Consumer-stress gauge. Spiked 2003-05 (record 2M filings before reform), fell post-2005 BAPCPA reform, low post-2010. Watch alongside credit-card delinquencies — bankruptcies lag delinquencies by 6-12 months.

aUSBCLAGQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, agricultural loans
aUSBCLAGQ/A.meaning: Charge-off rate, all banks, agricultural loans — share of ag loans deemed uncollectible. Quarterly FDIC release. Small loan book (~$80B) but cyclically sensitive to commodity prices.
aUSBCLAGQ/A.how_to_use: Track for ag-cycle stress. Spikes when crop prices fall sharply (1986 farm crisis, 2015-16 commodity downturn). Currently low. Combined with ag-real-estate values, signals farm-sector financial health.

aUSBCLCAIQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, commercial and industrial loans
aUSBCLCAIQ/A.how_to_use: Business credit-loss gauge. Rises ~6-12 months after recession start.

aUSBCLCOQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, consumer loans, all
aUSBCLCOQ/A.meaning: Bank charge-off rate, total consumer loans.
aUSBCLCOQ/A.how_to_use: Consumer credit losses — leading sign of household stress.

aUSBCLCOCQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, consumer loans, credit cards
aUSBCLCOCQ/A.meaning: Bank Charge-off Rate, credit cards. Most pro-cyclical loan category.
aUSBCLCOCQ/A.how_to_use: Crossing 4% historically signals recession-like consumer stress. Currently elevated, especially subprime. Card delinquencies (aUSBDLCOCQ/A) lead charge-offs by 3-6 months.

aUSBCLCOOQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, consumer loans, other
aUSBCLCOOQ/A.meaning: Charge-off rate, all banks, consumer loans (other) — auto loans + personal loans + other non-card consumer credit. Excludes credit cards (separate series) and mortgages.
aUSBCLCOOQ/A.how_to_use: Auto-loan-driven mostly. Subprime auto charge-offs are the leading edge — rising ahead of broader consumer stress. Track alongside auto-loan-90+-day delinquencies (NY Fed) for triangulated read.

aUSBCLEASQ/A.meaning: Charge-off rate, all banks, leases — equipment leasing exposures. Smaller portfolio than C&I loans (~$120B at large banks).
aUSBCLEASQ/A.how_to_use: Cyclical with capex cycles. Equipment leases (cars, trucks, machinery) charge off in slowdowns when small businesses fail. Watch alongside C&I charge-offs for full business-credit quality picture.

aUSBCLREQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, real estate loans, all
aUSBCLREQ/A.how_to_use: Combined residential + CRE charge-offs. CRE-led elevation now.

aUSBCLRECQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, real estate loans, commercial
aUSBCLRECQ/A.meaning: Bank Charge-off Rate, CRE (commercial real estate). Heavy office/retail CRE losses post-COVID.
aUSBCLRECQ/A.how_to_use: Bank stress concentrated here for regional banks (large banks have less CRE exposure). Office is the worst sub-sector; multifamily improving; industrial healthy. Watch alongside CMBS spreads.

aUSBCLRERQ/A.description: Charge-Off Rates, all banks, real estate loans, residential
aUSBCLRERQ/A.meaning: Bank charge-off rate, residential real estate.
aUSBCLRERQ/A.how_to_use: Mortgage charge-offs — historically low (mortgage credit standards strict post-2008).

aUSBCLALQ/A.description: Charge-Off rates, all banks, total loans and leases
aUSBCLALQ/A.meaning: Total Bank Charge-off Rate, all loans and leases. Aggregate bank-credit-loss gauge from FDIC quarterly.
aUSBCLALQ/A.how_to_use: Counter-cyclical: rises ~6-12 months after recession start. Currently elevated but well below 2008 levels. Card + CRE driving recent increase; mortgage charge-offs remain very low (mortgage credit standards strict post-GFC).

aUSBDLRECQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, Real estate loans, commercial
aUSBDLRECQ/A.meaning: CRE 30-day delinquency rate. Office sector driving elevation post-2022.
aUSBDLRECQ/A.how_to_use: Watch alongside CMBS spreads + special-servicing transfers. CRE loan defaults are slow-moving (loans don't reset until refinancing); the wave of 2024-26 maturities is the test.

aUSBDLAGQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, agricultural loans
aUSBDLAGQ/A.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, agricultural loans — share of ag loans 30+ days past due. Leading indicator for charge-offs (charge-offs follow delinquencies by 6-12 months).
aUSBDLAGQ/A.how_to_use: Watch for ag-cycle stress. Sustained rise above 2% historically signals farm-credit downturn. Crop prices (corn, soybean, wheat) drive farmer cash flow — track alongside USDA crop forecasts.

aUSBDLCAIQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, commercial and industrial loans
aUSBDLCAIQ/A.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, commercial and industrial loans — share of C&I loans 30+ days past due. Leading indicator of corporate-credit cycle.
aUSBDLCAIQ/A.how_to_use: Pre-recession warning: rising delinquencies precede rising charge-offs by 6-12 months. Currently elevated but below 2008 peak. SLOOS lending standards typically lead delinquencies by 1-2 quarters.

aUSBDLCOQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, consumer loans, all
aUSBDLCOQ/A.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, consumer loans (all) — share of consumer loans 30+ days past due. Comprehensive consumer-credit-stress gauge.
aUSBDLCOQ/A.how_to_use: Pre-2008 norm ~3-3.5%; 2008-09 peaked ~5%; post-recovery ~2%. Currently rising from 2022 lows as student-loan resumption + auto-loan stress feed through. Watch alongside subcategory delinquency rates for stress source.

aUSBDLCOCQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, consumer loans, credit cards
aUSBDLCOCQ/A.meaning: Credit card 30-day delinquency rate. Most pro-cyclical loan category.
aUSBDLCOCQ/A.how_to_use: Crossing 3% historically signals recession risk; now ~3.2% in 2024. Subprime card delinquencies are running much higher (~7%+). Watch alongside disposable income growth — delinquencies rise when real DPI growth turns negative.

aUSBDLCOOQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, consumer loans, other
aUSBDLCOOQ/A.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, consumer loans (other) — auto + personal loans + other non-card consumer credit. Excludes credit cards (separate series) and mortgages.
aUSBDLCOOQ/A.how_to_use: Auto-loan-driven mostly. Subprime auto delinquencies are the leading edge — rising ahead of broader consumer stress. Track alongside aUSBCLCOOQ/A (charge-offs) for the full credit-cycle.

aUSBDLEASQ/A.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, leases — equipment lease delinquencies. Smaller portfolio than C&I loans (~$120B at large banks).
aUSBDLEASQ/A.how_to_use: Cyclical with capex cycles. Equipment leases (cars, trucks, machinery) become delinquent in slowdowns when small businesses fail. Watch alongside C&I delinquencies for full business-credit-quality picture.

aUSBDLREQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, real estate loans, all
aUSBDLREQ/A.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, real estate loans (all) — combines residential mortgages + CRE delinquencies.
aUSBDLREQ/A.how_to_use: Aggregate housing-finance stress gauge. CRE-driven recently (office sector); residential delinquencies very low post-Dodd-Frank QM rules. Decompose into residential vs CRE for clean signal.

aUSBDLRERQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, real estate loans, residential
aUSBDLRERQ/A.meaning: Delinquency rate, all banks, residential real estate loans — single-family + multifamily mortgage delinquencies. Pure residential housing-credit gauge.
aUSBDLRERQ/A.how_to_use: Very low post-2010 due to QM rules + locked-in low fixed rates. 2008 peak was ~12%; now ~1.5%. Most US homeowners locked in 3-4% mortgages 2020-21 — virtually no delinquency stress despite rate hikes.

aUSBDLALQ/A.description: Delinquency rates, all banks, total loans and leases
aUSBDLALQ/A.meaning: Total Bank Loan Delinquency Rate. Earlier-stage stress signal than charge-offs.
aUSBDLALQ/A.how_to_use: Watch alongside SLOOS lending standards. Delinquencies rising while standards tightening = rough cycle (banks defensive but borrowers still struggling).

aUSMGFSHQ/A.meaning: All loans, foreclosures started — share of mortgages entering foreclosure during the period. MBA quarterly National Delinquency Survey.
aUSMGFSHQ/A.how_to_use: Most-direct mortgage-stress gauge. Pre-2008 ~0.5%; peaked ~1.5% in 2009; post-recovery ~0.2%. Currently very low. Track alongside FHA/VA-specific foreclosure rates (higher stress) for credit-tier breakdown.

aUSMGDHQ/A.meaning: All loans, total past due — share of mortgages 30+ days delinquent. Aggregate mortgage-credit-quality gauge from MBA.
aUSMGDHQ/A.how_to_use: Sum of 30/60/90+-day delinquencies. Cyclical: rises in recessions, falls in expansions. Currently low (~3.5%) reflecting structural low-rate-locked-in protection. 2008 peak was ~10%.

aUSMGFIHR.description: All loans in foreclosure at end of quarter
aUSMGFIHR.meaning: All loans in foreclosure at end of quarter.
aUSMGFIHR.how_to_use: Stock of in-process foreclosures. Plummeted with strong housing market.

aUSMGD3HQ/A.meaning: All loans, 30 days past due — early-stage mortgage delinquency. Most mortgages in this bucket cure (return to current) within 60 days.
aUSMGD3HQ/A.how_to_use: First sign of stress; cure rates ~70%. Watch the 30→60 progression rate as the meaningful credit-stress signal. Currently ~2% (vs ~5% peak in 2009).

aUSMGD6HQ/A.meaning: All loans, 60 days past due — mid-stage mortgage delinquency. Cure rates lower than 30-day (~40%); higher likelihood of progression to 90+ or foreclosure.
aUSMGD6HQ/A.how_to_use: Track for credit-cycle escalation. The 30→60 progression rate is a leading indicator of foreclosure starts. Currently ~0.7%.

aUSMGD9HQ/A.meaning: All loans, 90+ days past due — late-stage mortgage delinquency. High probability of foreclosure absent loan modification or short sale.
aUSMGD9HQ/A.how_to_use: Most-watched mortgage-stress bucket. Currently ~0.8% (vs 5% peak in 2010). Sustained increase signals housing-credit cycle turning.

aUSMALSO/A.meaning: Total Loans Serviced — number of mortgages being administered by servicers. Tracks mortgage-servicing industry size.
aUSMALSO/A.how_to_use: Servicing rights are valuable assets; track for servicing-industry consolidation patterns. Slows when refinance activity is low (no new originations being serviced).

aUSMGAAQ.meaning: MBA Mortgage Applications week-over-week change — composite of purchase + refinance applications. Released Wednesdays for the prior week.
aUSMGAAQ.how_to_use: Highest-frequency mortgage-demand gauge. Refinance index spikes on rate drops; purchase index follows housing-market activity. Pair with the rate level (aUSMGAR) for the rate-vs-volume relationship.

aUSMGPIAG.meaning: MBA Purchase Index — weekly mortgage-purchase application volume. Pure home-purchase demand gauge (excludes refinance).
aUSMGPIAG.how_to_use: Better real-estate-demand gauge than headline MBA index. Falls before existing home sales (purchase apps lead closings by 30-60 days). Currently weak as elevated rates suppress purchase demand.

aUSMGMAG.meaning: MBA Mortgage Market Index — composite of purchase + refinance volumes. Headline mortgage-application gauge.
aUSMGMAG.how_to_use: Volatile due to refi-rate-sensitivity. Refi spikes (when rates drop sharply) drive index moves but matter less for housing-market activity than purchase apps. Decompose to purchase + refi for clean signal.

aUSMGRAG.meaning: MBA Mortgage Refinance Index — weekly refinance application volume. Highly rate-sensitive: 50bp drop in rates can drive 50% spike in this index.
aUSMGRAG.how_to_use: Refi applications signal household interest in lowering payments. Most-locked-in borrowers from 2020-21 lows have no incentive to refi until rates fall toward 5%. Currently very low.

aUSMAH/A.meaning: Mortgage applications week-over-week change — same conceptual measure as aUSMGAAQ. Cross-check series.
aUSMAH/A.how_to_use: Use whichever is fresher. The MBA index is the standard benchmark for high-frequency mortgage activity.

aUSMTCMI/A.description: Mortgage applications, conventional market index, refinancing
aUSMTCMI/A.meaning: MBA Conventional Mortgage Market Index, refinance — refinance applications for conventional (non-government-insured) mortgages.
aUSMTCMI/A.how_to_use: Conventional-borrower-segment refinance gauge. Cleaner signal than total refi (excludes FHA/VA streamline programs which have different drivers).

aUSMTGMI/A.description: Mortgage applications, government market index, refinancing
aUSMTGMI/A.meaning: MBA Government Mortgage Market Index, refinance — refinance applications for government-insured (FHA/VA/USDA) mortgages.
aUSMTGMI/A.how_to_use: Government-program borrower segment. FHA streamline refi is rate-sensitive even at small rate drops because FHA is a fixed-spread market. Useful for tracking lower-credit-quality borrower behavior.

aUSMACI/A.meaning: MBA Mortgage Applications Composite Index — weekly Mortgage Bankers Association survey. Real-time housing-finance demand.
aUSMACI/A.how_to_use: Composite of purchase + refi indices. Most cyclical when refi-driven (rate-cycle bellwether — surges when rates fall). Purchase index is the cleaner housing-demand gauge.

aUSMACP/A.description: Mortgage applications, market composite index, purchase
aUSMACP/A.meaning: MBA Purchase Mortgage Applications Index — purchase only (excludes refi). The cleanest housing-demand-side gauge.
aUSMACP/A.how_to_use: Leads existing home sales by 1-2 months. Less rate-sensitive than refi but still rate-driven. Affordability (aUSHAI) drives multi-quarter trends.

aUSMACRI/A.description: Mortgage applications, market composite index, refinancing
aUSMACRI/A.meaning: MBA Refinance Mortgage Applications Index. Highly rate-sensitive — surges when rates fall ~50bp from local peak.
aUSMACRI/A.how_to_use: Refi waves are the canonical mortgage-rate-cycle indicator. Most outstanding mortgages have low locked-in rates (pre-2022 issuance), so refi index requires rates to fall well below 6% to reactivate.

aUSADPAO.description: ADP National Employment - Actual, Absolute change
aUSADPAO.meaning: Absolute period-over-period change in ADP private-sector employment (national region).
aUSADPAO.how_to_use: ADP private-payrolls release, two days before BLS NFP. Methodology change in 2022 makes ADP a less-reliable NFP predictor than it once was. Useful as a sectoral cross-check but not the headline.

aUSEMPADP/A.description: Labour Market n.i.e, ADP total nonfarm private employment (estimate)
aUSEMPADP/A.meaning: ADP private-sector employment estimate — released two days BEFORE the official BLS NFP. Based on ADP's payroll-processing client base.
aUSEMPADP/A.how_to_use: Methodology overhaul in 2022 made ADP a less-reliable NFP predictor. Use as a sectoral cross-check, not as a leading indicator of the BLS print. ADP captures small business better than BLS; BLS captures large + government better.

aUSLABFRCP.description: Activity, Labour Force, Civilian labor force, total, Employment & Hours, Monthly, Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor
aUSLABFRCP.meaning: Activity, Labour Force, Civilian labor force, total, Employment & Hours, Monthly, Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor.
aUSLABFRCP.how_to_use: Sub-component or variant within Employment & Hours. No standard practitioner usage notes have been written for this specific RIC — consult the upstream source publication (BEA, BLS, Federal Reserve, Census, USDA, EIA, or the relevant industry survey) for the formal definition before using it.

aUSCIVILPF.description: Activity, Labour Force, Civilian noninstitutional population
aUSCIVILPF.meaning: Level of a US population cohort.
aUSCIVILPF.how_to_use: Working-age population drives labor supply trend; aging cohorts drive Medicare/Social Security demand. Total US population growth has slowed to ~0.5%/yr from ~1%/yr historically.

aUSEMPNF/A.how_to_use: First Friday of the month, BLS release. Single most market-moving US data print. Watch (a) MoM change vs consensus, (b) prior-month revisions, (c) sectoral breakdown, (d) hours and earnings in the same release.

aUSJOLTAO.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS Job Openings
aUSJOLTAO.meaning: JOLTS Job Openings — total US job postings at the end of each month. BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, released ~6 weeks lagged.
aUSJOLTAO.how_to_use: Openings/unemployed ratio (V/U) is the Fed's preferred labor-tightness gauge. V/U > 1.5 = very tight; V/U < 1.0 = loose. Crashed from 2.0 in 2022 toward 1.0 in 2024 — Fed's 'soft landing' is partly built on this falling without UR rising.

aUSJBHIREO/A.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS, Nonfarm, Hires
aUSJBHIREO/A.meaning: Level of a JOLTS measure — BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, monthly. Job openings = posted vacancies; hires = new starts; quits = voluntary departures; separations = total departures.
aUSJBHIREO/A.how_to_use: Quits rate is the cleanest worker-confidence gauge — high quits = workers confident they can find better jobs. Openings/unemployed ratio (V/U) was Fed's preferred labor-tightness gauge during 2022-23 wage-spiral concerns.

aUSJBOPENO/A.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS, Nonfarm, Job openings
aUSJBOPENO/A.meaning: Level of a JOLTS measure — BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, monthly. Job openings = posted vacancies; hires = new starts; quits = voluntary departures; separations = total departures.
aUSJBOPENO/A.how_to_use: Quits rate is the cleanest worker-confidence gauge — high quits = workers confident they can find better jobs. Openings/unemployed ratio (V/U) was Fed's preferred labor-tightness gauge during 2022-23 wage-spiral concerns.

aUSJBLOFFP.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS, Nonfarm, Layoffs and discharges
aUSJBLOFFP.meaning: Level of a JOLTS measure — BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, monthly. Job openings = posted vacancies; hires = new starts; quits = voluntary departures; separations = total departures.
aUSJBLOFFP.how_to_use: Quits rate is the cleanest worker-confidence gauge — high quits = workers confident they can find better jobs. Openings/unemployed ratio (V/U) was Fed's preferred labor-tightness gauge during 2022-23 wage-spiral concerns.

aUSJBQUITO/A.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS, Nonfarm, Quits
aUSJBQUITO/A.meaning: JOLTS Quits — voluntary departures. The cleanest worker-confidence gauge: high quits = workers confident they can find better jobs.
aUSJBQUITO/A.how_to_use: Leads wage growth by 3-6 months (aUSEARNH/A YoY). 'Great Resignation' peak in 2022 (4.5M+/mo) faded by 2024. Quits below pre-pandemic baseline = workers locked in, wage growth moderating.

aUSJBSEPRO/A.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS, Nonfarm, Total separations
aUSJBSEPRO/A.meaning: Level of a JOLTS measure — BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, monthly. Job openings = posted vacancies; hires = new starts; quits = voluntary departures; separations = total departures.
aUSJBSEPRO/A.how_to_use: Quits rate is the cleanest worker-confidence gauge — high quits = workers confident they can find better jobs. Openings/unemployed ratio (V/U) was Fed's preferred labor-tightness gauge during 2022-23 wage-spiral concerns.
