aUSELSATOP.meaning: Total electricity sales across all sectors (residential, commercial, industrial, transportation).
aUSELSATOP.how_to_use: Real-economy demand gauge. Industrial sales lead manufacturing cycles; residential is weather-driven. Adjust for cooling/heating-degree-days for cycle signal.

aUSWEAICDD.meaning: Cooling degree-days — sum of (daily mean temperature − 65°F) when above 65°F. Higher = more AC demand.
aUSWEAICDD.how_to_use: Use to weather-adjust electricity, gas, and natgas storage data. Hot summer = high CDD = high electricity demand.

aUSWEAIHDD.meaning: Heating degree-days — sum of (65°F − daily mean) when below 65°F. Higher = more heating demand.
aUSWEAIHDD.how_to_use: Critical for natgas demand modeling — winter HDD drives storage drawdowns. Use 5-year normal as baseline.

aUSWIPRINP.how_to_use: Agricultural/hydro power input. Pair with crop progress reports for harvest forecasting.

aUSWIPRMMP.meaning: Total precipitation in millimeters — same data, metric units.
aUSWIPRMMP.how_to_use: Use whichever unit your model expects.

aUSSCBBR.meaning: Semiconductor equipment book-to-bill ratio — orders / shipments. Above 1.0 = orders outpace shipments (expanding).
aUSSCBBR.how_to_use: Leads semi capex cycle by 1-2 quarters. Watch for sustained sub-1.0 prints as recession warning.

aUSRSCO.meaning: US proved crude oil reserves — annual.
aUSRSCO.how_to_use: Reserve replacement ratio (additions vs production) is the long-run sustainability gauge. Surged with shale; growth slowing as best Permian acreage drilled.

aUSEXPFMGP.how_to_use: US is now a net products exporter despite being a net crude importer until ~2019 — refinery capacity exceeds domestic demand.

aUSIMCOP.how_to_use: Halved post-shale (2008-2020) but stable since. Source mix matters: Canada heavy crude is irreplaceable in Gulf Coast refineries.

aUSNGGWDRP.meaning: Gross natural gas withdrawals — total production from wells.
aUSNGGWDRP.how_to_use: US is world's largest natgas producer. Watch alongside Henry Hub prices and LNG export terminal utilization.

aUSINCOXRP.description: STOCKS - CRUDE OIL EXCLUDING STRATEGIC PETROLEUM RESERVES
aUSINCOXRP.meaning: Crude oil stocks excluding Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
aUSINCOXRP.how_to_use: Most-watched oil inventory series. Weekly EIA report moves prices; surprises vs API/consensus drive intraday action.

aUSINCOP.description: STOCKS - CRUDE OIL INCL STRATEGIC PETROLEUM RESERVES
aUSINCOP.how_to_use: Less useful than ex-SPR — SPR moves are policy-driven, not market-driven.

aUSINPPP.description: STOCKS - PETROLEUM & PRODUCTS INCL STRATEGIC PETROLEUM RESERVES
aUSINPPP.meaning: Total petroleum and products stocks (crude + gasoline + distillates etc).
aUSINPPP.how_to_use: Aggregate liquidity gauge. Big draws during driving season (gasoline) and winter (distillates).

aUSINSPRP.how_to_use: Drained 200M+ bbl in 2022 (Russia/Ukraine response). Refilling has been slow. Below ~350M bbl is historically low.

aUSBISNXBR.description: BIS, Nominal Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index
aUSBISNXBR.meaning: BIS Nominal Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index — comprehensive USD strength gauge against ~60 trading partners. Bank for International Settlements.
aUSBISNXBR.how_to_use: Broader than Fed TWI; methodologically different weights. Use as cross-check on Fed series. BIS series has the longest cross-country history.

aUSBISNXNR.description: BIS, Nominal Narrow Effective Exchange Rate Index
aUSBISNXNR.meaning: Nominal Narrow Effective Exchange Rate Index — narrower basket (~26 advanced economies).
aUSBISNXNR.how_to_use: Cleaner read on G10 USD positioning. Less noise from EM volatility.

aUSBISRXBR.description: BIS, Real Broad Effective Exchange Rate Index
aUSBISRXBR.meaning: Real (CPI-adjusted) Broad Effective Exchange Rate. Captures real competitiveness.
aUSBISRXBR.how_to_use: True purchasing power gauge. Rising real EER = US loses real competitiveness even if nominal rate flat.

aUSBISRXNR.description: BIS, Real Narrow Effective Exchange Rate Index
aUSBISRXNR.how_to_use: Use alongside the broad index. Narrow vs broad gap = EM vs DM USD strength.

aUSXRUSD.meaning: USD/EUR exchange rate — noon NY fixing. The most-traded FX pair globally.
aUSXRUSD.how_to_use: Largest weight in trade-weighted USD (~25%). EUR strength typically reflects relative ECB-Fed policy stance + relative growth. EUR is a low-beta currency in risk-off (counterintuitively).

aUSCORP/A.meaning: Commercial Paper rate — short-term corporate borrowing.
aUSCORP/A.how_to_use: Front-end credit gauge. Spread to T-bills (CP-bill spread) widens in stress.

aUS0CWMCRF/C.description: Federal Reserve, Price-adjusted Trade Weighted Exchange Real Index Major Currencies
aUS0CWMCRF/C.meaning: Fed Trade Weighted Real Index — Major Currencies.
aUS0CWMCRF/C.how_to_use: Fed's own real USD index. Diverges slightly from BIS due to weighting methodology.

aUSCWMCRF/C.description: Federal Reserve, Real Advanced Foreign Economies Dollar Index
aUSCWMCRF/C.meaning: Fed Real Advanced Foreign Economies Dollar Index.
aUSCWMCRF/C.how_to_use: Newer Fed index focused on AE trading partners — successor to the Major Currencies index.

aUSCXTWPF.description: Trade Weighted nominal exchange rate, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCXTWPF.meaning: Trade-weighted nominal USD MoM % change, standardized.
aUSCXTWPF.how_to_use: High-frequency USD strength signal. Watch alongside DXY.

aUSCXTWYF.description: Trade Weighted nominal exchange rate, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCXTWYF.meaning: Trade-weighted nominal USD YoY % change. The most market-relevant USD strength gauge for cycle-cycle comparisons.
aUSCXTWYF.how_to_use: >5% YoY USD strength is historically a drag on US multinational EPS (S&P 500 derives ~40% of revenue overseas). Triggers translation hedging activity in corporate treasury.

aUSCXTWF/C.description: Trade Weighted nominal exchange rate, Standardized
aUSCXTWF/C.meaning: Trade-weighted nominal US dollar index, standardized — Fed's broad USD strength gauge against major + emerging trading partners. Refinitiv/LSEG version.
aUSCXTWF/C.how_to_use: Rising = stronger USD = headwind for US exporters and EM debt service. Sub-components: USD vs DM (G10) vs USD vs EM. ~50% weight is EUR/CNY/JPY/MXN/CAD combined.

aUSCXTRPF.description: Trade Weighted real exchange rate, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCXTRPF.how_to_use: Strips inflation differentials. Cleaner competitiveness signal than nominal.

aUSCXTRYF.description: Trade Weighted real exchange rate, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCXTRYF.how_to_use: Best annual USD competitiveness measure for trade modeling.

aUSCXTRF/C.description: Trade Weighted real exchange rate, Standardized
aUSCXTRF/C.meaning: Trade-weighted REAL USD index (CPI-adjusted) — strips inflation differentials. The cleaner competitiveness signal.
aUSCXTRF/C.how_to_use: Diverges from nominal USD when inflation differs across trading partners. Real USD up while nominal flat = US loses real competitiveness even with stable nominal rate.

aUSOCFPP/A.description: Purchasing power parity, National currency per USD
aUSOCFPP/A.meaning: Purchasing power parity — units of national currency per USD. For US, this is base = 1.0.
aUSOCFPP/A.how_to_use: Useful only for cross-country GDP comparisons. Not market-tradable.

aUS66OLLBA.description: Brokers & dealers loans to nonfinancial corporate business
aUS66OLLBA.meaning: Brokers & dealers, loans to nonfinancial corporate business. Quarterly Z.1.
aUS66OLLBA.how_to_use: Margin/securities-financing channel of corporate debt. Surges in crises (e.g., 2008 hedge fund deleveraging).

aUS73PCDLA.description: Commercial banks holding of direct commercial paper
aUS73PCDLA.meaning: Commercial banks holding of direct commercial paper.
aUS73PCDLA.how_to_use: Bank participation in CP market. Watch as a money-market liquidity gauge.

aUS16IENN.how_to_use: Niche line; small fraction of NPISH balance sheet.

aUS31FGDSB/A.meaning: Federal government debt securities, liability — Z.1 flows.
aUS31FGDSB/A.how_to_use: Quarterly issuance flow. Cross-check against Treasury auction data.

aUS31FGDSA.meaning: Federal government debt securities, liability — Flow of Funds Z.1 measure of total federal debt held outside Treasury (treasury securities held by the public + non-Treasury federal liabilities).
aUS31FGDSA.how_to_use: Most-comprehensive federal-debt measure in Z.1 framework. Cross-check against Treasury Direct figures (aUSPDEBTA, aUSFEDETOS). The Z.1 includes some categories that Treasury direct excludes (FHLB, GNMA pools).

aUS31HCFLB/A.description: Federal government, Retiree healthcare fund, chg at annual rate
aUS31HCFLB/A.meaning: Federal retiree healthcare fund, change at annual rate.

aUSFFLNPO.description: Flow of Funds Balance Sheet, Household and nonprofit organizations, Net worth
aUSFFLNPO.meaning: Household and NPO net worth — total household wealth (Z.1 B.101).
aUSFFLNPO.how_to_use: The headline 'household wealth' number. Crashed 2008, hit ~$160T+ in 2024. Wealth-effect driver for consumption.

aUSDEBTDF/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic financial sectors
aUSDEBTDF/A.how_to_use: Total leverage in financial intermediaries. Plateaued post-2008 as banks deleveraged; nonbank finance grew.

aUS31CM1DB/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, federal government
aUS31CM1DB/A.how_to_use: Component of total domestic nonfinancial debt — federal share.

aUS14CM3DB/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, nonfederal, business total
aUS14CM3DB/A.how_to_use: Sum of corporate + noncorporate. Watch debt/GDP for leverage cycle.

aUS10CM3DB/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, nonfederal, business, corporate
aUS10CM3DB/A.how_to_use: Corporate leverage gauge. Includes loans + bonds. Hit 50%+ of GDP — historically high.

aUS15CM1DB/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, nonfederal, households total
aUS15CM1DB/A.how_to_use: Mortgage + consumer credit + auto + student. ~$20T total. Debt service ratio is lower than 2008 peak.

aUS15CCTDB/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, nonfederal, households, consumer credit
aUS15CCTDB/A.how_to_use: Front-end delinquencies elevated; flagging stress in subprime credit card / auto.

aUS15MGHDB/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, nonfederal, households, home mortgages
aUS15MGHDB/A.how_to_use: Largest household debt category. Delinquencies low but housing market frozen at high mortgage rates.

aUS21CM1DB/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, nonfederal, state and local government
aUS21CM1DB/A.meaning: State and local government debt outstanding (Z.1).
aUS21CM1DB/A.how_to_use: Munis. ~$3T total. Watch general obligation vs revenue bond mix.

aUSDEBTDN/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Domestic nonfinancial sectors, total
aUSDEBTDN/A.meaning: Total domestic nonfinancial debt (Z.1) — government + business + household.
aUSDEBTDN/A.how_to_use: Master leverage gauge. >300% of GDP currently. The denominator (GDP) growth determines sustainability.

aUSDEBTF/A.description: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Foreign
aUSDEBTF/A.meaning: Flow of Funds Debt Outstanding, Foreign — debt instruments held by foreign sectors. Includes Treasury holdings (TIC data) plus corporate and agency debt.
aUSDEBTF/A.how_to_use: Tracks foreign claims on US debt — the financing side of US current-account deficits. Slowing foreign demand has been a Treasury concern post-2022 as China and Japan reduced Treasury holdings; partial offset from Europe.

aUSXZLFFRA.description: Flow of Funds Instruments, Federal funds and security repo, Effective federal funds rate (percent)
aUSXZLFFRA.meaning: Flow of Funds: Federal funds and security repos — total fed-funds + repo lending volumes in the financial system. Z.1 quarterly.
aUSXZLFFRA.how_to_use: Tracks unsecured (fed funds) + secured (repo) interbank lending volumes. Repo dominates post-2008 (~$5T+ daily); fed funds is small (~$100B). Stress signals: spikes in repo rates relative to IORB indicate funding pressure.

aUSLGCMBAA.description: Flow of Funds Summaries, Domestic Nonfinancial Sector, CREDIT MARKET DEBT - PRIVATE DOMESTIC NONFIN (FOF ASSET)
aUSLGCMBAA.meaning: Domestic Nonfinancial Sector — credit market debt, private domestic.
aUSLGCMBAA.how_to_use: Private credit excludes federal. Cleaner cycle gauge than total.

aUS19MGHLA.description: Home mortgages, private domestic nonfinancial, not state & local
aUS19MGHLA.meaning: Home mortgages, private domestic nonfinancial — total household mortgage debt outstanding. The largest household liability category.
aUS19MGHLA.how_to_use: Tracks ~$13T household mortgage book. Growth slows sharply in housing-rate-shock periods (2022-23). Pair with mortgage-origination flows and home-price appreciation for the housing-finance cycle.

aUS15OLLHA.description: Household sector loans to nonfinancial corporate business
aUS15OLLHA.meaning: Household sector loans to nonfinancial corporate business.

aUS11RESTA.description: Nonfinancial Noncorporate Business, Assets, real estate
aUS11RESTA.meaning: Nonfinancial noncorporate business — real estate assets.
aUS11RESTA.how_to_use: CRE held outside corporate structures (sole prop, partnerships).

aUS11CHNIA.description: Nonfinancial noncorporate business, net increase in liabilities
aUS11CHNIA.meaning: Nonfinancial noncorporate business, net increase in liabilities.

aUS11CHNLA.meaning: Nonfinancial noncorporate business, net lending position.
aUS11CHNLA.how_to_use: Net financial position of small/private businesses.

aUS54PCCLA.meaning: Policy and contract claims, life insurance — life-insurance company liabilities to policyholders. Reflects expected future claim payouts.
aUS54PCCLA.how_to_use: Stable balance-sheet item. Useful for tracking life-insurance industry size. Major investor in long-duration assets (Treasuries, corporates, mortgages) — track for institutional fixed-income demand patterns.

aUS54PCCLB/A.description: Policy & contract claims, life insurance, chg at annual rate
aUS54PCCLB/A.meaning: Policy and contract claims, life insurance, change at annual rate.

aUS10XXAA.meaning: Total assets, all sectors — Flow of Funds Z.1 measure of total assets in the US economy. Aggregate balance-sheet wealth.
aUS10XXAA.how_to_use: Tracks total economy balance sheet. Used in wealth-effect calculations (consumption sensitivity to wealth changes). Most analytically useful at the household-sector subset level (separate Z.1 series).

aUS14SGTAA.meaning: Treasury securities held by nonfinancial business.
aUS14SGTAA.how_to_use: Corporate Treasury holdings — cash management. Surged with corporate cash piles post-2010.

aUSNCIOAA.description: Foreign Net Treasury International Capital Flows - Actual, USD
aUSNCIOAA.meaning: Foreign net Treasury international capital flows — actual.
aUSNCIOAA.how_to_use: TIC data: foreign demand for US debt. Big swings move long-end yields.

aUSNCISAA.how_to_use: Cleaner foreign demand signal stripping out short-term flows.

aUSNCIAA.description: Net purchases (net long-term capital inflows), total, Financial & Flow of Funds Accounts, Monthly, U.S. Department of the Treasury
aUSNCIAA.meaning: Net purchases (net long-term capital inflows), total.
aUSNCIAA.how_to_use: Headline TIC flow. Moves from policy regime shifts (e.g., China reducing UST holdings).

aUSFBTAA.description: Net purchases of U.S. treasury bonds & notes, total net foreign purchases, Financial & Flow of Funds Accounts, Monthly, U.S. Department of the Treasury
aUSFBTAA.meaning: Net foreign purchases of US Treasury bonds and notes.
aUSFBTAA.how_to_use: Most-watched TIC line. Persistent net buying needed to fund deficit.

aUSNSH47W.meaning: Balance on current account in NIPA terms — net of trade in goods, services, primary income (investment income), and secondary income (transfers).
aUSNSH47W.how_to_use: Differs slightly from BEA's headline current account due to NIPA accounting conventions. Persistent current-account deficits funded by capital inflows; reversal of inflows is a tail risk.

aUSN4RIKM.description: Current receipts from rest of world
aUSN4RIKM.meaning: Total current receipts from rest of world — exports of goods/services + income receipts + transfers from abroad.
aUSN4RIKM.how_to_use: Pair with current payments to compute the current-account balance. Strong dollar typically compresses receipts in USD terms (J-curve dynamics).

aUSN7DXQY.meaning: Exports of durable goods (capital equipment, autos, industrial supplies, consumer durables).
aUSN7DXQY.how_to_use: More cyclical than nondurables — leads the global capex cycle. Pair against ISM new export orders and global PMI for forward signal.

aUSNYV66Y.meaning: Exports of nondurable goods (food, energy, chemicals, agricultural products).
aUSNYV66Y.how_to_use: Less cyclical, more commodity-sensitive. Energy exports (US is a net exporter post-shale) drive much of the recent trend; strip them out for non-energy reads.

aUSGDPCC/CA.meaning: GDP per capita — total nominal GDP divided by population. Quarterly.
aUSGDPCC/CA.how_to_use: Long-run living-standards gauge. Use real (inflation-adjusted) per capita for cross-country comparison. The level matters less than the YoY growth rate.

aUSNZJZTM.meaning: Imports of durable goods. Larger than exports — the durables trade deficit is structural.
aUSNZJZTM.how_to_use: Cycles with US capex and consumer durables demand. Watch share from China (with tariff overlay) for trade-policy effects.

aUSN4VL9L.meaning: Imports of nondurable goods (food, beverages, energy, consumer staples).
aUSN4VL9L.how_to_use: Steadier than durables imports. Energy imports collapsed post-shale; what remains is mostly consumer staples.

aUSNS7V3L.meaning: Net lending or borrowing position vs rest of world (NIPA basis). Mirror of current-account balance with a few NIPA adjustments.
aUSNS7V3L.how_to_use: Positive = US is net lender (saving > investment), negative = net borrower. Persistent negatives need capital inflow to fund.

aUSN1RIK0/C.description: Average of GDP & gross domestic income, Constant Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Annual, BEA - Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. Department of Commerce
aUSN1RIK0/C.how_to_use: Primary US output gauge. Two consecutive negative quarters is the textbook recession (NBER uses a broader definition). Compare to consensus and to nominal GDP — divergence reflects inflation. Watch the advance/second/third revision sequence for direction.

aUSN1RIJY.description: Average of GDP & gross domestic income, Current Prices, GDP by Expenditure, Annual, BEA - Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. Department of Commerce
aUSN1RIJY.meaning: Level of nominal (current-dollar) US GDP — the dollar value of all final goods and services produced in the US in a given period.
aUSN1RIJY.how_to_use: Master scale variable. Real GDP for output cycle; nominal GDP for fiscal-burden ratios (debt/GDP), share calculations, and tax-base modeling.

aUSCGDHD/CA.description: GDP per capita, Constant prices, Standardized (based on annual data)
aUSCGDHD/CA.meaning: Real (inflation-adjusted) us gdp, standardized for cross-country comparison.

aUSCGDPPD/A.how_to_use: Single most-watched US growth indicator. Two consecutive negative quarters is the textbook recession definition (NBER uses broader). Compare against consensus (aUSAGDPF). Three vintages: advance (Q+30 days), second (Q+60), third (Q+90) — revisions can move 50-100bp.

aUSGDEFAA.how_to_use: The headline fiscal print. Cyclical: widens in recessions (auto stabilizers), narrows in expansions. Recent run rate ~$1.5-2T deficit annually post-COVID, structurally elevated relative to pre-2020. Watch primary deficit (excl interest) for underlying fiscal stance.

aUSGDEF.description: Federal Government total surplus or deficit
aUSGDEF.meaning: Federal government total surplus or deficit — annual/fiscal-year aggregate, complementary to the monthly aUSGDEFAA series. Same conceptual measure at lower frequency.
aUSGDEF.how_to_use: Use the monthly series (aUSGDEFAA) for high-frequency tracking; use this annual aggregate for historical comparison. Compare to GDP for the deficit-to-GDP ratio, the standard sustainability metric (~5-7% in recent years).

aUSXGBJUSA.meaning: Federal outlays: administration of justice — DOJ, FBI, federal courts, immigration enforcement, prisons. ~$70B annually.
aUSXGBJUSA.how_to_use: Discretionary spending. Watch for immigration-enforcement appropriations (DHS budget surge under Trump 2017+ and 2025+). Smaller share of total but politically watched.

aUSXGBAGA.how_to_use: Highly variable: farm bill cycle and price-support programs swing the line item.

aUSXGBCHCA.description: Federal outlays, commerce and housing credit
aUSXGBCHCA.meaning: Federal outlays — commerce and housing credit.
aUSXGBCHCA.how_to_use: Includes Fannie/Freddie support, SBA. Surged in COVID (PPP loans).

aUSXGBDEVA.description: Federal outlays, community and regional development
aUSXGBDEVA.meaning: Federal outlays: community and regional development — HUD community-development block grants, EDA programs, rural development. ~$40B annually.
aUSXGBDEVA.how_to_use: Small discretionary category. Includes urban-renewal grants and rural infrastructure funding. Watch for major program changes (CDBG zeroed in some Trump budgets, restored in others).

aUSXGBETSA.description: Federal outlays, education, training, empl & social serv
aUSXGBETSA.meaning: Federal outlays — education, training, employment & social services.
aUSXGBETSA.how_to_use: Department of Education + DOL. Student-loan-related outlays move this materially.

aUSXGBEGYA.how_to_use: ~1% of outlays. Includes nuclear weapons stewardship via NNSA.

aUSXGBGENA.meaning: Federal outlays: general government — Treasury, GSA, OPM, central agencies. The 'overhead' of running the federal government.
aUSXGBGENA.how_to_use: Stable around $30-40B. Useful for tracking federal-workforce size; rises when Congress funds federal pay raises.

aUSXGBSCIA.description: Federal outlays, general science, space and technology
aUSXGBSCIA.meaning: Federal outlays: general science, space and technology — NASA, NSF, basic research. ~$45B annually.
aUSXGBSCIA.how_to_use: Includes NASA (~$25B). NSF and DOE basic research split the rest. Track for science-policy debates and Mars-mission/Artemis funding.

aUSXGBHLTA.meaning: Federal outlays: health (excluding Medicare) — Medicaid, NIH, CDC, CHIP, public health. ~$700B annually combined.
aUSXGBHLTA.how_to_use: Medicaid is the dominant component (~$600B federal share, with state matches adding more). Growth driven by ACA expansion, demographic aging, and per-enrollee medical-cost inflation. ACA Medicaid expansion in 41 states drove sustained growth post-2014.

aUSXGBINCA.meaning: Federal outlays — income security (unemployment, SNAP, housing assistance).
aUSXGBINCA.how_to_use: Counter-cyclical: spikes in recessions. The COVID UI surge dominated 2020-21.

aUSXGBINTA.meaning: Federal outlays: net interest — interest paid on federal debt minus interest received. Fastest-growing major category as debt level meets higher rates.
aUSXGBINTA.how_to_use: Has crossed $1T annually post-2024, exceeding defense outlays. Trajectory determined by both debt growth (deficits) and average rate on debt (refinancing higher-coupon debt). Major fiscal sustainability concern; CBO projects net interest reaching 4% of GDP by 2034.

aUSXGBDIPA.meaning: Federal outlays: international affairs — State Department, USAID, foreign aid, embassies. ~$70B annually.
aUSXGBDIPA.how_to_use: ~1% of federal budget. Includes military aid (Israel, Ukraine, Egypt, Jordan), economic aid, multilateral commitments. Variable: surges during major foreign aid (Ukraine 2022-25) or pandemic response.

aUSXGBMEDA.meaning: Federal outlays: Medicare — health insurance for 65+ population (~65M beneficiaries). Second-largest federal outlay, ~$1T and growing fastest among major categories due to aging + medical-cost inflation.
aUSXGBMEDA.how_to_use: Hospital Insurance (Part A) trust fund projected insolvent ~2031. Total Medicare growth ~6%/year vs ~4% economic growth — structural fiscal stress. Watch alongside Medicaid (state-level partner program) for total federal health-care fiscal exposure.

aUSXGBDEFA.meaning: Federal outlays: national defense — DOD plus military assistance, atomic energy defense activities. ~$850B annually, ~13% of total federal outlays.
aUSXGBDEFA.how_to_use: Has fallen from ~5% of GDP in 2010 to ~3% in 2024 as percent of GDP, even as nominal level rose. Discretionary spending (subject to annual appropriations) — the largest target for budget negotiations. Geopolitical events (Ukraine, Middle East) have driven supplemental requests.

aUSXGBNATA.description: Federal outlays, natural resources and environment
aUSXGBNATA.meaning: Federal outlays: natural resources and environment — EPA, Interior, USFS, USGS. ~$45B annually.
aUSXGBNATA.how_to_use: Includes federal lands management (BLM, USFS), national parks, EPA enforcement. Watch for environmental-policy shifts; major budget changes often tied to administration changes.

aUSXGBSOCA.meaning: Federal outlays: Social Security — retirement and survivor benefits to ~67M beneficiaries. Largest single federal outlay category, ~$1.4T annually and growing with demographics.
aUSXGBSOCA.how_to_use: Mandatory spending — paid by formula not appropriations. Trust Fund projected to be insolvent by ~2034 absent legislation; would trigger automatic ~20% benefit cut. Track demographic profile (boomer retirement wave continues through 2034).

aUSFOUTL.meaning: Federal government outlays (total) — Social Security, Medicare/Medicaid, defense, interest on debt, all other discretionary + mandatory programs. Released monthly by Treasury.
aUSFOUTL.how_to_use: Mandatory + interest now ~75% of outlays — limited room for discretionary cuts. Net interest outlays passing $1T annually, growing fastest. Track interest-as-share-of-revenues for fiscal-sustainability stress signal (now ~20%, doubled vs 2010s).

aUSXGBTRNA.meaning: Federal outlays — transportation (DOT, FAA, highway trust fund).
aUSXGBTRNA.how_to_use: Infrastructure spending tracked here. IIJA boost showing through.

aUSXGBOFFA.meaning: Undistributed offsetting receipts — negative line (mineral leases, employer share of pension contributions).
aUSXGBOFFA.how_to_use: Treated as negative outlay in budget accounting. Don't include in 'spending share' analysis.

aUSFEDREC.meaning: Federal government receipts (revenues) — individual income taxes, corporate income taxes, payroll taxes, customs duties, excise taxes. Released monthly by Treasury.
aUSFEDREC.how_to_use: Individual income tax is ~50%, payroll tax ~35%, corporate ~10%. Cyclical: rises with GDP and labor income. April spike from individual tax filings; December peak from corporate quarterly estimated payments. Tariff-policy changes show up in customs duties (small share).

aUSOGBDOVA.description: GOVERNMENT BUDGET OUTLAYS FOR VETERANS BENEFITS
aUSOGBDOVA.how_to_use: Growing line as post-9/11 cohort ages and benefits expand (PACT Act).

aUSCGOVA.meaning: Central government deficit/surplus, standardized — OECD-comparable framing of US federal budget balance. Includes only central-government level (excludes state and local).
aUSCGOVA.how_to_use: Use for cross-country fiscal-position comparisons. US-domestic analysts use unified-budget aUSGDEFAA. The central-government framing aligns with IMF Article IV and OECD reporting.

aUSCGOVPA.description: Central government Deficit/Surplus, month on month, Standardized, Absolute change
aUSCGOVPA.meaning: Central government balance MoM absolute change.

aUSCGOVYA.description: Central government Deficit/Surplus, year on year, Standardized, Absolute change
aUSCGOVYA.meaning: Central government balance YoY absolute change.
aUSCGOVYA.how_to_use: Cleaner trend; strips monthly tax-timing noise.

aUSFYONET.meaning: Federal net outlays — outlays minus offsetting receipts (user fees, royalties on federal lands, mineral leases). The 'net spending' figure used in budget arithmetic.
aUSFYONET.how_to_use: Smaller than gross outlays by ~$200B (offsetting receipts). Use for budget-arithmetic consistency; gross outlays (aUSFOUTL) is the more commonly cited measure.

aUSFYFRCT.meaning: Federal receipts (alternative framing) — companion to aUSFEDREC at potentially different release vintage.
aUSFYFRCT.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever is fresher. The OMB and Treasury release the same data with slight timing differences.

aUSGBPGDP.description: Federal surplus/deficit as percent of GDP
aUSGBPGDP.meaning: Federal surplus/deficit as % of GDP — the standard fiscal-stance gauge.
aUSGBPGDP.how_to_use: >5% deficit during expansion is highly unusual and signals limited fiscal room for the next recession. Compare to historical norm (~2-3% during expansions). Fiscal projections (CBO baseline) suggest persistence above 5%.

aUSFEDETOS.meaning: Federal debt total amount outstanding — Treasury's gross debt position including all marketable securities (bills, notes, bonds, TIPS, FRNs) and nonmarketable issuances (savings bonds, intragovernmental).
aUSFEDETOS.how_to_use: Tracks the running tally of Treasury issuance. The marketable-debt subset (~$27T) is what funds the actual federal deficit; nonmarketable debt is mostly Trust Fund holdings. Issuance pattern (bills vs notes/bonds) signals Treasury's term-structure strategy.

aUSPDEBTA.meaning: Public debt outstanding — total Treasury debt held by both the public and intragovernmental accounts (Trust Funds). The 'gross debt' measure mentioned in headlines around the debt ceiling.
aUSPDEBTA.how_to_use: ~$36T in 2025. The 'debt held by the public' subset (~$28T) is the more economically meaningful measure since intragovernmental debt is a Treasury IOU to itself. Watch debt-ceiling negotiations — extraordinary measures kick in when ceiling is hit.

aUSPDBTR.description: GROSS PUBLIC DEBT AS % OF GDP
aUSPDBTR.meaning: Gross public debt as a percentage of GDP — the standard sustainability gauge using gross (not net of intragovernmental) debt. Higher than debt-held-by-public/GDP by ~25-30 percentage points.
aUSPDBTR.how_to_use: CBO projects debt/GDP rising to 120-130% by 2034 absent policy change. Threshold concerns vary: most economists view 100-120% as 'manageable for reserve currency issuer'; >150% historically associated with fiscal crisis. Watch debt-service/GDP ratio for nearer-term signal.

aUSSECMNSA.meaning: Total Treasury securities outstanding (public debt). Sum of bills, notes, bonds, plus nonmarketable.
aUSSECMNSA.how_to_use: Supply pipeline for Treasury auctions. Acceleration in growth implies more issuance, pressure on term premium.

aUSSECMKBA.meaning: Treasury bills outstanding — short-term debt (≤1Y). The bulk of refinancing risk sits here.
aUSSECMKBA.how_to_use: Heavy bill issuance keeps front-end yields elevated and TGA management active. Watch as % of total marketable debt — rising share signals fiscal stress.

aUSSCMKBNA.meaning: Treasury bonds outstanding — long-term coupon debt (>10Y). Mostly 20Y and 30Y bonds.
aUSSCMKBNA.how_to_use: Long-end supply impacts term premium. Bond issuance schedule announced in quarterly refunding. Demand monitored via primary dealer takedowns and indirect bidder share.

aUSSECNGSA.description: Treasury securities outstanding, nonmarketable, government account series
aUSSECNGSA.meaning: Nonmarketable Treasury securities held in government account series (Social Security, federal pensions, etc).
aUSSECNGSA.how_to_use: Doesn't trade in markets; subtract from gross debt to get marketable supply. Mainly accounting interest.

aUSSECMKNA.meaning: Treasury notes outstanding — coupon debt (2Y to 10Y maturity).
aUSSECMKNA.how_to_use: Belly of the curve — the most common duration target for asset managers. Watch 10Y note auction stats for global demand signal.

aUSSECMKTA.meaning: Total marketable Treasury securities — bills + notes + bonds + TIPS + FRNs. The free-float bond supply (excluding non-marketable issues like savings bonds).
aUSSECMKTA.how_to_use: Compare against M2 to see Treasury vs broad money balance. Bills (≤1Y) currently ~20% of marketable supply — historically high; signals refinancing stress. Issuance schedule announced quarterly in Refunding Statement.

aUSHESALEMD.description: Existing-Home Sales, Single-Family and Condos, median price
aUSHESALEMD.meaning: Level of US existing home sales.
aUSHESALEMD.how_to_use: NAR monthly. ~5x larger than new home sales. Heavily rate-sensitive (most buyers have a low rate to give up). Months-supply is the tight/loose gauge.

aUSHPIMAR.description: FHFA House Price Index- Actual, Chg P/P
aUSHPIMAR.how_to_use: Annualize for comparison: 0.4% MoM ≈ 5% YoY. Volatile single months; 3-month MA cleaner.

aUSHPIYAR.description: FHFA House Price Index- Actual, Chg Y/Y
aUSHPIYAR.meaning: FHFA House Price Index YoY change. Federal Housing Finance Agency — covers conforming-loan-only properties (≤$766k limit in most areas).
aUSHPIYAR.how_to_use: Cleaner than Case-Shiller in distress periods (excludes jumbo, all-cash). Different sample = different reads sometimes. Watch alongside Case-Shiller; if they diverge, jumbo segment is moving differently from conforming.

aUSHPIDAR.meaning: Index reading: House Prices, FHFA House Price Index.
aUSHPIDAR.how_to_use: Sub-component or variant within Housing & Real Estate Prices. No standard practitioner usage notes have been written for this specific RIC — consult the upstream source publication (BEA, BLS, Federal Reserve, Census, USDA, EIA, or the relevant industry survey) for the formal definition before using it.

aUSHSTART.meaning: Housing starts — new privately-owned residential construction projects begun, seasonally adjusted at annual rate. Lagging within the housing cycle (permits lead, starts follow, completions lag further).
aUSHSTART.how_to_use: Pair with building permits (leading) and new home sales (demand-side). Single-family vs multi-family split matters: multi-family is more rate-sensitive and has been the swing factor post-2022. Persistent declines in starts feed through to construction employment and lumber/cement demand.

aUSHNSAO.meaning: New Home Sales — Census monthly count of new single-family homes sold. Released ~25th of each month.
aUSHNSAO.how_to_use: Smaller than existing sales (~1/8) but more cyclical. Builder pricing power gauge. Watch alongside months-supply (a function of new sales pace + inventory) for builder-incentive intensity.

aUSHNSALES/A.meaning: New Home Sales (alternate series) — monthly Census/HUD report of newly built single-family homes sold, measured at contract signing rather than closing. More volatile than existing home sales because of the much smaller sample size (~70k annual transactions vs ~5M existing).
aUSHNSALES/A.how_to_use: Cross-check against the primary new home sales series and against existing home sales. Watch the months-supply ratio for a clean inventory signal — under 4 months is tight, over 7 months is a buyers' market. Builder pricing power and incentives follow months-supply directly.

aUSEXPP.meaning: Export prices, all commodities — BLS monthly.
aUSEXPP.how_to_use: Reflects US producer pricing power abroad. Combined with import prices gives terms-of-trade signal.

aUSEXPPNAG.meaning: Export prices, nonagricultural commodities — strips out volatile food/farm exports.
aUSEXPPNAG.how_to_use: Better signal of manufactured-goods pricing. Cleaner trend than the headline.

aUSEXPAR.how_to_use: Released ~mid-month. Early read on global demand for US goods. Exports prices YoY ≈ goods exports inflation.

aUSIMPP.how_to_use: Direct inflation pass-through to consumer prices. Crude oil moves are the dominant driver historically.

aUSIMPPXPT.description: Import Prices, All imports excluding petroleum
aUSIMPPXPT.meaning: Import prices excluding petroleum — strips out the biggest source of volatility.
aUSIMPPXPT.how_to_use: Cleaner core-import-inflation measure. Pair with USD trade-weighted to identify FX vs underlying global price drivers.

aUSIMPAR.how_to_use: Released alongside export prices. Direct CPI input — feeds goods inflation 1-2 months out.

aUSCEXIPF.description: Export Prices, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCEXIPF.how_to_use: Quarterly aggregation of monthly. Use for cross-country comparison via OECD framework.

aUSCEXIYF.description: Export Prices, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCEXIYF.meaning: Export Prices, year-over-year change (standardized) — pace of US export-price change. Reflects US producer pricing power abroad and currency effects.
aUSCEXIYF.how_to_use: Track alongside import prices for terms-of-trade signal. When export prices rise faster than import prices, terms of trade improve (US gets more imports per export). Currency-driven mostly: dollar strength compresses export prices in dollar terms.

aUSCEXIF/C.meaning: Export Prices, standardized index — companion to aUSEXPP at standardized framing for international comparison.
aUSCEXIF/C.how_to_use: Use for cross-country export-price comparisons. Domestic analysts use aUSEXPP. Standardization aligns with IMF/OECD cross-border statistics conventions.

aUSCIMIPF.description: Import Prices, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCIMIPF.how_to_use: Quarterly version. Pairs with export QoQ for terms-of-trade.

aUSCIMIYF.description: Import Prices, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCIMIYF.how_to_use: Pass-through to CPI is highest in goods categories; services CPI mostly domestic.

aUSCIMIF/C.meaning: Import Prices, standardized index — companion to aUSIMPP at standardized framing.
aUSCIMIF/C.how_to_use: Direct CPI input — feeds goods inflation. Crude oil moves are biggest single driver. Watch alongside dollar (DXY) for currency-pass-through to consumer prices.

aUSCTRMPF.description: Terms of Trade, % quarter on quarter, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCTRMPF.meaning: Terms-of-trade QoQ change — export prices / import prices.
aUSCTRMPF.how_to_use: Improving (rising) ToT = country gets more imports per unit of exports = real income transfer in.

aUSCTRMYF.description: Terms of Trade, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCTRMYF.how_to_use: Big oil price moves swing ToT for net importers/exporters. US flipped to net energy exporter, so oil shocks now help ToT.

aUSCTRMF/C.meaning: Terms of Trade, standardized — ratio of export prices to import prices. Measures how much imports a country gets per unit of export.
aUSCTRMF/C.how_to_use: Improving terms of trade = country gets more for less = real-income gain. US terms of trade improved post-shale (energy import collapse) but worsened during commodity-import surges. Watch for major shifts as macro-cycle signals.

aUSTOTPRCF/C.how_to_use: Long history version. Useful for showing decade-scale ToT trends.

aUSGBALBA.meaning: Advance Goods Trade Balance — preliminary monthly goods-only deficit.
aUSGBALBA.how_to_use: Released ~3 days before the full BEA trade report. Goods-only (services excluded). Big surprises move the dollar at release.

aUSEXPAUTO/A.how_to_use: Largest categories: capital goods, services (financial, IP, travel), industrial supplies. Services exports persistently surplus. Strong USD compresses receipts in local-currency-equivalent terms.

aUSEXPCAP/CA.how_to_use: Largest categories: capital goods, services (financial, IP, travel), industrial supplies. Services exports persistently surplus. Strong USD compresses receipts in local-currency-equivalent terms.

aUSEX2CACB/A.how_to_use: Largest categories: capital goods, services (financial, IP, travel), industrial supplies. Services exports persistently surplus. Strong USD compresses receipts in local-currency-equivalent terms.

aUSEX2EAPB/A.how_to_use: Largest categories: capital goods, services (financial, IP, travel), industrial supplies. Services exports persistently surplus. Strong USD compresses receipts in local-currency-equivalent terms.

aUSEX2OIMB/A.description: Exports, Capital goods, Industrial machines, other

aUSSSINF.how_to_use: Tracks digital-economy revenues. Use as a proxy for software/cloud and telecom demand alongside earnings prints. Volatile QoQ — smooth with 4Q averages.

aUSFEDAW.description: Policy Rates, Fed Funds Eff Rate
aUSFEDAW.meaning: Fed Funds Effective Rate — weekly average. Sister of aUSFEDFUND with weekly granularity.
aUSFEDAW.how_to_use: Use the daily effective rate for trading; this for averaged trend.

aUSDISWPCRM.meaning: Discount Window Primary Credit Rate — what banks pay for short-term Fed liquidity through the discount window. Set 0.50pp ABOVE the upper bound of fed funds target.
aUSDISWPCRM.how_to_use: Stigma rate; rarely used. Heavily used during March 2023 banking stress (SVB / FRB). Bank Term Funding Program (BTFP) was the 2023-24 alternative facility before it expired.

aUSFEDFUND.meaning: Federal Funds Effective Rate — the volume-weighted median rate at which depository institutions lend reserves to each other overnight. Set by market activity within the FOMC's target range. The Fed's primary policy lever.
aUSFEDFUND.how_to_use: Anchor for the entire US yield curve. Compare to (a) Fed Funds Target range, (b) market-implied path from Fed Funds futures (CME FedWatch), (c) SOFR. Real fed funds = nominal − expected inflation; positive and rising = restrictive policy.

aUSIORAR.meaning: Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB, formerly IOER) — the rate the Fed pays banks on reserves held at the Fed. Floor of the fed funds corridor for banks.
aUSIORAR.how_to_use: Banks won't lend in fed funds market below IORB (would just park reserves at Fed instead). Set 5-15bp below the upper bound of fed funds target range. ~$3T of bank reserves earn this rate.

aUSDISWPCR.description: Policy Rates, Discount Window Primary Credit Rate
aUSDISWPCR.meaning: Discount Window Primary Credit Rate — Fed's emergency lending rate to depository institutions. Primary credit is set ~50bps above top of fed funds target range.
aUSDISWPCR.how_to_use: Used in stress periods (SVB Mar 2023 saw $150B borrowing). Above-market rate by design — penalty rate for using emergency facility. Watch alongside Bank Term Funding Program (BTFP) usage for full Fed-emergency-lending picture.

aUSDISWSACR.description: Policy Rates, Discount Window Seasonal Credit Rate
aUSDISWSACR.meaning: Discount Window Seasonal Credit Rate — Fed lending rate for small banks with seasonal funding needs (agricultural areas, resort areas). Rarely used.
aUSDISWSACR.how_to_use: Niche facility — relevant only for small community banks with predictable seasonal liquidity gaps. Less than $1B in typical usage. Track only for completeness.

aUSDISWSCCR.description: Policy Rates, Discount Window Secondary Credit Rate
aUSDISWSCCR.meaning: Discount Window secondary credit rate — for less-sound banks. 0.50pp above primary.
aUSDISWSCCR.how_to_use: Higher-stigma rate. Use is rare and typically signals stress at the borrower.

aUSFEDFUNDT.description: Policy Rates, Fed Funds Target Rate, Daily, Federal Reserve, United States
aUSFEDFUNDT.meaning: Fed Funds Target Rate — the policy-set range (technically a range; we report the midpoint). What the FOMC actually decides at each meeting.
aUSFEDFUNDT.how_to_use: Effective rate (aUSFEDFUND) trades within this range. Watch FOMC meeting decisions vs Fed Funds futures (CME FedWatch) for surprise risk. The dot plot shows individual FOMC members' projections of where this should be.

aUSRRPAR.meaning: Overnight Reverse Repo Rate (ON RRP) — sister rate to IORB but for non-bank money funds. Floor of the corridor for money market funds, GSEs, primary dealers.
aUSRRPAR.how_to_use: Set 10bp below IORB. RRP usage drops as Fed shrinks balance sheet via QT — fewer excess reserves chasing yield. RRP balances peaked ~$2.5T in 2022 and drained to <$200B in 2024.

aUSMBK.description: Prime Rates, Major Banks, Daily, Federal Reserve, United States
aUSMBK.meaning: Prime rate at major banks — daily.
aUSMBK.how_to_use: Anchored at fed funds target + 3.0pp historically. Not market-determined; admin-set by banks.

aUSMBKAVG.description: Prime Rates, Major Banks, Monthly, Federal Reserve, United States
aUSMBKAVG.meaning: Prime rate, major banks (monthly Fed average) — the rate large banks charge their best corporate customers. Conventionally set at fed funds top + 300bps.
aUSMBKAVG.how_to_use: Floor for credit-card APRs (typically prime + margin) and small-business lending. Currently fed funds + 300bps; revised by major banks within 24 hours of FOMC moves. Tracks fed-funds path closely.

aUSPRIME.meaning: Bank Prime Rate — admin-set lending rate for top-tier corporate borrowers, anchored at fed funds + 3.0pp. Reference rate for HELOCs, credit cards, and many small business loans.
aUSPRIME.how_to_use: Not market-determined — banks set it together. Moves in lockstep with fed funds target. Used as the variable-rate index for many household loans (HELOCs, small business loans).

aUSFEDFUNDP.description: Policy Rates, Fed Funds Target Rate, Monthly, LSEG
aUSFEDFUNDP.meaning: Fed Funds Target Rate — monthly average. LSEG-sourced.
aUSFEDFUNDP.how_to_use: Use whichever (aUSFEDFUNDT vs aUSFEDFUNDP) has fresher data.

aUSMBAMLR.description: Mortgage Lending Rates, FRM 30-Year Contract Rate (MBA Sourced)
aUSMBAMLR.meaning: 30-Year Fixed Mortgage Contract Rate — MBA weekly survey. The household-relevant US borrowing cost.
aUSMBAMLR.how_to_use: Spread to 10Y Treasury (typically 150-200bp; widens during housing/MBS stress) is the closely-watched MBS-spread gauge. Drives housing affordability and turnover. Each 100bp increase reduces purchasing power ~10%.

aUSFOMCA.description: Policy Rates, Fed Funds Target Rate, Daily, Reuters
aUSFOMCA.meaning: Fed Funds Target Rate, daily — the actual FOMC-set policy-rate target (top end of range since Dec 2008). Released Reuters daily snapshot.
aUSFOMCA.how_to_use: The policy-rate decision itself. Markets watch FOMC meeting outcomes (8 per year) for changes. Currently 4.25-4.50% (Nov 2025); peak 5.25-5.50% (Jul 2023-Sep 2024); zero-bound 0-0.25% (2008-15, 2020-22).

aUSFFTRR.description: Policy Rates, Fed Funds Target Rate, Announcement Date
aUSFFTRR.meaning: Fed Funds Target Rate — at FOMC announcement dates.
aUSFFTRR.how_to_use: Snapshot at each FOMC meeting (8/year). Useful for plotting policy rate trajectory by decision.

aUSMGAR.description: Mortgage Lending Rates, MBA 30-Yr Mortgage Rate
aUSMGAR.meaning: MBA 30-Year Mortgage Rate — weekly survey of 30-year fixed-rate conforming mortgage average. Released Wednesdays by Mortgage Bankers Association.
aUSMGAR.how_to_use: The most-watched mortgage rate. Higher-frequency than Freddie Mac PMMS (also weekly but Thursday). Spreads over 10Y Treasury (~250-300bps) have widened post-2022 as MBS prepayment expectations shifted. Falls drive refinance applications (track MBA refi index).

aUSCRCUYRA.description: Foreign currency reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCRCUYRA.meaning: Foreign currency reserves YoY % change, standardized.
aUSCRCUYRA.how_to_use: Most useful for cross-country comparison. US reserves are tiny relative to GDP because USD is reserve currency — focus on the trend, not the level.

aUSCRESPA.description: Official international reserves, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCRESPA.meaning: Official international reserves MoM % change, standardized.
aUSCRESPA.how_to_use: Watch for unusual swings — large MoM moves can signal FX intervention or valuation effects from gold/SDR repricing.

aUSCRESYA.description: Official international reserves, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCRESYA.meaning: Official international reserves YoY % change, standardized.
aUSCRESYA.how_to_use: Cleaner trend signal than MoM. US reserves grow mostly through gold revaluation and IMF position changes; FX trading is rare.

aUSCRESA.how_to_use: Sum of FX, gold, SDR, IMF reserve position. Used for FX intervention capacity (rarely deployed for the US).

aUSRES.meaning: Reserve Assets (total) — US international reserves: gold, foreign currency holdings, IMF position, SDRs. ~$700B total.
aUSRES.how_to_use: Small relative to US GDP (~3%) — US is reserve issuer, not reserve holder. Track for FX intervention capacity (rarely used post-1985). ~80% of total is gold (revaluation gain over decades).

aUSRAFXCH.meaning: Foreign currency component of reserve assets — euros, yen, gold-backed.
aUSRAFXCH.how_to_use: Smallest piece of US reserves. Big country FX reserves are mostly USD; the US holds mostly gold.

aUSRESGLD.meaning: Gold stock component of reserve assets, valued at official rate (~$42/oz historically — way below market).
aUSRESGLD.how_to_use: The US holds ~8,100 tonnes — largest in the world. Valued at the legacy book price, vastly understated. Market value is 30x+ book.

aUSRESSDR.description: Reserve Assets, Holdings of Special Drawing Rights
aUSRESSDR.meaning: Holdings of Special Drawing Rights at the IMF.
aUSRESSDR.how_to_use: SDRs are an IMF reserve unit. US allocation grew sharply in the 2021 SDR allocation post-COVID.

aUSRESIMF.description: Reserve Assets, Reserve position in IMF
aUSRESIMF.meaning: US reserve position in IMF — quota subscription minus IMF holdings of US currency.
aUSRESIMF.how_to_use: Mostly accounting. Moves when the US lends to IMF programs or its quota changes.

aUSFXRESA.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: Total Assets — same conceptual measure as aUSRES. Treasury monthly release.
aUSFXRESA.how_to_use: Cross-check against aUSRES. The US holds reserves only minimally — most reserve-currency-issuer status means foreign central banks hold dollars instead.

aUSRESGLDA.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: Gold — Treasury's gold holdings (~261M troy oz / ~8,134 metric tons). Largest national gold holding globally. Valued at ~$42/oz on books but market value far higher.
aUSRESGLDA.how_to_use: Stock unchanged since 1970s. Book value uses 1973 statutory price ($42/oz); market value 50× higher. Recent gold rally has put 'unrealized' gains on US balance sheet at trillions — periodically discussed for revaluation.

aUSRESIMFIRA.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: IMF Position — US reserve tranche position at the IMF. Funds the US can withdraw on demand from IMF without conditions.
aUSRESIMFIRA.how_to_use: Small (~$50B). Used in BoP accounting; rarely activated. Tracks IMF financial commitments.

aUSRVSSDRA.meaning: US Foreign Reserves: Special Drawing Rights — SDR holdings at the IMF. International reserve asset created by IMF, valued by basket of major currencies.
aUSRVSSDRA.how_to_use: Boosted in 2021 IMF general allocation ($650B globally to support COVID recovery). Useful for tracking IMF reserve operations. Less liquid than Treasury foreign currency holdings.

aUSFCBOUT.description: Economic Forecasts, CBO, Budget projection, outlays
aUSFCBOUT.meaning: Congressional Budget Office baseline projection for federal outlays. Assumes current law (no policy changes). Released in CBO Budget and Economic Outlook (Jan + August updates).
aUSFCBOUT.how_to_use: Reference for fiscal-cliff debates and long-run sustainability framing. Compare to actual outlays (aUSFOUTL) for forecast accuracy. CBO projections are typically conservative on revenue, accurate on outlays.

aUSFCBREV.description: Economic Forecasts, CBO, Budget projection, revenues
aUSFCBREV.meaning: CBO baseline projection for federal receipts. Current-law forecast.
aUSFCBREV.how_to_use: CBO consistently UNDER-estimates revenue during expansions, OVER-estimates during downturns (revenue is more cyclical than they capture). Compare to aUSFEDREC.

aUSFCNAISQ.description: Economic Forecasts, CBO, Natural Rate of Unemployment (NAIRU) Short Term
aUSFCNAISQ.meaning: CBO baseline projection — current-law forecast for a US fiscal or macroeconomic line.
aUSFCNAISQ.how_to_use: Congressional Budget Office baseline — assumes current law. Reference for fiscal-cliff debates and long-run sustainability framing. Updated semi-annually; alternative scenarios published alongside.

aUSFCNAIRQ.description: Economic Forecasts, CBO, Noncyclical Rate of Unemployment
aUSFCNAIRQ.meaning: CBO baseline projection — current-law forecast for a US fiscal or macroeconomic line.
aUSFCNAIRQ.how_to_use: Congressional Budget Office baseline — assumes current law. Reference for fiscal-cliff debates and long-run sustainability framing. Updated semi-annually; alternative scenarios published alongside.

aUSFCCUFHR.meaning: Fed Summary of Economic Projections — Unemployment Rate central tendency, high range. Quarterly SEP released after FOMC meetings (March, June, September, December).
aUSFCCUFHR.how_to_use: Compare to actual UR (aUSUNTOTR) for Fed forecast track record. Fed UR forecasts have under-estimated rises (every cycle).

aUSFCCUFLR.description: Economic Forecasts, Federal Reserve, Central Tendency, Unemployment rate projection, 1st year from posted quarter, Low
aUSFCCUFLR.meaning: Forecast of the US civilian unemployment rate from official or consensus sources (central region).
aUSFCCUFLR.how_to_use: From the BLS household survey, released alongside NFP. Pair with participation rate: a falling unemployment rate driven by exits (not hires) is weak. Crossing the Sahm Rule threshold (3-mo avg up 0.5pp from trailing-12m low) historically signals recession.

aUSFCMURFR.how_to_use: From the BLS household survey, released alongside NFP. Pair with participation rate: a falling unemployment rate driven by exits (not hires) is weak. Crossing the Sahm Rule threshold (3-mo avg up 0.5pp from trailing-12m low) historically signals recession.

aUSFCRCFHR.description: Economic Forecasts, Federal Reserve, Range, Core PCE inflation projection, 1st year from posted quarter, High
aUSFCRCFHR.meaning: Forecast of the Core PCE price index (ex food and energy) from official or consensus sources.
aUSFCRCFHR.how_to_use: THE Fed inflation series. The 6-month annualized core PCE is what FOMC commentary typically references. Released ~2 weeks after CPI with the BEA Personal Income & Outlays report. Lower than CPI because of basket weighting (less shelter weight) and chain-weighting.

aUSFCRUFHR.description: Economic Forecasts, Federal Reserve, Range, Unemployment rate projection, 1st year from posted quarter, High
aUSFCRUFHR.meaning: Forecast of the US civilian unemployment rate from official or consensus sources.

aUSCMS0B/A.meaning: M0 / Monetary Base — currency in circulation + bank reserves at Fed. The Fed's direct liquidity injection.
aUSCMS0B/A.how_to_use: QE expanded the base 5x post-2008. Now shrinking via QT. Loose proxy for Fed balance sheet liquidity. Reserves portion specifically determines money market dynamics (RRP, fed funds market activity).

aUSCMS0PB/A.description: Money Supply M0, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCMS0PB/A.how_to_use: Volatile during balance-sheet operations. Less informative than YoY.

aUSCMS0YB/A.description: Money Supply M0, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCMS0YB/A.how_to_use: Useful long-run liquidity-cycle gauge. Negative growth = active QT.

aUSCMS1B/A.meaning: M1 Money Supply — currency + checking deposits + traveler's checks. Pre-2020 definition.
aUSCMS1B/A.how_to_use: Definition expanded in May 2020 to INCLUDE savings deposits — the level jumped artificially. Pre-2020 M1 series not directly comparable to post-2020. Use M2 for cleaner historical analysis.

aUSCMS1PB/A.description: Money Supply M1, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCMS1PB/A.meaning: Money Supply M1 standardized, MoM percent change — monthly growth rate of M1 (currency + demand deposits + savings deposits post-2020 reclassification).
aUSCMS1PB/A.how_to_use: Highly volatile post-2020 due to M1 reclassification. Watch year-over-year (aUSCMS1YB/A) for trend. Sustained negative monthly readings rare but happened in 2022-23 during QT.

aUSCMS1YB/A.description: Money Supply M1, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCMS1YB/A.how_to_use: Cross-check M1 vs M2 growth — divergence reveals whether liquidity is in transactional vs savings accounts.

aUSCMS2PB/A.description: Money Supply M2, % month on month, Standardized, Chg P/P
aUSCMS2PB/A.meaning: Money Supply M2, MoM percent change — monthly growth rate of broad M2 aggregate. The most-watched money-supply growth signal.
aUSCMS2PB/A.how_to_use: Watch for sustained MoM contractions as monetary-tightening signals. 2022-23 saw rare M2 contractions during QT — contributed to disinflation. Compare to nominal GDP for velocity-implied trend.

aUSCMS2YB/A.description: Money Supply M2, % year on year, Standardized, Chg Y/Y
aUSCMS2YB/A.meaning: M2 YoY % change — the most-watched money supply growth rate.
aUSCMS2YB/A.how_to_use: Loose proxy for inflation 12-18 months out (monetarist view; weak in practice). Surged to 27% in 2021 post-stimulus, contracted in 2023. Sustained negative M2 growth historically associated with recession.

aUSCMS2B/A.meaning: M2 Money Supply level, standardized — M1 + small time deposits + retail money funds. The broadest practical money supply measure.
aUSCMS2B/A.how_to_use: M3 was discontinued in 2006. M2 surged 27% YoY in 2021 post-stimulus, contracted in 2023 (first sustained negative since 1930s). Watch nominal growth rate vs nominal GDP growth.

aUSRESERVB/A.meaning: Adjusted reserves — bank reserves at the Fed, adjusted for changes in reserve requirements.
aUSRESERVB/A.how_to_use: Matters for the federal funds market. Reserves abundance reduces fed funds market activity (since 2008).

aUSADMBAS.1D/A.meaning: Adjusted monetary base — Fed's preferred monetary-base measure adjusted for changes in reserve requirements and required-reserve ratio shifts. Most consistent across regulatory regimes.
aUSADMBAS.1D/A.how_to_use: Cleaner than the raw monetary base for long-time-series comparisons. Post-2008 the distinction matters less because reserve requirements were eliminated in 2020. Track for Fed balance-sheet trajectory.

aUSMEMSVE/A.meaning: M2 velocity — nominal GDP divided by M2 money stock. Measures how often each dollar circulates per year in nominal output.
aUSMEMSVE/A.how_to_use: Post-2008 collapsed from ~2.0 to ~1.1 as M2 expanded faster than nominal GDP. A revival of velocity is a pre-condition for sustained inflation: more money + same velocity = inflation; more money + falling velocity = deflation pressure.

aUSGOCBN.description: H.6, U.S. government deposits, total cash balance
aUSGOCBN.meaning: H.6 — US government deposits, Treasury General Account (TGA) at Fed.
aUSGOCBN.how_to_use: TGA is a major liquidity siphon. When Treasury rebuilds TGA after a debt-ceiling deal, bank reserves drain — funding stress risk.

aUSMAAAAAA.meaning: Monetary base (Fed H.3 release) — currency in circulation plus bank reserves at the Fed. Direct Fed liability; expands with QE, contracts with QT. Distinct from broader money aggregates.
aUSMAAAAAA.how_to_use: Misleading as a 'money supply' indicator post-2008 because reserves became huge but velocity collapsed (banks held them rather than lend). Useful for tracking Fed balance-sheet operations directly. Compare to M2 for the bank-lending multiplier.

aUSMZMSTK/A.meaning: MZM (Money of Zero Maturity) money stock — all money instantly convertible to cash without penalty. Effectively M2 minus small time deposits plus all institutional money funds.
aUSMZMSTK/A.how_to_use: Less commonly tracked since the Fed discontinued its publication; private compilations remain. Some monetarists consider MZM more economically meaningful than M2 because time deposits are illiquid for transactional purposes.

aUSM1/A.meaning: M1 money supply (annual aggregate) — companion to monthly aUSM1 at lower frequency. Same conceptual measure.
aUSM1/A.how_to_use: Use monthly aUSM1 for high-frequency tracking. Annual aggregate useful for long-time-series analysis. Post-2020 M1 includes savings deposits — the M1 vs M2 distinction is now blurred.

aUSM1.meaning: M1 money supply — currency in circulation + demand deposits + savings deposits (post-May 2020 reclassification, which made M1 ≈ M2 minus small time deposits and money-market mutual funds).
aUSM1.how_to_use: Post-2020 the M1 vs M2 distinction blurred — savings deposits were moved from M2 into M1. Watch M2 instead for the meaningful aggregate. M1 still useful for tracking high-liquidity household balances; spikes during stress (cash hoarding) and post-stimulus.

aUSM1W/A.meaning: M1 money supply, weekly — Fed H.6 release at weekly frequency. Smoother than monthly because it's a weekly average.
aUSM1W/A.how_to_use: Track for high-frequency M1 movements. Useful for spotting sudden shifts in liquidity preference (cash hoarding, deposit flight). Pair with weekly M2 (aUSM2W) for full picture.

aUSM1W.meaning: M1 money supply, weekly (alternate release) — same conceptual measure as aUSM1W/A.
aUSM1W.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever is fresher.

aUSM2/A.meaning: M2 money supply (annual aggregate) — companion to monthly aUSM2 at lower frequency.
aUSM2/A.how_to_use: Use monthly aUSM2 for high-frequency tracking. Annual aggregate useful for long-time-series analysis.

aUSM2.meaning: M2 money supply — M1 + small time deposits + retail money-market mutual funds. The broadest commonly-tracked monetary aggregate; includes most household liquid savings.
aUSM2.how_to_use: Year-over-year M2 growth is the key indicator. Sustained M2 contraction is rare — happened in 2022-23 for the first time in modern data, contributing to disinflation pressure. Fast M2 growth (>10% YoY like 2020) tends to precede inflation surges with 12-18mo lag.

aUSM2W/A.meaning: M2 money supply, weekly — Fed H.6 release at weekly frequency. Most-watched high-frequency money-supply gauge.
aUSM2W/A.how_to_use: Tracks broad money at weekly resolution. Useful for spotting policy-effect timing: M2 acceleration signals expansion phase; sustained contraction signals tightening pressure (rare, observed 2022-23).

aUSM2W.meaning: M2 money supply, weekly (alternate release) — same conceptual measure as aUSM2W/A.
aUSM2W.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever has fresher data.

aUSTTOPAS/A.description: Total Tourism-Related Output, Passenger air transportation
aUSTTOPAS/A.meaning: Total tourism-related output for passenger air transportation. BEA Travel & Tourism Satellite Accounts, annual.
aUSTTOPAS/A.how_to_use: Long-run tourism trend gauge. Combine with monthly TSA throughput for high-frequency cross-check. Sensitive to fuel costs and consumer discretionary.

aUSSTIND/A.description: Total sales of tourism Industries total
aUSSTIND/A.meaning: Total tourism industry sales — quarterly aggregate of all tourism-related sectors.
aUSSTIND/A.how_to_use: Headline tourism cycle gauge. Watch alongside leisure & hospitality payrolls (in employment_hours) and consumer confidence for the broader services consumer view.

aUSTOAIRT/A.description: Total sales of tourism Industries, passenger air transportation
aUSTOAIRT/A.meaning: Total sales of passenger air transportation within tourism industries — quarterly.
aUSTOAIRT/A.how_to_use: Most cyclical tourism sub-line. Compare against airline industry revenues (BTS) and the TSA throughput series for a real-time cross-check.

aUSTOTRACC/A.description: Total sales of tourism Industries, traveler accommodations
aUSTOTRACC/A.meaning: Total sales of traveler accommodations (hotels, motels, B&Bs) within tourism industries — quarterly.
aUSTOTRACC/A.how_to_use: Pair with RevPAR and occupancy rate from STR/CBRE for sector-level depth. Sensitive to business travel cycles, not just leisure.

aUSTRTTP.meaning: TSA airport security checkpoint throughput — count of passengers screened. Daily; aggregated monthly here.
aUSTRTTP.how_to_use: Highest-frequency travel demand indicator. Use as a real-time cross-check on tourism / leisure consumer spend. Compare YoY to control for seasonality.

aUSTRTH/A.meaning: TSA Checkpoint Traveler Throughput — same as aUSTRTTP, alternate series with adjustments.
aUSTRTH/A.how_to_use: Use whichever has cleaner recent prints. Watch the YoY % change for trend; the level is heavily seasonal.

aUSPCEAR.description: PCE price index- Actual, Chg P/P
aUSPCEAR.meaning: Headline PCE price index, month-over-month change. Released with BEA Personal Income & Outlays.
aUSPCEAR.how_to_use: Sister series to core PCE (aUSPCEMAR) — headline includes food and energy. The 6m annualized rate is what FOMC speakers reference. Spread to core tells you how much the headline number is being moved by energy/food.

aUSEBM10Y.description: 10Y Government bond yield as % per annum
aUSEBM10Y.meaning: 10-year US government bond yield. The benchmark long-rate for global risk pricing.
aUSEBM10Y.how_to_use: Single most-watched US bond price. Decompose into real yield (TIPS) + breakeven inflation. The 2s10s spread is the classic recession signal. Tracks Fed expectations + term premium.

aUSEPDAPG.description: Energy Prices, Diesel, average retail price per gallon, all areas
aUSEPDAPG.meaning: Average US retail diesel price, all areas. Weekly EIA series, monthly here.
aUSEPDAPG.how_to_use: Truck/freight cost proxy. Diesel diverges from gasoline due to refinery yield mix and global maritime demand (low-sulfur regs). Spike in diesel relative to gasoline often precedes goods CPI moves.

aUSEPGAPG.description: Energy Prices, Gasoline Regular, Average Retail Price per Gallon, All Areas
aUSEPGAPG.meaning: Average US retail regular gasoline price, all areas. Weekly EIA, monthly here.
aUSEPGAPG.how_to_use: Most consumer-visible price — moves consumer confidence almost in real time. Heavy contributor to headline CPI (~3-4% weight). Use 4-week change for sentiment read.

aUSGSPRA.description: Energy Prices, Gasoline Regular, Average Retail Price, All Areas
aUSGSPRA.meaning: Average retail price for regular gasoline, all US areas — alternate series matching aUSEPGAPG.
aUSGSPRA.how_to_use: Use whichever has cleaner data. The MoM change feeds directly into the energy component of headline CPI.

aUSEPHAPG.description: Energy Prices, Heating oil, average price per gallon, residential consumers, methobrk oct19
aUSEPHAPG.meaning: Average residential heating oil retail price, all US areas. Highly seasonal — concentrated in Northeast.
aUSEPHAPG.how_to_use: Winter heating-cost gauge. Less macro-relevant than gasoline (much smaller share of budgets) but politically sensitive in cold-weather years.

aUSCPICNFB/A.description: CORPORATE PROFITS WITH IVA & CCADJ - NONFINANCIAL (AR)
aUSCPICNFB/A.meaning: Nonfinancial corporate profits with inventory valuation and capital consumption adjustments — the cleanest cyclical profit measure in the NIPA accounts.
aUSCPICNFB/A.how_to_use: Leading indicator for capex and hiring. Diverges from S&P 500 EPS (which is global + financial-heavy); useful as a domestic real-economy profit gauge. Compare to nonfinancial output to track margin trends.

aUS15IDGN.meaning: Personal consumption of consumer durables by households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISH). Annual NIPA detail.
aUS15IDGN.how_to_use: Long-cycle gauge of durables stock formation (vehicles, furniture, appliances). Use the QoQ retail/durables prints for cycle timing; this annual line is for level/trend.

aUSRSAHMN/A.meaning: Real-Time Sahm Rule indicator: 3-month moving average of the unemployment rate, minus its trailing-12-month low. Triggers (signals recession) when ≥ 0.5pp.
aUSRSAHMN/A.how_to_use: Among the cleanest historical recession signals — has fired at the start of every US recession since 1970. A trigger doesn't make a recession inevitable, but flagging it warrants caution. Watch alongside NFP, claims, and yield curve.

aUSGPYDPOP.how_to_use: Used as denominator for per-capita real disposable income — core consumer spending power gauge.

aUSPC169P.how_to_use: Teen labor force participation has structural decline since 2000 (more in school). Use for labor-supply modeling.

aUSPC65T9P.how_to_use: Boomer wave. Drives Medicare enrollment growth + labor force participation patterns.

aUSPC70T4P.meaning: Civilian noninstitutional population, age 70-74 — household-survey reference population for the 70-74 age cohort.
aUSPC70T4P.how_to_use: Key demographic for retirement-spending and Medicare projections. The leading edge of the boomer wave passed through this bracket 2016-2021. Track alongside Social Security beneficiary count for fiscal projections.

aUSPC75AOP.how_to_use: Long-term care + Medicare-heavy cohort. Fastest-growing age group.

aUSZGVCOP.description: IFDI, Governance, Corporate Governance, Average Share of Independent Directors on the Board
aUSZGVCOP.meaning: IFDI corporate governance — Independent directors share.

aUSZGVSHP.description: IFDI, Governance, Other Governance, Scholars with SSB Memberships
aUSZGVSHP.meaning: IFDI scholars with SSB (Shariah Supervisory Board) memberships.

aUSZPGEDP.description: IFDI, Knowledge, Education, Institutions Offering Islamic Finance Degrees
aUSZPGEDP.meaning: IFDI institutions offering Islamic finance degrees in US.

aUSZKGRHP.description: IFDI, Knowledge, Research, Peer Reviewed & Journal Articles on Islamic Finance
aUSZKGRHP.meaning: IFDI peer-reviewed research articles on Islamic finance.

aUSDEATH.meaning: Weekly deaths, all ages — CDC NCHS provisional.
aUSDEATH.how_to_use: Excess mortality vs 2015-19 baseline is the cleanest pandemic + aging signal. Lagged 1-2 weeks.

aUSDTH14.description: Weekly deaths, Compared to average of the same week in years 2015-2019, 0-14 years, %
aUSDTH14.meaning: Weekly deaths, 0-14 years — vs 2015-19 weekly average.
aUSDTH14.how_to_use: Stable baseline; deviations signal pediatric public-health events (RSV waves, etc).

aUSDTH64.description: Weekly deaths, Compared to average of the same week in years 2015-2019, 15-64 years, %
aUSDTH64.how_to_use: Working-age excess mortality. Pandemic, opioid, and mental-health driven.

aUSDTH74.description: Weekly deaths, Compared to average of the same week in years 2015-2019, 65-74 years, %

aUSDTH84.description: Weekly deaths, Compared to average of the same week in years 2015-2019, 75-84 years, %

aUSDTHAL.description: Weekly deaths, Compared to average of the same week in years 2015-2019, All ages, %
aUSDTHAL.meaning: Weekly deaths, all ages — vs 2015-19 baseline.
aUSDTHAL.how_to_use: Lead pandemic / public-health signal. Returned to ~baseline post-2023.

aUSDTH85.description: Weekly deaths, Compared to average of the same week in years 2015-2019, over 85 years, %
aUSDTH85.how_to_use: Highest mortality cohort. Care facility outbreaks visible here first.

aUSDTHEX.description: Weekly deaths, Excess deaths compared to average of the same week in years 2015-2019, All ages
aUSDTHEX.meaning: EXCESS deaths vs 2015-19 weekly average — all causes, all ages.
aUSDTHEX.how_to_use: The single cleanest mortality cycle indicator. Captures pandemic deaths whether labeled COVID or not.

aUSDTHCV.how_to_use: Direct COVID mortality. Underestimates true COVID mortality (some go unrecorded). Use with excess deaths for comparison.

aUSPOP18Y.how_to_use: High-school cohort. Tracks education / labor-supply pipeline.

aUSPOP24Y.how_to_use: Entry-level workforce + college-age. Recent stagnation = labor-supply headwind.

aUSPOP39Y.how_to_use: Drives housing / family-services demand. Millennials hitting peak.

aUSPOP44Y.how_to_use: Peak-earnings cohort. Drives discretionary spending / capital-formation demand.

aUSPOP64Y.how_to_use: Drives 401k withdrawal patterns + early retirement decisions.

aUSPOPTO.how_to_use: Base for per-capita calculations. Growth slowing — 0.5%/yr now vs 1%+ historically.

aUSCCVKS.how_to_use: Historic pandemic series — case reporting wound down 2023.

aUSPCIHSLF/C.description: PPI,  hides, skins, leather & related products
aUSPCIHSLF/C.meaning: Level of the Producer Price Index — the BLS measure of average prices received by domestic producers.
aUSPCIHSLF/C.how_to_use: Leads CPI for goods inflation. Watch core PPI (ex food/energy/trade) for the cleanest underlying signal. Final-demand services PPI is the input to core PCE.
