aUSHCNFARM/A.description: Earnings, Hourly, Hourly compensation, nonfarm business
aUSHCNFARM/A.meaning: Hourly compensation, nonfarm business sector. Includes wages + benefits.
aUSHCNFARM/A.how_to_use: Pair with productivity to compute unit labor costs (= compensation / productivity). Rising hourly comp without productivity gains = inflationary.

aUSEHRRHCNF/A.description: Earnings, Hourly, Real hourly compensation, business, nonfarm
aUSEHRRHCNF/A.meaning: REAL hourly compensation, nonfarm business — inflation-adjusted.
aUSEHRRHCNF/A.how_to_use: True purchasing-power gauge. Stagnant for decades; recent surge largely deflation rather than nominal growth.

aUSEMPBQA.description: Labour Cost, Employment Benefits QQ - Acutal, Chg P/P
aUSEMPBQA.how_to_use: Benefits inflation (mostly health insurance, retirement) is stickier than wages.

aUSEMPWAQ.description: Labour Cost, Employment Wages QQ, Chg P/P
aUSEMPWAQ.how_to_use: Cleaner wage signal than aggregate compensation. Pair with ECI total.

aUSEMPCIW/A.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, benefit costs
aUSEMPCIW/A.meaning: Employment Cost Index, benefit costs component.
aUSEMPCIW/A.how_to_use: Health insurance + retirement contributions. Not as sticky as wage component but harder to reduce.

aUSEMPCI/A.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, total compensation
aUSEMPCI/A.meaning: Employment Cost Index, total compensation — wages + benefits.
aUSEMPCI/A.how_to_use: Fed's preferred wage gauge: includes benefits, controls for industry/occupation mix. Quarterly. >4% YoY is too high for 2% inflation target.

aUSEMPCAR.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, total compensation, Chg P/P
aUSEMPCAR.how_to_use: Most market-relevant ECI series. Released on Fed black-out weeks; cleanest wage signal.

aUSEMPCIP/A.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, total compensation, private ind, service-producing
aUSEMPCIP/A.meaning: Employment Cost Index, total compensation (alternate framing) — companion series to aUSEMPCI/A. Quarterly BLS release.
aUSEMPCIP/A.how_to_use: Cross-check against aUSEMPCI/A. ECI is the Fed's preferred wage-pressure gauge over AHE because it controls for compositional shifts. Released Tue of NFP week — Fed pays close attention.

aUSECWNS/A.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, wages and salaries
aUSECWNS/A.meaning: ECI wages and salaries — strips out benefits.
aUSECWNS/A.how_to_use: Pure wage gauge. AHE (in employment_hours) is monthly/noisier; ECI is quarterly/cleaner.

aUSEMPCIB/A.description: Labour Cost, Employment cost index, wages and salaries, private industry
aUSEMPCIB/A.meaning: ECI wages and salaries, private industry.
aUSEMPCIB/A.how_to_use: Strip out government wages (which lag and are policy-driven).

aUSLCPAPG.how_to_use: Watch the revisions; preliminary often gets revised meaningfully.

aUSULC/A.meaning: Unit Labor Costs, business sector. ULC = compensation / productivity.
aUSULC/A.how_to_use: Most useful labor-cost-driven inflation signal. ULC growth > productivity growth = wage-push inflation. Watch the 4-quarter change.

aUSLCOSTE/CA.meaning: Unit labor costs, business sector (index form) — labor cost per unit of output. Productivity-adjusted wage measure.
aUSLCOSTE/CA.how_to_use: ULC = compensation per hour ÷ output per hour. Sustained ULC growth above ~2% inconsistent with 2% inflation absent productivity gains. The Fed's go-to wage-inflation gauge alongside ECI.

aUSLCRAPG.meaning: Unit labor cost growth, business nonfarm — pace of unit-labor-cost change. Productivity-adjusted wage-pressure indicator.
aUSLCRAPG.how_to_use: Annualized growth rate. Above 4% sustained = wage-driven inflation pressure; below 2% = wage costs not inflationary. The Fed cites this in monetary-policy decisions.

aUSULCNF/A.how_to_use: Cleanest ULC measure (nonfarm strips out volatile farm sector). The Fed inflation hawks watch this directly.

aUSULCNBSE/CA.description: Labour Cost, Unit, business, nonfarm, index
aUSULCNBSE/CA.meaning: Unit labor costs, business nonfarm sector (index form) — same as aUSULCNF/A but in standardized index format for international comparison.
aUSULCNBSE/CA.how_to_use: Cleanest international-comparison ULC measure. Use for cross-country competitiveness analysis. Domestic analysts use aUSULCNF/A.

aUSPRODNFRM/A.description: Labour Productivity, Hours of all persons, business, nonfarm
aUSPRODNFRM/A.meaning: Hours of all persons, nonfarm business — total hours worked.
aUSPRODNFRM/A.how_to_use: Denominator for productivity. Pair with output for productivity computation.

aUSPHOPBUS/A.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, business, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor
aUSPHOPBUS/A.meaning: Output per hour, business sector — productivity.
aUSPHOPBUS/A.how_to_use: Headline productivity gauge. Trend ~1.5%/yr; 2010s averaged below trend; AI may lift trend forward.

aUSPRODPH/A.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, business, Volume Index, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of Labor
aUSPRODPH/A.meaning: Output per hour of all persons, business sector — broad productivity gauge. The headline productivity number cited in BLS releases.
aUSPRODPH/A.how_to_use: Trend ~1.5%/year; 2010s averaged sub-trend; 2024-25 showing recovery toward 2%. Most economically meaningful productivity measure. Trend matters more than quarterly: smooth with 4Q averages.

aUSPRODVTQ/CA.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, business, index
aUSPRODVTQ/CA.meaning: Output per hour of all persons, business sector, QoQ change — quarterly productivity-growth pace.
aUSPRODVTQ/CA.how_to_use: Highly volatile quarterly. Smooth with 4Q averages for trend. The Fed cares about trend productivity for its implications for wage-inflation tolerance: high productivity allows higher wage growth without inflation.

aUSPHOPMFG/A.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, manufacturing
aUSPHOPMFG/A.how_to_use: Manufacturing productivity has historically grown faster than services. Slowed materially since 2010.

aUSPRORAPG.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, nonfarm business
aUSPRORAPG.meaning: Output per hour, nonfarm business — preliminary.

aUSOUTNF/A.description: Labour Productivity, Output per hour of all persons, nonfarm business
aUSOUTNF/A.how_to_use: Strips out volatile farm sector. Fed's preferred productivity gauge.

aUSBUPRNF/A.how_to_use: Numerator for nonfarm productivity. Output growth ≈ productivity growth + hours growth.

aUSNFPRAR.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Reuters
aUSNFPRAR.meaning: Series mislabeled in source as 'foreign exchange reserves' — actually nonfarm productivity/labor costs related.
aUSNFPRAR.how_to_use: Cross-section / drill-down series; verify source before using.

aUSLCTSAR.description: Foreign exchange reserves - BMO, Productivity & Labor Costs, Quarterly, Reuters
aUSLCTSAR.meaning: Series mislabeled in source as 'foreign exchange reserves' — actually labor costs related.
aUSLCTSAR.how_to_use: Cross-section / drill-down series; verify source before using.

aUSCRETF/C.meaning: Retail sales, standardized — broad measure of consumer goods spending at retail outlets. Captures ~1/3 of consumer expenditure (goods only; services tracked elsewhere).
aUSCRETF/C.how_to_use: Watch the 'control group' (ex autos, gasoline, building materials, food services) — that feeds directly into PCE goods. Volatile month-to-month; smooth with 3M average. Real retail sales (deflated by CPI) is a better cyclical gauge than nominal.

aUSCRETE/CA.meaning: Retail Sales, standardized — OECD-comparable framing of total US retail sales. Conceptually similar to aUSRSLSFS/A but with international harmonization.
aUSCRETE/CA.how_to_use: Use for cross-country retail comparisons. Domestic analysts use aUSRSLSFS/A or aUSRLCOA. The standardization mostly affects category mapping (e.g., what counts as 'food retail').

aUSCRETPE/A.how_to_use: Monthly retail-sales print MoM. Big surprise vs consensus moves USD/equities.

aUSCRETPF.meaning: Retail Sales, standardized, MoM percent change — month-over-month growth rate of standardized retail sales total.
aUSCRETPF.how_to_use: Monthly retail-sales pulse. Decompose into volatile categories (autos, gas) vs control group for cleaner consumer-demand read. >0.5% MoM hot, <0% cool. Watch for revisions: prior month often revised by ±0.2pp.

aUSCRETYE/A.how_to_use: Trend signal. >5% YoY healthy; sub-2% signals weak consumer.

aUSCRETYF.meaning: Retail Sales, standardized, YoY percent change — year-over-year growth rate. Smoother than MoM, better for trend identification.
aUSCRETYF.how_to_use: >5% YoY growth = healthy consumer; <2% = weak; negative = recession territory. Strip out auto/gas YoY share for the underlying consumer-demand signal. Compare to PCE (broader consumption measure) and consumer credit growth.

aUSRBSIY.description: Chain Store Sales, Johnson Redbook Index, yoy% index
aUSRBSIY.meaning: Johnson Redbook chain-store sales index, YoY — weekly chain-store sales tracker covering ~9,000 stores across major retailers (Walmart, Target, dollar stores, etc.).
aUSRBSIY.how_to_use: Highest-frequency retail signal — released Tuesdays for the prior week. Volatile but useful for spotting demand shifts before official monthly retail report. Holiday-season weeks (Black Friday, December) are most-watched.

aUSRBSIM.description: Chain Store Sales, Johnson Redbook Index, mom% index, Suspended
aUSRBSIM.meaning: Johnson Redbook chain-store sales, MoM — month-over-month change in weekly Redbook tracker. Rolled-up monthly aggregate.
aUSRBSIM.how_to_use: Pair with YoY for trend. Diverges from official retail-sales report when sample mix shifts (Redbook over-weights big-box and discount). Useful for early monthly-print directional signal.

aUSRSLYQA.description: Retail Sales YoY - Acutal, Chg Y/Y

aUSRSLSBMAT/A.description: Retail Sales, Building materials, garden equipment and supplies dealers
aUSRSLSBMAT/A.meaning: Retail Sales: building materials, garden equipment, supplies dealers — Home Depot/Lowe's/local-hardware-store sales. ~7% of total retail.
aUSRSLSBMAT/A.how_to_use: Highly cyclical with housing — driven by remodeling and DIY activity. Falls in housing-affordability stress (2022-23) when home transactions slow. Watch alongside existing home sales (most remodeling follows home-purchase by 6-12 months).

aUSRSLSCL/A.description: Retail Sales, Clothing and clothing accessories stores
aUSRSLSCL/A.how_to_use: Discretionary signal. First to soften when consumers pull back.

aUSRSLSDPS/A.description: Retail Sales, Department stores (excluding leased departments)
aUSRSLSDPS/A.how_to_use: Long-term decline category — losing share to e-commerce + general merchandise.

aUSRSLSEC.meaning: Retail sales, e-commerce. Quarterly Census release.
aUSRSLSEC.how_to_use: Online share tracking. ~16% of retail and rising. Use the share, not absolute level.

aUSRSLSAPP/A.description: Retail Sales, Electronics and appliance stores
aUSRSLSAPP/A.meaning: Retail sales, electronics and appliance stores.
aUSRSLSAPP/A.how_to_use: Big-ticket discretionary; cycles with housing and credit availability.

aUSRSLSFB/A.description: Retail Sales, Food and beverage stores
aUSRSLSFB/A.meaning: Retail sales, food and beverage stores (grocery).
aUSRSLSFB/A.how_to_use: Staple category; least cyclical. Reflects food-at-home inflation.

aUSRSLSFSDP/A.description: Retail Sales, Food services and drinking places
aUSRSLSFSDP/A.meaning: Retail sales, food services and drinking places (restaurants/bars).
aUSRSLSFSDP/A.how_to_use: Discretionary services proxy. Watch for divergence from grocery — substitution gauge.

aUSRSLSHF/A.description: Retail Sales, Furniture and home furnishings stores
aUSRSLSHF/A.meaning: Retail Sales: furniture and home furnishings stores — sofas, rugs, lamps, decor. Strongly housing-cycle driven (people buy furniture when they move).
aUSRSLSHF/A.how_to_use: Leading indicator for housing-related consumption. Falls 6-12 months after housing-transaction declines. Currently weak post-2022 housing slowdown. Watch alongside aUSRSLSBMAT/A for full housing-related-retail picture.

aUSRSLSGAS/A.how_to_use: Mostly tracks gasoline price changes (volume is fairly steady). Strip out for ex-gasoline core retail.

aUSRSLSGM/A.meaning: Retail sales, general merchandise stores (Walmart/Target/Costco etc).
aUSRSLSGM/A.how_to_use: Broad consumer staples + discretionary mix. Healthier in down markets.

aUSRSLSGRS/A.how_to_use: Sub-component of food and beverage stores. Most price-sensitive consumer category.

aUSRSLSHPC/A.description: Retail Sales, Health and personal care stores
aUSRSLSHPC/A.meaning: Retail sales, health and personal care stores (drugstores).

aUSRSLSMV/A.description: Retail Sales, Motor vehicle and parts dealers
aUSRSLSMV/A.meaning: Retail sales, motor vehicle and parts dealers.
aUSRSLSMV/A.how_to_use: Largest retail category. Most rate-sensitive (auto financing).

aUSRSLSNSR/A.meaning: Retail sales, nonstore retailers (e-commerce + mail order).
aUSRSLSNSR/A.how_to_use: E-commerce primary measure. ~17% of retail and rising.

aUSRSLSSLG/A.description: Retail Sales, Sporting goods, hobby, musical instrument, and book stores
aUSRSLSSLG/A.meaning: Retail sales, sporting goods, hobby, instruments, books.

aUSRLCOA.description: Retail Sales, Total excluding bldg material & motor vehicle & parts & gasoline station & food svc, Chg P/P
aUSRLCOA.meaning: Retail Sales Control Group — total retail sales excluding autos, gas stations, building materials and food services. The cleanest signal of underlying consumer goods demand and the version that feeds directly into the BEA's GDP retail-control adjustment.
aUSRLCOA.how_to_use: The most analytically useful retail series. Smoother than headline because it strips out the most volatile categories. Use as a real-time GDP nowcast input — control group growth maps almost 1:1 to goods PCE in the quarterly accounts.

aUSSRXBDFB/A.description: Retail Sales, Total excluding bldg material, autos, gasoline station & food services
aUSSRXBDFB/A.meaning: Retail sales ex bldg material, autos, gas, food services — alternate.

aUSRSLS/A.description: Retail Sales, Total excluding food services
aUSRSLS/A.meaning: Retail sales, total ex food services.
aUSRSLS/A.how_to_use: Goods-only retail. Pair with food services for full headline.

aUSRETTOXA.description: Retail Sales, Total excluding food services
aUSRETTOXA.meaning: Retail sales total ex food services — alternate.

aUSRSLSXMV.description: Retail Sales, Total excluding food services and motor vehicle and parts dealers
aUSRSLSXMV.meaning: Retail sales ex food services and motor vehicle/parts.
aUSRSLSXMV.how_to_use: Strips two biggest categories. Reveals everything-else trends.

aUSRSLGA.description: Retail Sales, Total excluding motor vehicle dealers and gasoline station, Chg P/P
aUSRSLGA.meaning: Retail sales ex motor vehicle and gas, MoM.

aUSRSLSFS/A.description: Retail Sales, Total including food services
aUSRSLSFS/A.meaning: Retail Sales Total including Food Services — the broadest US retail aggregate from the Census Monthly Retail Trade Survey. Captures all retail trade (general merch, autos, gas, building materials, etc.) plus restaurant/bar sales.
aUSRSLSFS/A.how_to_use: The headline retail print released around the 15th of each month with two-month lag. Compare MoM and YoY changes vs consensus. Volatile categories (autos, gas) often drive surprises — switch to the 'control group' (aUSRLCOA) to see underlying consumer demand.

aUSRSLS.description: Retail Sales, Total including food services
aUSRSLS.meaning: Retail sales total including food services — alternate.

aUSRSLAR.meaning: Retail sales total inc food services MoM.

aUSRSLXAR.how_to_use: Inventory-to-sales ratio is the cycle gauge — rising = excess (margin pressure ahead); falling = shortage (pricing power). Watch alongside ISM customer-inventories sub-index.

aUSLIDXNOR/C.meaning: Index of the Conference Board Leading Economic Index (LEI).
aUSLIDXNOR/C.how_to_use: Composite of 10 leading indicators. Sustained 6-month declines historically signal recession with 6-12 month lead. Was a false positive in 2022-23 (predicted recession that didn't arrive). Use alongside yield curve, not in isolation.

aUSAHVEA.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings, year-over-year change — the headline wage-inflation gauge from the BLS establishment survey, released with NFP. Captures pay growth across all private nonfarm employees.
aUSAHVEA.how_to_use: Markets watch this for Fed implications: AHE growth above ~4% is incompatible with 2% inflation absent a productivity miracle. Less reliable than ECI (aUSEMPCI/A) at turning points because it's sensitive to compositional shifts (when low-wage hospitality jobs are cut, the average mechanically rises).

aUSAVGEAR.meaning: Average hourly earnings month-over-month change — monthly wage-growth pulse from BLS establishment survey, released with NFP.
aUSAVGEAR.how_to_use: Monthly wage-momentum read. >0.4% MoM hot (sustained ~5% YoY pace), <0.2% cool (sustained ~2.5% YoY). Highly volatile month-to-month due to compositional shifts and timing — smooth with 3-month moving average for cleaner signal.

aUSWRIMDA.description: Average hourly earnings, Producion workers, durable goods
aUSWRIMDA.meaning: Average hourly earnings, production workers, durable goods.
aUSWRIMDA.how_to_use: Manufacturing wages, durables. Less sensitive to services wage spirals.

aUSWAGMANA.description: Average hourly earnings, Producion workers, manufacturing
aUSWAGMANA.meaning: Average hourly earnings, production workers, total manufacturing — narrower than headline AHE. Captures shop-floor manufacturing wage levels (excludes supervisory/administrative).
aUSWAGMANA.how_to_use: Track for industrial-sector wage pressure separately from services. Manufacturing wages matter for unit labor costs and for international competitiveness. Watch alongside non-manufacturing services wages (aUSEARNHS/A) for broad wage pressure picture.

aUSWRIMNA.description: Average hourly earnings, Producion workers, nondurable goods
aUSWRIMNA.meaning: Average hourly earnings, production workers, nondurable manufacturing — wages at food, chemicals, paper, plastics, textiles plants. Less cyclical than durables wages.
aUSWRIMNA.how_to_use: Less cyclical than durables (aUSWRIMDB/A) because nondurable demand (food, consumer staples) is more stable. Use for tracking wage pressure in stable-demand manufacturing. Diverges from durables in recessions — durables wage growth slows faster.

aUSEARNHC/A.how_to_use: Construction wages — key for housing affordability and infrastructure cost models.

aUSWRIMDB/A.description: Average hourly earnings, manufacturing, durable goods
aUSWRIMDB/A.meaning: Average hourly earnings, manufacturing, durable goods, all employees — wages in autos, machinery, electronics, metals, transportation equipment. Broader (all-employees) than production-only series.
aUSWRIMDB/A.how_to_use: Most cyclical wage measure — durable manufacturing has the most volatile demand. Watch as a leading wage indicator: durables wages turn before headline. Useful proxy for skilled-trades wage pressure.

aUSWKIMDA.meaning: Average weekly hours, production workers, durable goods manufacturing — hours-per-worker measure. Pro-cyclical: rises in booms (overtime), falls in slowdowns (hours cuts before layoffs).
aUSWKIMDA.how_to_use: Leading labor-market indicator: hours cuts come before layoffs. Sustained drop below 40 hours/week historically signals manufacturing recession. Combined with manufacturing employment, gives total labor input for productivity calculations.

aUSWKIMA.meaning: Average weekly hours, production workers, total manufacturing — combined durable + nondurable. Pro-cyclical: rises in booms, falls in slowdowns.
aUSWKIMA.how_to_use: Manufacturing-hours cuts precede manufacturing-employment cuts by 1-3 months. Watch for sub-40-hour readings as recession-leading indicators. Combined with aUSWKIMDA (durables) for cyclical sub-segment read.

aUSWKIMNA.meaning: Average weekly hours, production workers, nondurable manufacturing — hours in food, chemicals, paper, plastics, textiles. Less cyclical than durables.
aUSWKIMNA.how_to_use: More stable than durable-goods hours. Useful as a baseline for stripping out cyclical demand effects. Sustained drops here (rare) would signal broad-based manufacturing-recession risk.

aUSWKNDURB/A.description: Average weekly earnings, nonfarm , durable goods
aUSWKNDURB/A.meaning: Average weekly earnings, nonfarm durable goods.
aUSWKNDURB/A.how_to_use: Take-home pay proxy. Hours × hourly wage.

aUSWKNMANB/A.meaning: Average weekly earnings, nonfarm manufacturing — hours × hourly wage for manufacturing workers. Take-home pay proxy for industrial-sector labor.
aUSWKNMANB/A.how_to_use: Combines wage and hours signals. Watch alongside services weekly earnings (aUSWEIPB/A) for pay-growth-by-sector picture. Manufacturing weekly wages have grown slower than services since 2010 — structural shift.

aUSWAGESD/CA.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, AVG HOURLY REAL EARNINGS OF ALL EMPLOYEES - TOTAL PRIVATE
aUSWAGESD/CA.meaning: Real average hourly earnings, all employees, total private.
aUSWAGESD/CA.how_to_use: Inflation-adjusted wages. Stagnant for years; 2022-23 had negative real wage growth.

aUSEARNHG/A.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm goods producing industries
aUSEARNHG/A.how_to_use: Goods-producing wage gauge. Cycles with manufacturing/construction.

aUSEARNH/A.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm payroll, total private
aUSEARNH/A.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings of all private nonfarm employees — level (not change). The headline wage series released alongside NFP each month from the BLS establishment survey. Around $35/hour in recent prints.
aUSEARNH/A.how_to_use: The level itself is rarely traded; markets focus on the YoY change (aUSAHVEA) as a wage-inflation gauge. Use the level for compositional adjustments and to track real wages (deflate by CPI). Production and nonsupervisory wages (separate series) are a cleaner signal of low-wage worker bargaining power.

aUSWAGMANB/A.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm payrolls, all employees, manufacturing
aUSWAGMANB/A.meaning: Average hourly earnings, nonfarm manufacturing, all employees — broader (all-employees) than production-only series. Includes supervisory + admin.
aUSWAGMANB/A.how_to_use: More inclusive than production-only AHE. Tracks total compensation pressure in manufacturing. Use for unit-labor-cost calculations alongside productivity (aUSPHOPBUS/A).

aUSEARNHS/A.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm service-producing industries
aUSEARNHS/A.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings, services-providing nonfarm — wages in healthcare, leisure, professional services, retail, finance, education. ~85% of the workforce.
aUSEARNHS/A.how_to_use: Drives core services CPI inflation — services-sector wage growth above ~4% sustains 2-3% core services inflation. The Fed's most-cited wage-pressure measure. Decompose by sub-sector: leisure/hospitality wages spiked 2021-22 then normalized; healthcare wages still rising structurally.

aUSEAHNPVT/A.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm, all private employees
aUSEAHNPVT/A.meaning: AHE all private employees — alternate series.

aUSWAGESB/A.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Nonfarm, all private employees, Chg Y/Y
aUSWAGESB/A.meaning: AHE all private employees YoY change.
aUSWAGESB/A.how_to_use: Wage inflation. >4% YoY too hot for 2% inflation; <3% suggests easing.

aUSEARNHM/A.meaning: Average Hourly Earnings, nonfarm, manufacturing (all employees) — same conceptual measure as aUSWAGMANB/A. Cross-check series.
aUSEARNHM/A.how_to_use: Cross-check against aUSWAGMANA. Use whichever has fresher data. The 'all-employees' framing has been the BLS standard since 2006 reform.

aUSEARN/CA.description: Earnings, Average Hourly, Real average, total private
aUSEARN/CA.how_to_use: Inflation-adjusted; the wage-gain that actually buys things.

aUSEARN.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Nonfarm payroll, total private
aUSEARN.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, total private nonfarm — hourly wage × hours worked per week. Pre-tax weekly take-home gauge.
aUSEARN.how_to_use: More cyclical than hourly wages because hours worked are pro-cyclical (overtime cut in slowdowns, expanded in booms). Better predictor of consumer spending than hourly wage alone. Watch for divergence: when hours fall while hourly wage rises, total income may flatten.

aUSEARNW/A.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Nonfarm payroll, total private
aUSEARNW/A.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, nonfarm payroll, total private — annual aggregate companion to aUSEARN at lower frequency.
aUSEARNW/A.how_to_use: Long-time-series wages tracking. Use aUSEARN for monthly tracking. Real version (deflated by CPI, aUSEARNW/CA) is the most analytically useful for household-income trend.

aUSWEIPB/A.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Nonfarm payrolls, all employees, total private
aUSWEIPB/A.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, nonfarm, all employees (private) — broader than production-only weekly earnings. Includes supervisory + admin staff.
aUSWEIPB/A.how_to_use: More inclusive than aUSEARN (production-only). Use for total private-sector wage-pressure tracking. Diverges from production weekly earnings when supervisory-vs-production hiring mix shifts.

aUSEARNW/CA.description: Earnings, Average Weekly, Real average, total private
aUSEARNW/CA.meaning: Real average weekly earnings — average weekly earnings deflated by CPI. Best take-home-pay-after-inflation gauge for tracking household real-income trends.
aUSEARNW/CA.how_to_use: The single best 'how is the typical worker doing' indicator. Negative real wage growth (2021-22) drives consumer-confidence collapses; recovery (2024+) supports spending. Track alongside real disposable personal income (DPI) for full household-cash-flow picture.

aUSEAWNPVT/CA.meaning: Average Weekly Earnings, total private, alternative source — companion series to aUSWEIPB/A.
aUSEAWNPVT/CA.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever is fresher. Useful for revisions tracking.

aUSACUIP.how_to_use: Sub-component or variant within Workforce & Unemployment. No standard practitioner usage notes have been written for this specific RIC — consult the upstream source publication (BEA, BLS, Federal Reserve, Census, USDA, EIA, or the relevant industry survey) for the formal definition before using it.

aUSAYUOP.how_to_use: Sub-component or variant within Workforce & Unemployment. aUSJOBAO.meaning: Level of US initial jobless claims.
aUSJOBAO.how_to_use: Highest-frequency US labor data — weekly Thursday release. Watch the 4-week moving average for trend. Sustained moves above ~250k signal labor-market deterioration.

aUSJOBCC/A.meaning: Continuing Claims (insured unemployment), national. Workers who filed initially and remain unemployed receiving benefits, lagged one week vs initial claims.
aUSJOBCC/A.how_to_use: More structural than initial claims — captures DURATION of unemployment. Rising continuing claims while initial claims stable = harder to find new jobs (a worse signal than rising initial claims). Caps at 26 weeks in most states.

aUSJOBCC4W/A.description: Jobless Claims, National, Continued, four week moving average
aUSJOBCC4W/A.meaning: Continuing Claims 4-week moving average — smoother trend.
aUSJOBCC4W/A.how_to_use: Use this for cycle reads; the weekly continuing-claims series has too much noise from holiday weeks and individual states. Crossing 1.9M is historically a recession signal.

aUSJOBC/A.meaning: Initial Jobless Claims, national. Weekly Department of Labor release every Thursday — the highest-frequency US labor data.
aUSJOBC/A.how_to_use: Watch the 4-week moving average for trend (weekly is too noisy). Sustained moves above ~250k signal labor-market deterioration; below 200k = very tight. First labor data to react to layoffs.

aUSUNCLP.meaning: Level of US initial jobless claims (national region).
aUSUNCLP.how_to_use: Highest-frequency US labor data — weekly Thursday release. Watch the 4-week moving average for trend. Sustained moves above ~250k signal labor-market deterioration.

aUSJOBAVG/A.description: Jobless Claims, National, Initial, four week moving average
aUSJOBAVG/A.meaning: Level of US initial jobless claims (national region).
aUSJOBAVG/A.how_to_use: Highest-frequency US labor data — weekly Thursday release. Watch the 4-week moving average for trend. Sustained moves above ~250k signal labor-market deterioration.

aUSUNPEP.description: Jobless Claims, National, Pandemic Emergency Unemployment Compensation
aUSUNPEP.meaning: Level of US initial jobless claims (national region).
aUSUNPEP.how_to_use: Highest-frequency US labor data — weekly Thursday release. Watch the 4-week moving average for trend. Sustained moves above ~250k signal labor-market deterioration.

aUSUNPUP.description: Jobless Claims, National, Pandemic Unemployment Assistance
aUSUNPUP.meaning: Level of US initial jobless claims (national region).
aUSUNPUP.how_to_use: Highest-frequency US labor data — weekly Thursday release. Watch the 4-week moving average for trend. Sustained moves above ~250k signal labor-market deterioration.

aUSUNIPP.description: Jobless Claims, National, Pandemic Unemployment Assistance
aUSUNIPP.meaning: Level of US initial jobless claims (national region).
aUSUNIPP.how_to_use: Highest-frequency US labor data — weekly Thursday release. Watch the 4-week moving average for trend. Sustained moves above ~250k signal labor-market deterioration.

aUSUNRJOBLI/A.description: Jobless Claims, National, Unemployment rate, insured
aUSUNRJOBLI/A.meaning: Level of the US civilian unemployment rate (national region).
aUSUNRJOBLI/A.how_to_use: From the BLS household survey, released alongside NFP. Pair with participation rate: a falling unemployment rate driven by exits (not hires) is weak. Crossing the Sahm Rule threshold (3-mo avg up 0.5pp from trailing-12m low) historically signals recession.

USBOS=ECI.meaning: Actual NOPA monthly soybean oil inventory stocks in millions of pounds, measuring crude soy oil held by processing members.
USBOS=ECI.how_to_use: Tight stocks indicate strong biofuel or food demand; bearish if above consensus (ample supply). Compare with CBOT soybean oil futures (BO) for basis moves.

pUSBOS=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for NOPA soybean oil stocks from the Reuters pre-release poll, typically from ~10 analysts.
pUSBOS=M.how_to_use: Primary benchmark for CBOT soy oil surprise; print below median (tighter stocks) is bullish for BO futures and soybean complex broadly.

pUSBOS=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for NOPA bean oil stocks.
pUSBOS=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median; model may incorporate crush pace, biofuel mandate data, and export inspections to produce a supply-side estimate.

pUSBOS=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for NOPA bean oil stocks — directional estimate of deviation from consensus at release.
pUSBOS=P.how_to_use: Use pre-release to set bias for CBOT soy oil and RD/RIN (renewable diesel) feedstock trades; tighter-than-expected stocks lift biofuel margins.

pUSBOS=E.meaning: Mean forecast for NOPA bean oil stocks across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSBOS=E.how_to_use: Compare vs median; mean-median divergence in small-sample agri polls is common — weight median more heavily for market impact assessment.

pUSBOS=O.meaning: Mode forecast for NOPA bean oil stocks among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSBOS=O.how_to_use: With a small analyst panel, mode can equal median; large gap signals diverse views on seasonal drawdown pace or biofuel demand.

pUSBOS=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for NOPA bean oil stocks in the Reuters poll.
pUSBOS=L.how_to_use: Defines most bullish (tightest supply) scenario; actual below min is a major upside surprise for CBOT BO futures and soy crush margins.

pUSBOS=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for NOPA bean oil stocks in the Reuters poll.
pUSBOS=H.how_to_use: Defines most bearish (loosest supply) scenario; actual above max pressures BO futures and signals weaker biofuel or export demand than expected.

pUSBOS=T.description: Bean Oil Stocks — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSBOS=T.meaning: Standard deviation of NOPA bean oil stocks forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSBOS=T.how_to_use: Small analyst panel means StdDev can be large relative to median; high uncertainty reflects variable biofuel blending mandate pace.

pUSBOS=C.description: Bean Oil Stocks — Number of Forecasters
pUSBOS=C.meaning: Number of analysts submitting a bean oil stocks forecast in the current Reuters poll.
pUSBOS=C.how_to_use: NOPA polls draw a small specialist panel (~8-15 respondents); interpret consensus with caution when count is below 10.

USDGXT=ECI.meaning: Actual MoM percent change in US durable goods orders excluding transportation equipment (aircraft, autos), from Census Bureau.
USDGXT=ECI.how_to_use: Preferred signal for underlying manufacturing demand since it strips Boeing batch effects; sustained positive trend indicates broad capex expansion.

pUSDGXT=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change from the Reuters pre-release poll.
pUSDGXT=M.how_to_use: Most watched durables sub-forecast by markets; positive surprise vs this median is the cleaner signal for industrial/capex sentiment compared to headline.

pUSDGXT=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change.
pUSDGXT=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median for model vs analyst divergence on core manufacturing trend; PMI/ISM inputs typically anchor this estimate.

pUSDGXT=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for durable goods ex-transport MoM change.
pUSDGXT=P.how_to_use: Pre-release surprise gauge for core manufacturing demand; positive predicted surprise with ISM confirmation raises industrial equity and USD outlook.

pUSDGXT=E.meaning: Mean forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGXT=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to check for outlier forecaster influence on the distribution of expectations for core manufacturing.

pUSDGXT=O.meaning: Mode forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGXT=O.how_to_use: When mode matches median, consensus is tightly formed; divergence signals forecaster disagreement on auto/machinery sub-component trends.

pUSDGXT=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSDGXT=L.how_to_use: Bearish bound for core manufacturing; actual below min is a strong contraction signal that may weigh on industrial capex outlook.

pUSDGXT=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for durable goods ex-transport MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSDGXT=H.how_to_use: Bullish bound for core manufacturing; print above max signals broad-based order strength and supports upward Industrial Production revisions.

pUSDGXT=T.meaning: Standard deviation of durable goods ex-transport MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGXT=T.how_to_use: Benchmark uncertainty for core manufacturing; compare to headline StdDev to confirm that stripping transport reduces forecast variance.

pUSDGXT=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting a durable goods ex-transport forecast in the current Reuters poll.
pUSDGXT=C.how_to_use: Higher participation than ex-defense given analyst focus on this strip; validate consensus quality, especially following supply-chain disruption periods.

USFORD=ECI.meaning: Census Bureau actual MoM percent change in total US factory orders (durable + nondurable goods), released ~4 weeks after the reference month.
USFORD=ECI.how_to_use: Broader than durables alone; nondurable component (chemicals, food, petroleum) adds refinery and consumer goods cycle signals. Upside confirms manufacturing recovery.

pUSFORD=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for US factory orders MoM change from the Reuters pre-release poll.
pUSFORD=M.how_to_use: Primary factory orders benchmark; surprise vs median typically drives industrials and materials equities. Cross-check with the durables advance release already known.

pUSFORD=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for factory orders MoM change.
pUSFORD=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median; model may incorporate petroleum-price and PMI signals that analyst surveys lag, especially for nondurable component.

pUSFORD=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for factory orders MoM change — SmartEconomics directional estimate of actual deviation from consensus.
pUSFORD=P.how_to_use: Use pre-release to size surprise risk for broad manufacturing; strongly positive predicted surprise supports cyclical equity rotation.

pUSFORD=E.meaning: Mean forecast for factory orders MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSFORD=E.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median; energy-price swings can pull nondurable orders outliers, creating mean-median skew in the forecast distribution.

pUSFORD=O.meaning: Mode forecast for factory orders MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSFORD=O.how_to_use: Mode near zero indicates stable consensus; significant positive mode reflects shared view on nondurable rebound (e.g., petroleum orders recovery).

pUSFORD=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for factory orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSFORD=L.how_to_use: Defines worst-case scenario for total manufacturing demand; actual below min signals broad-based weakness across durable and nondurable goods.

pUSFORD=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for factory orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSFORD=H.how_to_use: Defines bullish case; print above max would indicate unexpected surge across both durable and nondurable orders, rare outside energy-price spikes.

pUSFORD=T.description: Factory Orders MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSFORD=T.meaning: Standard deviation of factory orders MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSFORD=T.how_to_use: Elevated StdDev typically driven by uncertainty in petroleum/chemicals orders; compare with durable goods StdDev to identify nondurable uncertainty component.

pUSFORD=C.description: Factory Orders MM — Number of Forecasters
pUSFORD=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting a factory orders forecast in the current Reuters poll.
pUSFORD=C.how_to_use: Factory orders draws a moderate response rate; lower count than NFP or CPI polls — validate consensus size before trading the surprise.

USGFSF=ECI.meaning: Actual release of Real Final Sales Final Estimate — the third and most comprehensive BEA vintage of GDP excluding inventories, published ~90 days after quarter-end.
USGFSF=ECI.how_to_use: The definitive read on final demand for the quarter. Large revisions from Prelim (USGFSP=ECI) to Final are uncommon; when they occur, they often reflect BEA benchmark source-data revisions.

pUSGFSF=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the GDP Sales Final Estimate from the Reuters poll — the street's expected final revision to real domestic demand.
pUSGFSF=M.how_to_use: By the Final stage, surprises vs consensus are rare. A notable beat or miss of pUSGFSF=M on the actual is highly significant and often tied to benchmark data revisions rather than estimation errors.

pUSGFSF=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the GDP Sales Final Estimate — an algorithmic estimate with access to the most complete set of quarterly source data.
pUSGFSF=F.how_to_use: At the Final stage, the SmartEconomics model and human consensus should converge; persistent divergence from pUSGFSF=M may indicate SmartEconomics is capturing an outlier data series.

pUSGFSF=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Sales Final Estimate — pre-release directional signal for the definitive final-demand revision.
pUSGFSF=P.how_to_use: A non-zero Predicted Surprise at the Final stage is unusual and noteworthy. If pUSGFSF=P and pUSGDPF=P (GDP Final Predicted Surprise) diverge, expected surprise is inventory-side, not demand-side.

pUSGFSF=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the GDP Sales Final Estimate across surveyed economists — arithmetic average of all submitted final-demand forecasts.
pUSGFSF=E.how_to_use: By the Final stage, mean and median (pUSGFSF=M) typically converge, indicating a symmetric, narrow distribution. Residual mean-median divergence implies outlier forecasters with access to different data.

pUSGFSF=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Sales Final Estimate — the most frequently submitted point estimate in the Reuters economist survey for the final demand vintage.
pUSGFSF=O.how_to_use: Mode-median alignment at the Final stage confirms tight, converged consensus on demand. Used alongside StdDev (pUSGFSF=T) to confirm whether the forecast distribution is narrow or still bimodal.

pUSGFSF=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) forecast for the GDP Sales Final Estimate — the floor of the final-demand distribution at the definitive vintage.
pUSGFSF=L.how_to_use: An actual print (USGFSF=ECI) below the Min at the Final stage would be extraordinary and would likely reflect a benchmark data revision. Track to ensure the range is narrowing from Advance to Final.

pUSGFSF=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) forecast for the GDP Sales Final Estimate — the ceiling of the forecast range for the definitive final-demand release.
pUSGFSF=H.how_to_use: Narrowing Max from Prelim to Final is expected as uncertainty resolves. If the Max remains elevated versus the Prelim, it signals ongoing data ambiguity in the quarterly accounts.

pUSGFSF=T.description: GDP Sales Final — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSGFSF=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the GDP Sales Final Estimate — the residual level of economist disagreement about final domestic demand at the definitive revision stage.
pUSGFSF=T.how_to_use: StdDev at the Final stage should be the lowest of the three vintages (Advance, Prelim, Final). A Final-stage StdDev similar to the Advance stage implies the data was genuinely hard to forecast throughout.

pUSGFSF=C.description: GDP Sales Final — Number of Forecasters
pUSGFSF=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting forecasts for the GDP Sales Final Estimate in the Reuters poll — the sample size at the definitively revised vintage.
pUSGFSF=C.how_to_use: Count often drops from Advance to Final as the Final release commands less market attention. A very low count means the Final consensus statistics are unreliable and should be treated as indicative only.

USISME=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Manufacturing Employment sub-index, measuring net hiring/firing intentions across ~300 surveyed manufacturing firms.
USISME=ECI.how_to_use: Leads Nonfarm Payrolls for the manufacturing sector; a sustained move below 50 is an early warning of factory-sector job losses before the BLS print.

pUSISME=M.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Median Consensus
pUSISME=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index from the Reuters economist poll.
pUSISME=M.how_to_use: Sets the expected baseline; surprise relative to consensus refines the pre-NFP labor market read for the manufacturing sector.

pUSISME=F.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — SmartEconomics Forecast
pUSISME=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index.
pUSISME=F.how_to_use: Compare to Median Consensus (pUSISME=M) for model-vs-street divergence; a gap above consensus may pre-signal better factory hiring than the street expects.

pUSISME=P.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Predicted Surprise
pUSISME=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation from street consensus.
pUSISME=P.how_to_use: Use to adjust directional bias on the ISM Employment sub-index before release; feeds into pre-NFP positioning for manufacturing payrolls.

pUSISME=E.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Mean Forecast
pUSISME=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSISME=E.how_to_use: Compare with median (pUSISME=M) to detect skew; a mean below median implies tail risk of a negative labor-market surprise in manufacturing.

pUSISME=O.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Mode Forecast
pUSISME=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index — the most frequently submitted value in the poll.
pUSISME=O.how_to_use: Identifies the most common scenario among forecasters; useful when the distribution is bimodal and mean/median do not clearly represent the consensus.

pUSISME=L.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Min Forecast
pUSISME=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) individual forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
pUSISME=L.how_to_use: Defines the downside boundary; a print near or below this level indicates a severe manufacturing labor-market miss relative to all surveyed economists.

pUSISME=H.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Max Forecast
pUSISME=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) individual forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
pUSISME=H.how_to_use: Defines the upside boundary; a print above this signals an outsized beat — likely to drive a stronger-than-expected reaction in rate and FX markets.

pUSISME=T.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSISME=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index — measures economist disagreement.
pUSISME=T.how_to_use: Rising dispersion ahead of the release signals elevated uncertainty about factory hiring conditions; consider widening risk bounds in pre-NFP models.

pUSISME=C.description: ISM Manuf Employment Idx — Number of Forecasters
pUSISME=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for the ISM Manufacturing Employment Index in the current Reuters poll.
pUSISME=C.how_to_use: Low participation may indicate limited forecaster coverage of this sub-index; treat consensus with lower confidence when the count is well below average.

USISMP=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid sub-index, measuring the net share of firms reporting higher input costs month-on-month.
USISMP=ECI.how_to_use: A leading indicator for goods-price inflation and PPI/CPI goods components; a surge above 60 has historically preceded rising core goods CPI by 1-3 months.

pUSISMP=M.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Median Consensus
pUSISMP=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid from the Reuters economist poll.
pUSISMP=M.how_to_use: Sets the inflation-signal baseline; a beat vs. consensus can shift breakeven inflation expectations and pressure the front-end of the rates curve.

pUSISMP=F.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — SmartEconomics Forecast
pUSISMP=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid, incorporating commodity prices and pipeline inflation inputs.
pUSISMP=F.how_to_use: A model forecast above street median (pUSISMP=M) warns of underappreciated inflation pressure in manufacturing supply chains.

pUSISMP=P.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Predicted Surprise
pUSISMP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will exceed or undershoot consensus.
pUSISMP=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise in Prices Paid has hawkish implications; use as a pre-release signal for TIPS breakevens and USD positioning.

pUSISMP=E.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Mean Forecast
pUSISMP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSISMP=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect distributional skew; an elevated mean relative to median suggests some forecasters see sharp cost-pressure acceleration.

pUSISMP=O.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Mode Forecast
pUSISMP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid — the most frequently submitted individual forecast in the poll.
pUSISMP=O.how_to_use: Identifies the modal price-pressure scenario; cross-reference with commodity futures trends to validate whether the consensus cluster makes sense.

pUSISMP=L.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Min Forecast
pUSISMP=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid in the Reuters poll — the most dovish cost-pressure view.
pUSISMP=L.how_to_use: Defines the downside scenario where input costs ease sharply; a print at or below this level signals unexpected goods deflation risk.

pUSISMP=H.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Max Forecast
pUSISMP=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid in the Reuters poll — the most hawkish cost-pressure view.
pUSISMP=H.how_to_use: Defines the upside scenario; a print above this level would represent a significant inflation shock from the manufacturing sector.

pUSISMP=T.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSISMP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid — a measure of disagreement on manufacturing inflation.
pUSISMP=T.how_to_use: High dispersion ahead of the release suggests commodity-price volatility is making inflation forecasting difficult; widen inflation risk premia accordingly.

pUSISMP=C.description: ISM Mfg Prices Paid — Number of Forecasters
pUSISMP=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid in the current Reuters poll.
pUSISMP=C.how_to_use: A larger panel provides more reliable consensus; a sharp drop in participant count may reduce confidence in the median forecast ahead of the release.

USOPMI=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity sub-index, which measures current output levels across services firms — the closest services equivalent to ISM Manufacturing Production.
USOPMI=ECI.how_to_use: Often leads the headline Non-Manufacturing PMI at cycle turns; a sharp decline relative to consensus (pUSOPMI=M) signals abrupt softening in services output.

pUSOPMI=M.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Median Consensus
pUSOPMI=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity from the Reuters economist poll.
pUSOPMI=M.how_to_use: Sets the expected services output level; surprise vs. consensus can shift near-term GDP tracking estimates and broad risk-asset sentiment.

pUSOPMI=F.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — SmartEconomics Forecast
pUSOPMI=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity.
pUSOPMI=F.how_to_use: Model divergence from street median (pUSOPMI=M) flags potential for an asymmetric services output surprise.

pUSOPMI=P.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Predicted Surprise
pUSOPMI=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will beat or miss street consensus.
pUSOPMI=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise signals stronger-than-expected services output; bullish for consumer discretionary and rate-sensitive sectors.

pUSOPMI=E.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Mean Forecast
pUSOPMI=E.meaning: Mean forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSOPMI=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect skew; a mean significantly below median implies downside tail risk to services output — consider GDP tracking downside scenarios.

pUSOPMI=O.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Mode Forecast
pUSOPMI=O.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — the most frequently submitted value in the poll.
pUSOPMI=O.how_to_use: Reveals the modal output scenario; cross-check against current credit-card spending and retail data to validate the consensus cluster's plausibility.

pUSOPMI=L.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Min Forecast
pUSOPMI=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — the most bearish output view in the poll.
pUSOPMI=L.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk boundary; a print at or below this level indicates a significant services output shock and will likely prompt downward GDP revisions.

pUSOPMI=H.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Max Forecast
pUSOPMI=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — the most bullish output view in the poll.
pUSOPMI=H.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk boundary; a print above this implies exceptional services strength and is likely to trigger a broad risk-on move.

pUSOPMI=T.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSOPMI=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity — measures forecast dispersion.
pUSOPMI=T.how_to_use: Elevated standard deviation signals uncertainty about near-term services output; corresponds to wider implied volatility on services-sensitive assets.

pUSOPMI=C.description: ISM N-Mfg Bus Act — Number of Forecasters
pUSOPMI=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing Business Activity in the current Reuters poll.
pUSOPMI=C.how_to_use: A stable, large panel count increases confidence in the consensus; a low or declining count raises questions about coverage and reliability of the median.

USIMP=ECI.meaning: Actual month-over-month change in US Import Prices from the BLS, released ~mid-month. Captures price pressures entering the US economy from abroad, driven by commodity prices, FX, and global supply-chain conditions.
USIMP=ECI.how_to_use: Compare to pUSIMP=M to assess the surprise; a larger-than-expected increase raises pass-through inflation risk and can lift breakeven inflation rates and front-end yields.

pUSIMP=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for US Import Prices month-over-month from the Reuters poll, collected ahead of the BLS mid-month release.
pUSIMP=M.how_to_use: Use as the key benchmark for the release; an actual print above the median — especially in a tariff-sensitive environment — reinforces inflation persistence narratives and weighs on rate-cut expectations.

pUSIMP=F.meaning: SmartEconomics algorithmic forecast for US Import Prices MoM, providing a model-derived estimate ahead of the BLS release.
pUSIMP=F.how_to_use: Divergence between pUSIMP=F and pUSIMP=M highlights cases where high-frequency commodity/FX inputs disagree with human forecasters; a higher SmartEcon forecast signals commodity or USD-driven upside risk.

pUSIMP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for US Import Prices MoM — the systematic expected deviation of the actual from the median consensus.
pUSIMP=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise suggests the actual MoM print will likely exceed consensus; combine with pUSIMP=T to assess confidence in that directional call before the BLS release.

pUSIMP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for US Import Prices MoM across all Reuters poll respondents, which may diverge from the median when a minority of forecasters hold outsized views on commodity or currency moves.
pUSIMP=E.how_to_use: When the mean exceeds the median, the distribution is right-skewed, implying more upside than downside risk to import inflation; relevant for USD and TIPS positioning ahead of the release.

pUSIMP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for US Import Prices MoM — the most commonly submitted estimate in the Reuters panel.
pUSIMP=O.how_to_use: If the mode differs markedly from the median, forecasters are clustered around two distinct scenarios (e.g., energy-driven spike vs. soft reading); useful for scenario-weighting in macro overlays.

pUSIMP=L.meaning: Minimum (most deflationary) forecast for US Import Prices MoM in the Reuters poll, marking the floor of economist expectations.
pUSIMP=L.how_to_use: Together with pUSIMP=H, defines the full forecast range; an actual reading below the floor is a rare disinflationary shock that would strengthen rate-cut expectations and weigh on commodity currencies.

pUSIMP=H.meaning: Maximum (most inflationary) forecast for US Import Prices MoM in the Reuters poll, marking the ceiling of economist expectations.
pUSIMP=H.how_to_use: Use the H-L spread as a proxy for forecast uncertainty around global commodity and FX conditions; a wide spread warrants larger volatility allowances in inflation-sensitive strategies.

pUSIMP=T.description: Import Prices MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSIMP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for US Import Prices MoM in the Reuters poll, indicating economist disagreement about near-term import inflation.
pUSIMP=T.how_to_use: High standard deviation ahead of the release (relative to recent cycles) suggests increased sensitivity to oil prices or FX volatility; combine with pUSIMP=M to construct a symmetric surprise range for risk management.

pUSIMP=C.description: Import Prices MM — Number of Forecasters
pUSIMP=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting forecasts in the Reuters US Import Prices MoM poll for the current release.
pUSIMP=C.how_to_use: Track alongside pUSIMP=T to ensure the standard deviation is based on a sufficiently large sample; a falling count may signal declining market interest in import-price risk ahead of a data release.

USJOLT=ECI.meaning: BLS monthly actual count of US job openings (JOLTS), released with ~6-week lag. Measures unfilled demand for labor across all industries.
USJOLT=ECI.how_to_use: Pre-COVID baseline ~7M; peaked ~12M (2022); now ~8M. Rising openings signal tight labor supply and support Fed hawkishness; compare with quits and layoffs in the same release.

pUSJOLT=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for US JOLTS Job Openings from Reuters poll conducted ~1 week before BLS release.
pUSJOLT=M.how_to_use: Primary benchmark for surprise calculation; positive surprise (actual > median) lifts short-dated Treasuries via Fed tightening expectations. Track alongside NFP and quits rate.

pUSJOLT=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for JOLTS Job Openings, derived from macro factor inputs rather than surveyed economists.
pUSJOLT=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median (=M) to detect systematic model bias; large divergence may signal non-consensus regime shift in labor demand.

pUSJOLT=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for JOLTS Job Openings — SmartEconomics estimate of likely direction and magnitude of deviation from consensus.
pUSJOLT=P.how_to_use: Use pre-release to position for surprise risk; a strongly positive predicted surprise combined with tight labor market context raises rate-hike odds.

pUSJOLT=E.meaning: Mean (average) of all surveyed economist forecasts for JOLTS Job Openings for the upcoming BLS release.
pUSJOLT=E.how_to_use: Use with median (=M) to detect skew in the distribution; mean > median indicates upside outlier forecasts skewing expectations.

pUSJOLT=O.meaning: Mode (most frequently submitted) forecast for JOLTS Job Openings among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSJOLT=O.how_to_use: Mode near median confirms tight consensus clustering; large gap signals bi-modal forecast distribution and higher surprise risk.

pUSJOLT=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) individual forecast for JOLTS Job Openings submitted in the Reuters poll.
pUSJOLT=L.how_to_use: Defines the bearish tail of analyst expectations; actual print below min signals an extreme downside surprise with potential risk-off impact.

pUSJOLT=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) individual forecast for JOLTS Job Openings submitted in the Reuters poll.
pUSJOLT=H.how_to_use: Defines the bullish tail; actual print above max is an extreme upside surprise, typically hawkish for rates and bullish for USD.

pUSJOLT=T.description: JOLTS Job Openings — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSJOLT=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for JOLTS Job Openings across all Reuters poll respondents, measuring forecast dispersion.
pUSJOLT=T.how_to_use: High StdDev ahead of release signals elevated uncertainty; wider dispersion increases options premium on rate-sensitive instruments around JOLTS day.

pUSJOLT=C.description: JOLTS Job Openings — Number of Forecasters
pUSJOLT=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for JOLTS Job Openings in the Reuters poll for the current release cycle.
pUSJOLT=C.how_to_use: Higher count improves reliability of median/mean; fewer than ~15 respondents makes the consensus less representative of street expectations.

USNSC=ECI.meaning: Actual monthly volume of soybeans crushed by NOPA member processors, reported in million bushels (56 lb/bu), typically released mid-month.
USNSC=ECI.how_to_use: Strong crush pace draws down soybean stocks and supports CBOT soybean prices (ZS); cross-check with USDA crush estimates for seasonal demand trend.

pUSNSC=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for NOPA monthly soy crush volume from the Reuters pre-release poll.
pUSNSC=M.how_to_use: Primary crush benchmark; actual above median (stronger crush) is bullish for CBOT soybeans (ZS) and signals strong meal/oil demand from livestock and biofuel sectors.

pUSNSC=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for NOPA monthly soy crush volume.
pUSNSC=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median; model likely incorporates crush margins, soybean meal export inspections, and biofuel demand signals.

pUSNSC=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for NOPA soy crush — directional estimate of actual deviation from consensus at release.
pUSNSC=P.how_to_use: Use pre-release for CBOT soy positioning; positive predicted surprise combined with tight soybean stocks is a strong bullish signal for ZS futures.

pUSNSC=E.meaning: Mean forecast for NOPA soy crush volume across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSNSC=E.how_to_use: Small specialist panel; compare mean vs median to assess whether outlier crush estimates skew the distribution, common during seasonal processing peaks.

pUSNSC=O.meaning: Mode forecast for NOPA soy crush volume among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSNSC=O.how_to_use: Mode-median clustering indicates consensus on processing pace; wide gap signals split analyst views on crush margin incentives.

pUSNSC=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for NOPA soy crush volume in the Reuters poll.
pUSNSC=L.how_to_use: Defines the bearish crush scenario (weak processing demand); actual below min suggests plant outages or margin compression reducing crush pace.

pUSNSC=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for NOPA soy crush volume in the Reuters poll.
pUSNSC=H.how_to_use: Defines the bullish crush scenario; actual above max indicates exceptional processing pace, strongly bullish for soybean cash basis and ZS futures.

pUSNSC=T.meaning: Standard deviation of NOPA soy crush volume forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSNSC=T.how_to_use: Seasonal peaks (Sep-Nov) show lower StdDev as crush pace is predictable; high StdDev outside peak season signals unusual margin or supply disruption uncertainty.

pUSNSC=C.meaning: Number of analysts submitting a NOPA soy crush forecast in the current Reuters poll.
pUSNSC=C.how_to_use: Specialist agri panel; low count (~8-12) is typical — weigh consensus quality accordingly and cross-reference USDA weekly crush data.

USNCI=ECI.meaning: Actual monthly net long-term cross-border securities flows excluding swap-related transactions, from the TIC report. Captures combined foreign purchases of US stocks, bonds, and agencies minus US purchases of foreign securities.
USNCI=ECI.how_to_use: A broader capital-flow gauge than T-bond buying alone; persistent positive flows underpin USD demand and finance the current-account deficit, while a sustained decline can signal portfolio rebalancing away from US assets.

USNDCG=ECI.description: Nondef Cap Ex-Air R MM — Actual
USNDCG=ECI.meaning: Revised actual MoM percent change for nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft, published alongside the following month's advance release.
USNDCG=ECI.how_to_use: Revision from the advance (USNDXA=ECI) captures order adjustments; compare advance vs revised to assess measurement noise and improve forecasting models.

USBPE=ECI.meaning: Realised monthly Building Permits issued, released jointly with Housing Starts by Census/HUD mid-month. Permits lead starts by 1–3 months and are considered a leading indicator of residential construction activity.
USBPE=ECI.how_to_use: Track USBPE=ECI vs USHST=ECI ratio to gauge the permits-to-starts pipeline; a rising permits surplus signals future starts acceleration. Use to cross-check pUSBPE=M forecast accuracy ahead of subsequent releases.

pUSBPE=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for US Building Permits from the Reuters pre-release poll. Permits are a leading indicator authorising future construction and reflect developer confidence in demand conditions.
pUSBPE=M.how_to_use: A permits beat above pUSBPE=M implies pipeline strength 1–3 months forward; pair with pUSHST=M for the current-month read and pUSEHS=M for existing-home demand context in a unified housing dashboard.

pUSBPE=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based point forecast for Building Permits, offering a quantitative cross-check against the analyst panel median prior to the Census release.
pUSBPE=F.how_to_use: When pUSBPE=F deviates meaningfully from pUSBPE=M, consult pUSBPE=P (Predicted Surprise) to determine direction; model-consensus divergence in permits can foreshadow a starts revision the following month.

pUSBPE=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for Building Permits, capturing the gap between the SmartEconomics model forecast (pUSBPE=F) and the analyst consensus (pUSBPE=M). Positive values signal the model expects a stronger-than-consensus print.
pUSBPE=P.how_to_use: Use as an early directional signal for the permits release; combine with pUSHST=P to identify whether the entire housing report is skewed to the upside or downside relative to consensus.

pUSBPE=E.meaning: Mean forecast for Building Permits across all Reuters poll participants, which alongside the median reveals skew in the distribution of analyst expectations.
pUSBPE=E.how_to_use: A mean above the median indicates bullish tail risk from optimistic outliers; use pUSBPE=E vs pUSBPE=M divergence as a skew gauge when setting risk-reward on construction-sensitive trades.

pUSBPE=O.meaning: Mode of Building Permits forecasts—the value most frequently submitted by poll participants—indicating where analyst conviction clusters most tightly.
pUSBPE=O.how_to_use: If pUSBPE=O differs sharply from pUSBPE=M, the consensus is bimodal and the median may be misleading; in such cases weight pUSBPE=T (StdDev) more heavily when assessing market impact risk.

pUSBPE=L.meaning: Minimum individual Building Permits forecast in the Reuters poll, representing the lowest (most bearish) analyst estimate submitted for the upcoming release.
pUSBPE=L.how_to_use: Pair with pUSBPE=H to establish the full analyst range; a realised print below pUSBPE=L constitutes a tail miss and typically triggers meaningful downward revisions to residential construction forecasts.

pUSBPE=H.meaning: Maximum individual Building Permits forecast in the Reuters poll, representing the highest (most bullish) analyst estimate submitted for the upcoming release.
pUSBPE=H.how_to_use: A print above pUSBPE=H is an extreme upside outcome; the H-minus-L spread scaled by pUSBPE=M gives a normalised uncertainty ratio useful for volatility-adjusted position sizing.

pUSBPE=T.description: Building Permits: Number — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSBPE=T.meaning: Standard deviation of Building Permits forecasts across Reuters poll participants, measuring the degree of analyst uncertainty ahead of the Census/HUD release.
pUSBPE=T.how_to_use: Rising StdDev month-over-month signals increasing uncertainty about the housing pipeline—often tied to volatile mortgage rates or weather; calibrate event-risk trades on homebuilder or MBS instruments accordingly.

pUSBPE=C.description: Building Permits: Number — Number of Forecasters
pUSBPE=C.meaning: Number of individual analysts who submitted Building Permits forecasts in the current Reuters poll round, reflecting the statistical depth behind the consensus figures.
pUSBPE=C.how_to_use: Cross-reference with pUSHST=C; months where both permit and starts forecaster counts are low should be treated with lower confidence, particularly in volatile rate environments.

USDGN=ECI.meaning: Census Bureau monthly actual MoM percent change in US durable goods orders (items intended to last 3+ years), released ~25-26th of the following month.
USDGN=ECI.how_to_use: Highly volatile due to aircraft/defense swings; use Ex-Transport (USDGXT=ECI) for trend. Upside surprises lift cyclicals and USD.

pUSDGN=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for the MoM change in US durable goods orders from the Reuters pre-release poll.
pUSDGN=M.how_to_use: Headline durable goods is noisy; track deviation from median alongside Ex-Transport median to distinguish underlying trend from transport volatility.

pUSDGN=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for durable goods orders MoM change.
pUSDGN=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median (=M) to flag potential non-consensus signal; useful for assessing whether model factors (PMI, ISM) confirm or diverge from analyst consensus.

pUSDGN=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for durable goods orders — SmartEconomics directional estimate of deviation from consensus at release.
pUSDGN=P.how_to_use: Use pre-release to gauge skew risk; combine with ISM Manufacturing New Orders as a directional cross-check.

pUSDGN=E.meaning: Mean forecast for durable goods orders MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGN=E.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median to detect skew from outlier forecasters; outlier large Boeing orders sometimes pull mean well above median.

pUSDGN=O.meaning: Mode (most common) forecast for durable goods orders MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGN=O.how_to_use: Mode clustering near zero indicates consensus expects a flat month; significant deviation from median signals split views on transport orders.

pUSDGN=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for durable goods orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSDGN=L.how_to_use: Defines the bearish bound; actual print below min indicates an extreme negative surprise, typically negative for industrial/cyclical equities.

pUSDGN=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for durable goods orders MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSDGN=H.how_to_use: Defines the bullish bound; Boeing large-order months can produce prints well above max, which tend to be followed by mean-reversion next month.

pUSDGN=T.meaning: Standard deviation of durable goods orders forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGN=T.how_to_use: High StdDev reflects uncertainty about aircraft/defense swing factor; compare with Ex-Transport StdDev to isolate volatility source.

pUSDGN=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting a forecast for durable goods orders in the current Reuters poll cycle.
pUSDGN=C.how_to_use: Validate consensus reliability; low count ahead of releases following large Boeing announcements reflects forecaster uncertainty about transport component.

USDGND=ECI.meaning: Actual MoM percent change in US durable goods orders excluding volatile defense spending, from Census Bureau.
USDGND=ECI.how_to_use: Removes lumpy government contracts to reveal private-sector demand; compare with headline and Ex-Transport to triangulate underlying manufacturing momentum.

pUSDGND=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for durable goods orders MoM change excluding defense orders from the Reuters poll.
pUSDGND=M.how_to_use: Use to separate private demand trends from government contract timing; persistent upside vs consensus indicates non-defense manufacturing recovery.

pUSDGND=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change.
pUSDGND=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median to check if macro models aligned on defense-stripped trend; useful when large DoD contracts distort headline consensus.

pUSDGND=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for durable goods ex-defense orders MoM change.
pUSDGND=P.how_to_use: Signals pre-release surprise direction for private manufacturing demand; combine with ISM New Orders sub-index as a cross-check.

pUSDGND=E.meaning: Mean forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGND=E.how_to_use: Compare vs median to identify skew; outlier views on commercial aircraft can still distort mean even after defense exclusion.

pUSDGND=O.meaning: Mode forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGND=O.how_to_use: Tight clustering of mode near median signals analyst consensus on underlying ex-defense trend; gaps indicate split views.

pUSDGND=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSDGND=L.how_to_use: Defines the bearish scenario for private manufacturing; useful for stress-testing capex outlooks when combined with core capex (USNDXA) range.

pUSDGND=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for durable goods ex-defense MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSDGND=H.how_to_use: Defines the bullish scenario; actual print above max indicates unexpected surge in private-sector capital goods demand.

pUSDGND=T.description: Durables Ex-Defense MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSDGND=T.meaning: Standard deviation of durable goods ex-defense MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSDGND=T.how_to_use: Lower StdDev vs headline durables confirms defense exclusion reduces forecast uncertainty; persistent high StdDev may reflect aircraft order uncertainty.

pUSDGND=C.description: Durables Ex-Defense MM — Number of Forecasters
pUSDGND=C.meaning: Number of forecasters submitting an ex-defense durable goods estimate in the current Reuters poll.
pUSDGND=C.how_to_use: Typically lower response rate than headline durables; low count increases noise in consensus measures.

USEHSP=ECI.meaning: Realised month-over-month percentage change in Existing Home Sales as published by the NAR, derived directly from USEHS=ECI. Provides a rate-of-change perspective that is easier to compare across time than the level series.
USEHSP=ECI.how_to_use: Use USEHSP=ECI vs pUSEHSP=M to score the percentage-change forecast; a large negative surprise (e.g., -5% vs consensus +1%) is a strong housing-cycle deceleration signal that often precedes downward revisions to GDP residential investment.

pUSEHSP=M.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Median Consensus
pUSEHSP=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the month-over-month percentage change in Existing Home Sales from the Reuters poll. Summarises analyst expectations in rate-of-change terms, which many traders monitor alongside the level (pUSEHS=M).
pUSEHSP=M.how_to_use: When pUSEHSP=M is positive but pUSEHS=M implies a still-depressed level, contextualise the recovery as base-effect driven; use the pair together to avoid misinterpreting a bounce in % change as a true demand recovery.

pUSEHSP=F.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — SmartEconomics Forecast
pUSEHSP=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for the MoM percentage change in Existing Home Sales, providing a quantitative cross-check to the analyst panel consensus in percentage-change space.
pUSEHSP=F.how_to_use: Compare pUSEHSP=F with pUSEHSP=M alongside pUSEHS=F vs pUSEHS=M; consistent directional agreement between level and % change model forecasts raises conviction in the Predicted Surprise signal.

pUSEHSP=P.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Predicted Surprise
pUSEHSP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the Existing Home Sales MoM percentage change—the difference between SmartEconomics model (pUSEHSP=F) and analyst consensus (pUSEHSP=M). A positive value signals the model expects a stronger-than-consensus monthly gain.
pUSEHSP=P.how_to_use: Use in conjunction with pUSEHS=P; when both level and % change Predicted Surprises agree in direction the signal is more robust. Divergence between the two may indicate rounding or seasonal-adjustment artefacts in the consensus.

pUSEHSP=E.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Mean Forecast
pUSEHSP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the MoM percentage change in Existing Home Sales across all Reuters poll submissions, more sensitive to extreme outlier estimates than the median.
pUSEHSP=E.how_to_use: A mean well above the median in % change space implies a cluster of analysts expects a large monthly jump; pair with pUSEHSP=H to gauge how extreme the bullish tail is and whether it reflects genuine data signals or stale revisions.

pUSEHSP=O.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Mode Forecast
pUSEHSP=O.meaning: Mode of the Existing Home Sales MoM percentage-change forecasts—the single % change estimate submitted most frequently by Reuters poll participants.
pUSEHSP=O.how_to_use: When pUSEHSP=O clusters at 0.0%, analysts may be anchoring to a no-change prior; contrast with pUSEHSP=M and pUSEHSP=T to determine whether the consensus embeds genuine uncertainty or conservative round-number anchoring.

pUSEHSP=L.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Min Forecast
pUSEHSP=L.meaning: Minimum (most bearish) individual MoM percentage-change forecast for Existing Home Sales in the Reuters poll, anchoring the downside of the distribution.
pUSEHSP=L.how_to_use: A realised MoM change below pUSEHSP=L is a tail shock in rate-of-change space; alongside pUSEHSP=H it defines the analyst forecast range, useful for setting option strikes or scenario-weighting macro models.

pUSEHSP=H.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Max Forecast
pUSEHSP=H.meaning: Maximum (most bullish) individual MoM percentage-change forecast for Existing Home Sales in the Reuters poll, anchoring the upside of the distribution.
pUSEHSP=H.how_to_use: A print above pUSEHSP=H in % change terms implies the NAR release was a strong tail beat; cross-reference with USEHS=ECI level to ensure the % surprise is not purely a base-effect or prior-month revision artefact.

pUSEHSP=T.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSEHSP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of the Existing Home Sales MoM percentage-change forecasts submitted to the Reuters poll, measuring dispersion in rate-of-change expectations.
pUSEHSP=T.how_to_use: High pUSEHSP=T alongside high pUSEHS=T signals broad uncertainty across both level and momentum dimensions; this regime calls for wider event-risk buffers on real-estate and mortgage-sensitive positions around the NAR release.

pUSEHSP=C.description: Exist. Home Sales % Chg — Number of Forecasters
pUSEHSP=C.meaning: Number of analysts who submitted Existing Home Sales MoM percentage-change forecasts in the current Reuters poll round, indicating participation depth for this derivative series.
pUSEHSP=C.how_to_use: Compare pUSEHSP=C with pUSEHS=C; materially fewer submissions for % change than for the level implies some analysts only provide level estimates—the % change consensus is then thinner and should be interpreted with more caution.

USEHS=ECI.meaning: Realised monthly Existing Home Sales as reported by the National Association of Realtors (NAR), released around the 20th–25th of the following month. Represents roughly 90% of total US home sales and reflects conditions in the existing housing stock.
USEHS=ECI.how_to_use: Use as the benchmark to evaluate poll accuracy (vs pUSEHS=M); sustained weakness in USEHS=ECI relative to expectations signals affordability constraints from mortgage rates and can lead housing-sensitive equity sectors.
