pUSEHS=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for Existing Home Sales from the Reuters pre-release poll, representing the midpoint of analyst expectations for the NAR release.
pUSEHS=M.how_to_use: Surprises vs pUSEHS=M of ±100k units typically move mortgage-REIT spreads and real-estate sector ETFs; combine with the percentage-change companion (pUSEHSP=M) to contextualise the magnitude of the miss or beat.

pUSEHS=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based point forecast for Existing Home Sales, providing a systematic quantitative estimate that can differ materially from the analyst panel consensus.
pUSEHS=F.how_to_use: Compare pUSEHS=F against pUSEHS=M; when the model is significantly higher (lower) than consensus, check pUSEHS=P (Predicted Surprise) to confirm directionality and use as a pre-release positioning signal.

pUSEHS=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for Existing Home Sales, the signed difference between the SmartEconomics model forecast (pUSEHS=F) and the analyst consensus (pUSEHS=M). Positive values mean the model expects an upside surprise.
pUSEHS=P.how_to_use: High positive pUSEHS=P ahead of an NAR release, combined with tight StdDev (pUSEHS=T), is a high-conviction setup for long housing exposure; negative pUSEHS=P warns of downside risk despite sanguine consensus.

pUSEHS=E.meaning: Mean (average) of all individual Existing Home Sales forecasts from Reuters poll participants, sensitive to extreme high or low outlier submissions.
pUSEHS=E.how_to_use: When pUSEHS=E exceeds pUSEHS=M, optimistic outliers are pulling the average up—monitor whether those outliers are consistently correct to decide how much weight to give the mean vs median.

pUSEHS=O.meaning: Mode of Existing Home Sales forecasts—the most commonly submitted estimate in the Reuters poll—indicating where analyst clustering is strongest.
pUSEHS=O.how_to_use: A mode-median gap in Existing Home Sales is often driven by round-number anchoring (e.g., 4.0M vs 4.05M) and may slightly distort median signal; check against pUSEHS=T for full uncertainty context.

pUSEHS=L.meaning: Minimum individual Existing Home Sales forecast in the Reuters poll, anchoring the bearish end of the analyst distribution ahead of the NAR release.
pUSEHS=L.how_to_use: A realised print below pUSEHS=L indicates a full tail-miss; this threshold, alongside pUSEHS=H, establishes a hard bound for scenario analysis and option-strike selection on housing-related instruments.

pUSEHS=H.meaning: Maximum individual Existing Home Sales forecast in the Reuters poll, anchoring the bullish end of the analyst distribution ahead of the NAR release.
pUSEHS=H.how_to_use: A print above pUSEHS=H represents an extreme upside shock for the existing housing market; the H-L range expressed as a percentage of pUSEHS=M provides a normalised uncertainty metric for cross-indicator comparison.

pUSEHS=T.description: Existing Home Sales — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSEHS=T.meaning: Standard deviation of Existing Home Sales forecasts across all Reuters poll participants, measuring dispersion of analyst views ahead of the NAR release.
pUSEHS=T.how_to_use: Elevated pUSEHS=T typically coincides with uncertain mortgage-rate trajectories; use to scale stop-losses on housing-sensitive positions and compare alongside pUSHST=T and pUSBPE=T for a cross-sector uncertainty heatmap.

pUSEHS=C.description: Existing Home Sales — Number of Forecasters
pUSEHS=C.meaning: Number of analysts who submitted Existing Home Sales forecasts in the current Reuters poll round, providing a gauge of survey participation depth.
pUSEHS=C.how_to_use: Low participation months reduce median reliability; pair with pUSHST=C and pUSBPE=C to identify quarters where the entire housing poll complex is thinly covered, warranting wider uncertainty bands across all three indicators.

USEXP=ECI.meaning: Actual month-over-month change in US Export Prices from the BLS, measuring price competitiveness of US goods in global markets and the terms-of-trade dynamics.
USEXP=ECI.how_to_use: Compare to pUSEXP=M for the surprise; rising export prices can improve the terms of trade and narrow the nominal trade deficit, but may also signal lost competitiveness if driven by USD strength rather than demand.

pUSEXP=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for US Export Prices month-over-month from the Reuters poll, the central market expectation ahead of the BLS mid-month release.
pUSEXP=M.how_to_use: Pair with pUSIMP=M to track expected terms-of-trade shifts; when export price expectations diverge from import price expectations, it signals a changing relative-price dynamic with FX and sector implications.

pUSEXP=F.meaning: SmartEconomics algorithmic forecast for US Export Prices MoM, providing a model-derived estimate that draws on commodity prices and USD index data.
pUSEXP=F.how_to_use: Divergence from pUSEXP=M signals where commodity and FX models diverge from human analyst consensus; relevant when agricultural or energy export prices are moving sharply.

pUSEXP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for US Export Prices MoM — the systematic expected deviation of the actual from the Reuters median consensus.
pUSEXP=P.how_to_use: Use alongside pUSIMP=P to assess whether import and export price surprises are expected to move in the same or opposite direction, which has different implications for the trade balance and terms of trade.

pUSEXP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for US Export Prices MoM across all Reuters poll respondents, sensitive to outlier views on agricultural commodity or energy price trajectories.
pUSEXP=E.how_to_use: A mean notably above the median suggests a right-skewed distribution driven by a subset of forecasters pricing in commodity-export price spikes; relevant for agri-commodity and energy-sector positioning.

pUSEXP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for US Export Prices MoM — the most frequently submitted individual estimate in the Reuters economist panel.
pUSEXP=O.how_to_use: A mode equal to the median confirms a unimodal, consensus-aligned distribution; deviation implies bifurcated views on export-price drivers such as grain or LNG pricing.

pUSEXP=L.meaning: Minimum forecast for US Export Prices MoM in the Reuters poll, representing the most deflationary individual estimate in the panel.
pUSEXP=L.how_to_use: Use with pUSEXP=H to bound the distribution of outcomes; an actual print below the floor signals unexpected export deflation, potentially from USD appreciation or weak global demand.

pUSEXP=H.meaning: Maximum forecast for US Export Prices MoM in the Reuters poll, representing the most inflationary individual estimate in the panel.
pUSEXP=H.how_to_use: The H-L range captures the full spectrum of economist views on global price conditions; a wide range relative to pUSEXP=T indicates distribution tails may be driven by commodity-price outliers.

pUSEXP=T.description: Export Prices MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSEXP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for US Export Prices MoM in the Reuters poll, a direct measure of uncertainty about near-term export-price dynamics.
pUSEXP=T.how_to_use: Compare with pUSIMP=T: when export-price standard deviation is low but import-price standard deviation is high, terms-of-trade uncertainty is dominated by import-side risk, e.g., from tariff uncertainty.

pUSEXP=C.description: Export Prices MM — Number of Forecasters
pUSEXP=C.meaning: Number of economists participating in the Reuters US Export Prices MoM poll for the current release cycle.
pUSEXP=C.how_to_use: A smaller panel for export prices (vs. trade balance) is common; track to ensure the median is statistically meaningful before using it as an event benchmark.

USGDEF=ECI.meaning: Actual monthly US Federal Budget surplus or deficit from the Treasury Monthly Statement, released ~10th of the following month. Negative values indicate a deficit; large monthly deficits typically occur in April and September.
USGDEF=ECI.how_to_use: Compare against the Reuters poll median (pUSGDEF=M) for the surprise; cumulative fiscal-year deficits relative to CBO projections drive Treasury supply forecasts and term-premium dynamics in the long end.

pUSGDEF=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for the monthly US Federal Budget balance from the Reuters poll, the central market expectation before the Treasury Monthly Statement.
pUSGDEF=M.how_to_use: Budget surprises are driven by tax receipt timing and outlay volatility; a materially narrower-than-expected deficit can temporarily reduce Treasury issuance expectations and compress long-end yields.

pUSGDEF=F.meaning: SmartEconomics algorithmic forecast for the monthly US Federal Budget balance, using high-frequency Treasury cash-flow data to estimate the official monthly figure.
pUSGDEF=F.how_to_use: SmartEcon has an advantage on the federal budget because Treasury publishes daily cash data (Daily Treasury Statement); divergence from pUSGDEF=M often reflects the model incorporating recent DTS flows that human forecasters have not updated.

pUSGDEF=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the US Federal Budget — the systematic expected deviation between the actual monthly balance and the Reuters median forecast.
pUSGDEF=P.how_to_use: Combine with pUSGDEF=T: a large positive predicted surprise (surplus beat) alongside low standard deviation gives high-conviction signal for Treasury market positioning ahead of the release.

pUSGDEF=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the monthly US Federal Budget balance across all Reuters poll respondents, potentially skewed by outlier estimates around large tax-receipt months.
pUSGDEF=E.how_to_use: When the mean is materially more negative (larger deficit) than the median, a subset of forecasters is pricing in unusual outlays or lower-than-typical receipts; relevant for tail-risk assessment in duration-sensitive portfolios.

pUSGDEF=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the monthly US Federal Budget balance — the single most commonly submitted estimate among Reuters panel economists.
pUSGDEF=O.how_to_use: A mode clustered far from the median suggests genuinely bifurcated fiscal views, perhaps around whether a month's tax receipts will be above or below trend; cross-reference with Daily Treasury Statement data.

pUSGDEF=L.meaning: Minimum (most bearish / largest-deficit) forecast for the monthly US Federal Budget balance in the Reuters poll.
pUSGDEF=L.how_to_use: Use with pUSGDEF=H to frame the full range of fiscal outcomes; an actual print below this floor — implying a larger-than-expected deficit — could steepen the yield curve by raising near-term Treasury supply concerns.

pUSGDEF=H.meaning: Maximum (most bullish / smallest-deficit or largest-surplus) forecast for the monthly US Federal Budget balance in the Reuters poll.
pUSGDEF=H.how_to_use: The H-L range is typically wide for the federal budget given timing uncertainty of large outlays; a narrow range signals unusually high forecaster consensus and makes surprises outside the band more impactful for rates.

pUSGDEF=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the monthly US Federal Budget balance in the Reuters poll, measuring economist disagreement about the fiscal position.
pUSGDEF=T.how_to_use: Federal budget standard deviations are typically large (often $20-40B) due to timing of corporate tax receipts; compare across months — April (tax season) and September (fiscal year-end) carry the highest forecast uncertainty.

pUSGDEF=C.meaning: Number of economists participating in the Reuters US Federal Budget poll for the current release cycle.
pUSGDEF=C.how_to_use: Track alongside pUSGDEF=T: a low forecaster count with high standard deviation renders the consensus statistically unreliable; in such months, the SmartEcon forecast (pUSGDEF=F) based on DTS data may be more actionable.

USFBT=ECI.meaning: Actual monthly net foreign purchases of US Treasury bonds from the Treasury International Capital (TIC) report, released with a ~6-week lag. Positive values indicate net foreign buying; negative values indicate net selling.
USFBT=ECI.how_to_use: Monitor for sustained shifts in foreign appetite for Treasuries — large net selling episodes (especially by official holders) can pressure long-end yields; use alongside USNCI=ECI for the full cross-border capital picture.

USGDPP=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the US GDP Second (Preliminary) Estimate — the BEA's revision published ~60 days after quarter-end, incorporating fuller source data than the Advance.
USGDPP=ECI.how_to_use: Market impact is typically smaller than the Advance unless the revision is large. Compare to the Advance (USGDPA=ECI) to track revision direction; persistent upward revisions signal data momentum.

pUSGDPP=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the US GDP Second Estimate from the Reuters economist poll. By this vintage, most income and spending source data are available so consensus is typically tighter.
pUSGDPP=M.how_to_use: Since the 2nd Estimate revises the Advance, analysts compare pUSGDPP=M to the prior Advance print (USGDPA=ECI) — a rising median implies expected upward revision, which is bullish for risk assets.

pUSGDPP=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the GDP Second Estimate — an algorithm-driven nowcast produced independently of the surveyed economist panel.
pUSGDPP=F.how_to_use: Compare to pUSGDPP=M: when SmartEconomics diverges materially from the survey median at the 2nd Estimate stage (where data are richer), it may signal a pending revision surprise.

pUSGDPP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Second Estimate — directional signal indicating expected beat or miss versus the consensus median, based on Refinitiv's pre-release model.
pUSGDPP=P.how_to_use: Since 2nd Estimate surprises are typically smaller than Advance surprises, a non-zero Predicted Surprise here is informative. Use alongside pUSGDPP=T to judge magnitude vs uncertainty.

pUSGDPP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the US GDP Second Estimate, arithmetic average across all economists in the Reuters poll. Sensitive to outlier submissions compared to the median.
pUSGDPP=E.how_to_use: Mean-median comparison reveals skew in the 2nd Estimate consensus. At the preliminary stage, richer data availability tends to compress mean-median spreads versus the Advance poll.

pUSGDPP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Second Estimate — the most frequently submitted point estimate among surveyed economists, indicating where forecasters cluster most densely.
pUSGDPP=O.how_to_use: A mode matching the median signals a symmetric, concentrated consensus; divergence implies bimodal views. Useful for assessing options strike density around growth scenarios.

pUSGDPP=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) single forecast for the GDP Second Estimate — the bear case boundary in the Reuters economist survey.
pUSGDPP=L.how_to_use: Track whether the bear case for the 2nd Estimate is more extreme than for the Advance; a widening downside tail suggests lingering uncertainty about the quarter's data quality.

pUSGDPP=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) single forecast for the GDP Second Estimate — the bull case boundary in the Reuters economist survey.
pUSGDPP=H.how_to_use: If the actual 2nd Estimate (USGDPP=ECI) exceeds the Max, it is an outsized upside surprise. Narrowing Max-Min range from Advance to 2nd Estimate indicates consensus convergence as data availability improves.

pUSGDPP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of individual forecasts for the GDP Second Estimate — measures economist disagreement at the preliminary revision stage.
pUSGDPP=T.how_to_use: StdDev for the 2nd Estimate is typically lower than the Advance as more data is in hand. A 2nd Estimate StdDev that remains high suggests unusual underlying data uncertainty even after the first revision.

pUSGDPP=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting forecasts for the GDP Second Estimate in the Reuters poll — sample size for the 2nd Estimate consensus statistics.
pUSGDPP=C.how_to_use: Compare count to the Advance poll (pUSGDPA=C) — a material drop signals reduced analyst engagement with the revision release, which can inflate the apparent surprise effect.

USGDPA=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the US GDP Advance Estimate (QoQ annualized) — the BEA's first estimate of quarterly GDP, published ~30 days after quarter-end. This is the market-moving print against which all poll forecasts are measured.
USGDPA=ECI.how_to_use: Compare to pUSGDPA=M (Median Consensus) to calculate the surprise. A beat or miss drives 5-10 bp Treasury moves intraday. Track across vintages (Advance → 2nd → Final) to measure revision bias.

pUSGDPA=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the US GDP Advance Estimate, aggregated from Reuters' poll of ~70-80 Wall Street economists ~1 week before release. The median is the single most-cited 'street consensus' figure.
pUSGDPA=M.how_to_use: The baseline 'expected' GDP — markets trade the surprise (Actual minus Median). When median and mean (pUSGDPA=E) diverge, the forecast distribution is skewed, signalling asymmetric risk around the print.

pUSGDPA=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics proprietary model forecast for the GDP Advance Estimate — an algorithm-based nowcast blending high-frequency data, rather than a surveyed economist opinion.
pUSGDPA=F.how_to_use: Compare SmartEconomics to the human-poll median (pUSGDPA=M) to detect model-vs-consensus divergence. A persistent SmartEconomics edge vs median can signal where the surprise lands.

pUSGDPA=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Advance Estimate — Refinitiv's directional signal indicating whether the actual print is expected to beat or miss the median consensus and by how much.
pUSGDPA=P.how_to_use: Use as a pre-release directional bias overlay. A positive Predicted Surprise alongside a high StdDev (pUSGDPA=T) implies a potential upside catalyst with wide uncertainty bounds.

pUSGDPA=E.meaning: Mean (arithmetic average) forecast for the GDP Advance Estimate across all surveyed economists. The mean is sensitive to outlier forecasts unlike the median.
pUSGDPA=E.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median (pUSGDPA=M): a mean above the median signals a positive skew (some bulls pulling the average up), below implies a negative tail. Helps traders gauge distribution shape.

pUSGDPA=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Advance Estimate — the single most common point estimate submitted by economists in the Reuters survey.
pUSGDPA=O.how_to_use: When mode equals median, economist views are tightly clustered at a round number; when they diverge, the distribution is bimodal. Useful for options traders assessing probability mass at specific growth rates.

pUSGDPA=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) individual forecast for the GDP Advance Estimate from all economists surveyed — the bear case boundary of the forecast distribution.
pUSGDPA=L.how_to_use: Defines the lower tail of consensus. Pair with Max (pUSGDPA=H) to set the full forecast range; an unusually wide Min-Max spread reflects heightened macro uncertainty around the quarter.

pUSGDPA=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) individual forecast for the GDP Advance Estimate — the bull case boundary of the economist survey distribution.
pUSGDPA=H.how_to_use: Defines the upper tail; if the actual print (USGDPA=ECI) exceeds the Max, it constitutes a consensus-busting surprise. Track the Max-Min range over time as a forward-looking uncertainty gauge.

pUSGDPA=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for the GDP Advance Estimate — measures the degree of disagreement among surveyed Wall Street economists.
pUSGDPA=T.how_to_use: Higher StdDev signals greater uncertainty and typically leads to larger market moves on release. Compare across quarters — a rising StdDev warns that consensus is fragmenting ahead of a difficult-to-forecast print.

pUSGDPA=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted forecasts for the GDP Advance Estimate in the Reuters poll — the sample size underpinning the consensus statistics.
pUSGDPA=C.how_to_use: A count below ~40 means consensus statistics are less reliable; above ~70 indicates a robust survey. Check for sudden drops in count as a sign of reduced analyst coverage ahead of an uncertain release.

USDGEA=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the GDP Chain-Type Price Index (Deflator) Advance Estimate — the BEA's broadest inflation measure covering all goods and services in GDP, released ~30 days after quarter-end.
USDGEA=ECI.how_to_use: The GDP Deflator is broader than CPI or PCE; a surprise versus pUSDGEA=M signals unexpected inflationary or deflationary pressure across the full economy, relevant to Fed policy discussions.

pUSDGEA=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate — the street's aggregate expectation for the broadest quarterly US inflation measure.
pUSDGEA=M.how_to_use: Compare to the actual (USDGEA=ECI) for a broad inflation surprise. A Deflator beat alongside a GDP beat is a stagflation-lite signal; a miss with a GDP beat is goldilocks — growth without inflation.

pUSDGEA=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate — an algorithm-based projection of broad quarterly inflation.
pUSDGEA=F.how_to_use: When SmartEconomics diverges from the Deflator consensus median, it often reflects real-time commodity or import price data not yet fully incorporated by surveyed economists.

pUSDGEA=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate — directional signal indicating whether the broad price index will beat or miss consensus.
pUSDGEA=P.how_to_use: A hawkish Predicted Surprise (upside deflator beat expected) reinforces the case for Fed tightening. Compare with PCE deflator Predicted Surprises for consistency across inflation gauges.

pUSDGEA=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate across all economists in the Reuters poll — the arithmetic average of submitted inflation forecasts.
pUSDGEA=E.how_to_use: Mean-median divergence for the Deflator indicates skewed inflation views. If the mean exceeds the median, some economists expect an inflation overshoot — relevant for assessing TIPS breakeven fair value.

pUSDGEA=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate — the most common inflation expectation point estimate submitted by economists in the Reuters survey.
pUSDGEA=O.how_to_use: A mode at a round number (e.g., 2.0%) for the Deflator signals strong consensus anchoring around a particular inflation rate, which can suppress implied volatility in inflation-linked instruments.

pUSDGEA=L.meaning: Minimum (most dovish) forecast for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate — the lowest inflation expectation in the Reuters survey.
pUSDGEA=L.how_to_use: The Min Deflator forecast anchors the disinflationary scenario. A print at or below Min signals an unexpected deflation pulse, which would typically rally Treasuries and compress real yields.

pUSDGEA=H.meaning: Maximum (most hawkish) forecast for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate — the highest inflation expectation among all economists in the Reuters survey.
pUSDGEA=H.how_to_use: A print above the Max is a significant inflation shock, likely triggering repricing of Fed rate expectations. Max-Min spread narrows during anchored inflation regimes and widens during supply shocks.

pUSDGEA=T.description: GDP Deflator Advance — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSDGEA=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the GDP Deflator Advance Estimate — gauge of economist disagreement about quarterly broad inflation.
pUSDGEA=T.how_to_use: Rising Deflator StdDev signals analyst uncertainty about the inflation regime, typically during commodity price volatility or supply-chain disruptions. Elevated StdDev amplifies the market impact of the actual print.

pUSDGEA=C.description: GDP Deflator Advance — Number of Forecasters
pUSDGEA=C.meaning: Number of economists providing GDP Deflator Advance forecasts in the Reuters poll — sample size underpinning the Deflator consensus statistics.
pUSDGEA=C.how_to_use: The Deflator is polled alongside the GDP Advance but typically draws fewer responses; a low count reduces the statistical robustness of the median and StdDev and should be noted in research.

USDGEF=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the GDP Chain-Type Price Index Final Estimate — the BEA's definitive broad inflation measure for the quarter, released ~90 days after quarter-end.
USDGEF=ECI.how_to_use: Use the final Deflator print to benchmark the inflation environment for the full quarter. Compare all three vintages (Advance, Prelim, Final) to assess whether BEA had a systematic bias in initial price estimates.

pUSDGEF=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate — the street's expected definitive quarterly broad inflation reading.
pUSDGEF=M.how_to_use: By the Final stage, surprises vs median are rare. A significant surprise here typically reflects a BEA methodological revision rather than new economic data. Use as the closing benchmark for quarterly inflation analysis.

pUSDGEF=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate — the definitive algorithmic inflation estimate with access to all quarterly source data.
pUSDGEF=F.how_to_use: At the Final stage, SmartEconomics and human consensus (pUSDGEF=M) should converge. Persistent divergence may suggest SmartEconomics uses a different chain-weighting methodology assumption.

pUSDGEF=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate — a directional signal for whether the definitive broad inflation print will beat or miss the median consensus.
pUSDGEF=P.how_to_use: A non-zero Predicted Surprise at the Deflator Final stage is notable and should prompt investigation of whether BEA has issued any advance signals about methodology changes or data revisions.

pUSDGEF=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate across all economists in the Reuters poll — arithmetic average of all submitted definitive inflation forecasts.
pUSDGEF=E.how_to_use: Mean-median convergence at the Final stage confirms a tight, symmetric consensus. Any residual divergence at this stage highlights outlier models with non-standard price deflator assumptions.

pUSDGEF=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate — the most frequently submitted single inflation estimate at the definitive revision stage.
pUSDGEF=O.how_to_use: Mode alignment with median confirms consensus certainty about the final quarterly inflation number. Used in academic studies comparing forecast accuracy across the three deflator vintages.

pUSDGEF=L.meaning: Minimum (most dovish) forecast for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate — the lower bound of the inflation distribution at the definitive BEA release.
pUSDGEF=L.how_to_use: The Min at the Final stage should be tighter than the Advance Min. A print below the Final Min implies a methodology-driven downward revision to prices, which can temporarily flatten the yield curve.

pUSDGEF=H.meaning: Maximum (most hawkish) forecast for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate — the ceiling of inflation expectations at the definitive revision stage.
pUSDGEF=H.how_to_use: A print above the Final Max for the Deflator would be an exceptional upside inflation surprise at the definitive stage, warranting immediate reassessment of the real rate environment.

pUSDGEF=T.description: GDP Deflator Final — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSDGEF=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the GDP Deflator Final Estimate — measures the residual economist disagreement about the definitive quarterly broad inflation rate.
pUSDGEF=T.how_to_use: Final-stage Deflator StdDev should be the lowest of the three vintages. Elevated Final StdDev signals structural disagreement about the price index methodology, not just the data — important for real GDP decomposition.

pUSDGEF=C.description: GDP Deflator Final — Number of Forecasters
pUSDGEF=C.meaning: Number of economists providing GDP Deflator Final forecasts in the Reuters poll — the sample size for the definitive inflation consensus.
pUSDGEF=C.how_to_use: The Final Deflator poll draws the fewest respondents of the three vintages. A very low count (below 30) makes the median and StdDev highly sensitive to individual outlier submissions.

USDGEP=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the GDP Chain-Type Price Index Preliminary Estimate — the BEA's second vintage of the broad inflation measure, released ~60 days after quarter-end.
USDGEP=ECI.how_to_use: Track the Advance-to-Prelim revision for the Deflator (USDGEA=ECI vs USDGEP=ECI). An upward revision at the Prelim stage is a hawkish signal, as the broadest inflation gauge is running hotter than initially estimated.

pUSDGEP=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate — the street's expected revision to quarterly broad inflation at the second-vintage stage.
pUSDGEP=M.how_to_use: Compare to the Advance actual (USDGEA=ECI): median above the prior print signals expected upward inflation revision. A hawkish revision here may reinforce Fed communication ahead of the next FOMC meeting.

pUSDGEP=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate — algorithmic nowcast of the revised broad inflation figure.
pUSDGEP=F.how_to_use: At the Prelim stage, SmartEconomics has access to full monthly price indices. A persistent divergence from pUSDGEP=M may reflect different methodological treatments of hedonic price adjustments.

pUSDGEP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate — directional signal for whether the revised broad inflation print will beat or miss consensus.
pUSDGEP=P.how_to_use: A hawkish Predicted Surprise at the Deflator Prelim (upside beat expected) compounds Fed tightening risk if the 2nd GDP Estimate is also expected to beat, reinforcing a nominal overheating narrative.

pUSDGEP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate across all economists in the Reuters poll.
pUSDGEP=E.how_to_use: Mean-median comparison for the Deflator Prelim reveals whether outlier hawkish or dovish inflation views are distorting the distribution. Important context for rates traders watching for inflation tail risks.

pUSDGEP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate — the most common single inflation estimate submitted by economists at the second-vintage stage.
pUSDGEP=O.how_to_use: Mode alignment with median at the Prelim stage confirms that the central inflation view is symmetric and well-anchored. Use as part of qualitative consensus assessment.

pUSDGEP=L.meaning: Minimum (most dovish) forecast for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate — the lowest inflation expectation in the Reuters survey for this vintage.
pUSDGEP=L.how_to_use: If the Prelim Deflator actual comes in at or below the survey minimum, it signals a significant disinflationary development that may shift market pricing toward rate cuts.

pUSDGEP=H.meaning: Maximum (most hawkish) forecast for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate — the highest inflation expectation in the Reuters survey at the second-vintage stage.
pUSDGEP=H.how_to_use: Max narrows from Advance to Prelim as more data arrives. A widening Max at the Prelim stage is unusual and suggests a specific data source (e.g., energy prices, import prices) is introducing fresh inflation uncertainty.

pUSDGEP=T.description: GDP Deflator Prelim — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSDGEP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the GDP Deflator Preliminary Estimate — measures residual analyst disagreement about broad quarterly inflation.
pUSDGEP=T.how_to_use: Deflator Prelim StdDev should narrow versus the Advance. If it does not, energy or commodity price data since the Advance release is injecting new inflation uncertainty — a signal to monitor TIPS vol.

pUSDGEP=C.description: GDP Deflator Prelim — Number of Forecasters
pUSDGEP=C.meaning: Number of economists providing GDP Deflator Preliminary forecasts in the Reuters poll — the sample size for this second-vintage inflation consensus.
pUSDGEP=C.how_to_use: Count typically declines from the Advance to Prelim Deflator poll as fewer economists formally re-forecast. A thin count should be flagged as a caveat on any consensus-based inflation view.

USGFSA=ECI.meaning: Actual release of Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (GDP Sales) Advance Estimate — GDP excluding the change in private inventories. Released simultaneously with the GDP Advance, ~30 days after quarter-end.
USGFSA=ECI.how_to_use: GDP Sales strips out inventory swings, making it a cleaner read on underlying demand. When GDP Sales and GDP diverge, the gap is inventory accumulation or drawdown — a key signal for the next quarter's growth outlook.

pUSGFSA=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate from the Reuters economist poll. Reflects the street's expectation of demand-side GDP growth excluding inventory effects.
pUSGFSA=M.how_to_use: Compare pUSGFSA=M vs pUSGDPA=M: a significantly lower GDP Sales consensus implies inventories are expected to flatter the headline GDP number. The Sales surprise (Actual minus pUSGFSA=M) is a purer demand signal.

pUSGFSA=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate — an algorithm-based nowcast of real final sales excluding inventory change.
pUSGFSA=F.how_to_use: When SmartEconomics diverges from the median on GDP Sales specifically (vs GDP), it signals disagreement on the inventory component, which is often the least predictable sub-component.

pUSGFSA=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate — directional pre-release signal for whether final sales will beat or miss the consensus median.
pUSGFSA=P.how_to_use: A divergence between the GDP Predicted Surprise (pUSGDPA=P) and the GDP Sales Predicted Surprise here implies the surprise is expected to come from the inventory component, not underlying demand.

pUSGFSA=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate, averaging across all economists in the Reuters survey. Captures the full distribution of views on final demand growth.
pUSGFSA=E.how_to_use: Mean-median spread indicates distribution skew for the Sales forecast. A negative skew (mean below median) suggests some economists anticipate a soft final-demand quarter regardless of headline GDP.

pUSGFSA=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate — the most common single point estimate submitted by economists surveyed by Reuters.
pUSGFSA=O.how_to_use: Useful when analysts want to know the most 'expected' single number rather than the central tendency; for GDP Sales, the mode is often a round number reflecting inventory-adjusted growth views.

pUSGFSA=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) forecast for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate — the bear case for underlying demand in the quarter.
pUSGFSA=L.how_to_use: If the actual GDP Sales (USGFSA=ECI) falls below the Min, final demand came in worse than the worst-case economist estimate — a rare but powerful recession warning signal.

pUSGFSA=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) forecast for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate — the bull case for final domestic demand in the Reuters poll.
pUSGFSA=H.how_to_use: Serves as the upper bound for a demand-driven growth scenario. A print above the Max on GDP Sales, paired with a GDP beat, confirms genuine demand strength rather than inventory-led growth.

pUSGFSA=T.description: GDP Sales Advance — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSGFSA=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the GDP Sales Advance Estimate — gauge of economist disagreement about the underlying demand component of GDP.
pUSGFSA=T.how_to_use: A high GDP Sales StdDev even when GDP StdDev is low implies uncertainty is concentrated in the final-demand component rather than inventories. Compare vintages to see if demand uncertainty is resolving.

pUSGFSA=C.description: GDP Sales Advance — Number of Forecasters
pUSGFSA=C.meaning: Number of economists providing GDP Sales Advance forecasts in the Reuters poll — the sample size for the GDP Sales Advance consensus.
pUSGFSA=C.how_to_use: GDP Sales is less followed than headline GDP; a significantly lower count vs the GDP Advance poll (pUSGDPA=C) means the Sales consensus is thinner and individual outliers have more weight.

USGFSP=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the Real Final Sales Preliminary Estimate — the 2nd-vintage revision of GDP excluding inventories, published ~60 days after quarter-end alongside the GDP 2nd Estimate.
USGFSP=ECI.how_to_use: Track the revision from Advance (USGFSA=ECI) to Prelim — persistent upward revisions to final sales confirm demand was better than initially measured, supporting a positive revision to the headline GDP outlook.

pUSGFSP=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate from the Reuters economist poll — the street's expected revision to final domestic demand.
pUSGFSP=M.how_to_use: Compare to the prior Advance actual (USGFSA=ECI): median above the Advance signals expected upward demand revision, which reduces concern that earlier growth was inventory-driven.

pUSGFSP=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate — algorithm-based estimate of the revised final-sales figure.
pUSGFSP=F.how_to_use: SmartEconomics at the prelim stage has access to fuller monthly source data. A divergence from pUSGFSP=M here is more informative than at the Advance stage.

pUSGFSP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate — pre-release directional signal for the revision to final domestic demand.
pUSGFSP=P.how_to_use: When the GDP 2nd Estimate Predicted Surprise (pUSGDPP=P) and GDP Sales Predicted Surprise diverge, the expected surprise is inventory-driven. Use to assess whether a GDP beat will be demand-based or not.

pUSGFSP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate across all economists in the Reuters poll. Reflects the average view on final demand at the second-vintage stage.
pUSGFSP=E.how_to_use: Mean-median spread at the prelim stage is informative about outlier views. If the mean is pulling well above the median, some economists expect a strong upward revision to final sales.

pUSGFSP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate — the most commonly submitted single point estimate by economists in the Reuters survey.
pUSGFSP=O.how_to_use: Mode convergence with the median at the prelim stage (more data available) indicates high consensus certainty. A gap between mode and median suggests bimodal views on the revision direction.

pUSGFSP=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) forecast for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate — the bear case for the revised final-demand figure.
pUSGFSP=L.how_to_use: If the actual Prelim GDP Sales prints at or below the Min forecast, demand was significantly weaker than any surveyed economist expected — a macro warning sign worth flagging alongside retail and PCE data.

pUSGFSP=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) forecast for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate — the upper boundary of surveyed expectations for revised final domestic demand.
pUSGFSP=H.how_to_use: Tracks how bullish the most optimistic economist is on demand. Narrowing Max-Min range from Advance to Prelim is normal as data quality improves; a widening range is unusual and signals model uncertainty.

pUSGFSP=T.description: GDP Sales Prelim — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSGFSP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate — measures the spread of economist views on revised final domestic demand.
pUSGFSP=T.how_to_use: Compare to the Advance StdDev (pUSGFSA=T): StdDev should narrow at the Prelim stage as more monthly data is available. If it fails to narrow, analyst uncertainty about demand remains elevated.

pUSGFSP=C.description: GDP Sales Prelim — Number of Forecasters
pUSGFSP=C.meaning: Number of economists providing forecasts for the GDP Sales Preliminary Estimate in the Reuters poll.
pUSGFSP=C.how_to_use: A low respondent count relative to the GDP poll (pUSGDPP=C) indicates the GDP Sales Prelim is a less-followed release; thin coverage means the median consensus is less reliable.

USHST=ECI.meaning: Realised monthly Housing Starts reported by Census/HUD, measuring the annualised number of new residential construction projects begun in the period. Typically released around the 16th–19th of the following month and subject to revision.
USHST=ECI.how_to_use: Use as the benchmark to score prior poll consensus accuracy; compare USHST=ECI against pUSHST=M to track systematic forecast bias. Persistent beats/misses signal turning points in the residential construction cycle.

pUSHST=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for US Housing Starts from the Reuters poll conducted roughly one week before the Census/HUD release. The median is the central tendency of all individual analyst submissions.
pUSHST=M.how_to_use: Markets compare actual vs median; a surprise >50k units often moves homebuilder stocks and mortgage-rate expectations. Pair with permits (pUSBPE=M, forward-looking) and existing home sales (pUSEHS=M, current stock) for a full housing-cycle read.

pUSHST=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based point forecast for Housing Starts, generated by Reuters' quantitative forecasting engine ahead of the release. Provides a data-driven alternative to the survey median.
pUSHST=F.how_to_use: Divergence between pUSHST=F and pUSHST=M signals that the model sees information the panel has not yet priced; track pUSHST=P (Predicted Surprise) alongside this to assess directional risk.

pUSHST=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for Housing Starts, quantifying how much the SmartEconomics forecast (pUSHST=F) deviates from the current analyst consensus (pUSHST=M). A positive value indicates the model expects an upside print.
pUSHST=P.how_to_use: Use as a pre-release directional signal; a large positive Predicted Surprise alongside a wide StdDev (pUSHST=T) points to elevated upside risk and justifies asymmetric positioning in rate-sensitive sectors.

pUSHST=E.meaning: Mean (arithmetic average) of all individual Housing Starts forecasts submitted to the Reuters poll. The mean is more sensitive to outlier estimates than the median and can reveal skew in analyst expectations.
pUSHST=E.how_to_use: Compare pUSHST=E vs pUSHST=M: if mean > median the distribution is right-skewed (bullish tail); use alongside pUSHST=L/H to gauge the full range of analyst conviction.

pUSHST=O.meaning: Mode (most frequently submitted value) of Housing Starts forecasts in the Reuters poll, representing the single point-estimate shared by the largest cluster of analysts.
pUSHST=O.how_to_use: When mode equals median the consensus is tightly clustered; a large gap between pUSHST=O and pUSHST=M reveals bimodal analyst disagreement that median alone would mask.

pUSHST=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) individual Housing Starts forecast submitted in the Reuters poll, representing the bear-case anchor of the distribution.
pUSHST=L.how_to_use: Use pUSHST=L and pUSHST=H together to set the option-implied range; if the actual release falls below pUSHST=L it constitutes a true tail shock and warrants reassessing the macro housing view.

pUSHST=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) individual Housing Starts forecast submitted in the Reuters poll, representing the bull-case anchor of the distribution.
pUSHST=H.how_to_use: A print above pUSHST=H is an extreme upside shock; the L-to-H range relative to consensus indicates how much uncertainty remains in the construction pipeline heading into the release.

pUSHST=T.description: Housing Starts Number — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSHST=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual Housing Starts forecasts in the Reuters poll, measuring the spread of analyst uncertainty around the consensus.
pUSHST=T.how_to_use: Elevated StdDev ahead of the release suggests higher headline risk; calibrate stop-loss widths or options vol positioning on homebuilder names when pUSHST=T is in the upper quartile of its historical range.

pUSHST=C.description: Housing Starts Number — Number of Forecasters
pUSHST=C.meaning: Count of individual analysts who submitted Housing Starts forecasts in the current Reuters poll round, indicating the breadth and statistical reliability of the consensus.
pUSHST=C.how_to_use: Low forecaster count (e.g., <15) reduces confidence in the median; flag months where pUSHST=C drops materially below its average, as thin participation inflates the apparent precision of pUSHST=M.

USPMI=ECI.meaning: Actual release of ISM Manufacturing PMI — the headline diffusion index from the Institute for Supply Management's survey of ~300 manufacturing firms. Released first business day of each month at 10:00 ET.
USPMI=ECI.how_to_use: Above 50 = expansion; sub-50 sustained signals manufacturing recession. Most-watched single business-cycle gauge in US data. Compare against Median Consensus (pUSPMI=M) — surprise drives Treasury yields, USD, and equity sector rotation.

pUSPMI=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI from Reuters' poll of Wall Street economists, compiled ~1 week ahead of release.
pUSPMI=M.how_to_use: The 'expected' PMI. Markets trade the surprise (Actual minus Median). The 50 line is psychologically critical — consensus crossing back above signals a cycle inflection.

pUSPMI=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI, generated by Refinitiv's quantitative model using macro leading indicators.
pUSPMI=F.how_to_use: Use alongside the Median Consensus (pUSPMI=M) to identify model-vs-street divergences; a large gap can signal an unusually directional risk ahead of the print.

pUSPMI=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Manufacturing PMI — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation between the actual release and the street consensus.
pUSPMI=P.how_to_use: A positive value implies the actual is likely to beat consensus; useful for pre-positioning or setting asymmetric options strategies around the release.

pUSPMI=E.meaning: Mean (arithmetic average) forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI across all poll contributors, published alongside the median.
pUSPMI=E.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median — a large spread indicates skew in the distribution of forecasts, signaling asymmetric risk around the consensus view.

pUSPMI=O.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI — the single most commonly submitted forecast value among poll participants.
pUSPMI=O.how_to_use: Shows where the largest cluster of forecasters sits; useful for identifying the 'modal scenario' when mean and median differ significantly.

pUSPMI=L.meaning: Minimum (most bearish) individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI submitted in the Reuters poll.
pUSPMI=L.how_to_use: Marks the bear-case boundary; if the actual print approaches or breaches this level it signals an outsized negative surprise.

pUSPMI=H.meaning: Maximum (most bullish) individual forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI submitted in the Reuters poll.
pUSPMI=H.how_to_use: Marks the bull-case boundary; use with pUSPMI=L to define the full forecast range and gauge how wide market uncertainty is ahead of the release.

pUSPMI=T.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSPMI=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Manufacturing PMI in the Reuters poll — a direct measure of economist disagreement.
pUSPMI=T.how_to_use: Elevated standard deviation before a release implies higher macro uncertainty; options vol tends to be richer when forecast dispersion is wide.

pUSPMI=C.description: ISM Manufacturing PMI — Number of Forecasters
pUSPMI=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Manufacturing PMI in the current Reuters poll.
pUSPMI=C.how_to_use: Higher participation increases consensus reliability; a low count relative to prior months may reflect unusual uncertainty or a thin pre-holiday survey.

USEPMI=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment sub-index, reflecting net hiring intentions in services-sector firms surveyed by ISM.
USEPMI=ECI.how_to_use: A key early read on services-sector payrolls ahead of the monthly BLS report; sustained sub-50 readings flag deterioration in the dominant US employment sector.

pUSEPMI=M.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Median Consensus
pUSEPMI=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index from the Reuters economist poll.
pUSEPMI=M.how_to_use: Benchmark for expected services labor demand; a beat vs. consensus strengthens the pre-NFP bullish labor narrative and supports risk assets.

pUSEPMI=F.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — SmartEconomics Forecast
pUSEPMI=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index.
pUSEPMI=F.how_to_use: Model forecast vs. street median (pUSEPMI=M) divergence highlights potential for upside or downside labor-market surprises in the services sector.

pUSEPMI=P.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Predicted Surprise
pUSEPMI=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index — SmartEconomics' estimate of actual minus consensus at release.
pUSEPMI=P.how_to_use: Use ahead of the services PMI release as a directional bias signal for the employment sub-index; feeds into pre-NFP positioning.

pUSEPMI=E.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Mean Forecast
pUSEPMI=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSEPMI=E.how_to_use: Use alongside median to detect distributional asymmetry; a mean below the median signals a fatter left tail in services employment expectations.

pUSEPMI=O.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Mode Forecast
pUSEPMI=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index — the most frequently submitted individual estimate in the poll.
pUSEPMI=O.how_to_use: Identifies the modal labor-demand scenario; useful when skewed distributions make the mean or median a poor representation of central tendency.

pUSEPMI=L.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Min Forecast
pUSEPMI=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
pUSEPMI=L.how_to_use: Sets the downside boundary for services hiring expectations; a print at or below this level implies a significant NFP downside risk in the services sector.

pUSEPMI=H.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Max Forecast
pUSEPMI=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index in the Reuters poll.
pUSEPMI=H.how_to_use: Sets the upside boundary for services hiring; a print above this level would be a strongly bullish pre-NFP signal.

pUSEPMI=T.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSEPMI=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index.
pUSEPMI=T.how_to_use: Higher dispersion signals uncertainty about the services labor market ahead of the release; use to calibrate NFP forecast confidence intervals.

pUSEPMI=C.description: ISM N-Mfg Employment Idx — Number of Forecasters
pUSEPMI=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for the ISM Non-Manufacturing Employment Index in the current Reuters poll.
pUSEPMI=C.how_to_use: Low participation signals limited forecaster coverage of this sub-index; treat the consensus with appropriate caution when the count is well below historical norms.

USNPMI=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the ISM Non-Manufacturing (Services) PMI — the headline composite index from ISM's survey of ~400 services-sector firms. Released third business day of each month at 10:00 ET.
USNPMI=ECI.how_to_use: Services represent ~80% of US GDP, so this index is the dominant PMI for aggregate cycle tracking. A sustained move below 50 signals services recession; compare to pUSNPMI=M for the market-moving surprise.

pUSNPMI=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI from Reuters' economist poll, published ~1 week before the release.
pUSNPMI=M.how_to_use: Benchmark for the expected services activity level. The actual-vs-median surprise moves risk assets, particularly rate-sensitive equities and front-end Treasuries.

pUSNPMI=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI, using high-frequency consumption and services activity data.
pUSNPMI=F.how_to_use: A model forecast diverging from street median (pUSNPMI=M) flags potential for a larger-than-expected surprise in the services sector.

pUSNPMI=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation from the street consensus.
pUSNPMI=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise in services activity has bullish macro implications; trade-through into consumer discretionary equities and risk-on FX.

pUSNPMI=E.meaning: Mean forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSNPMI=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect skew; a mean well below median implies a fat left tail in the services activity distribution ahead of the release.

pUSNPMI=O.meaning: Mode forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — the most frequently submitted forecast value among poll participants.
pUSNPMI=O.how_to_use: Reveals where the largest consensus cluster sits; useful when mean and median diverge and a clearer modal scenario is needed.

pUSNPMI=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — the bear-case floor in the Reuters poll.
pUSNPMI=L.how_to_use: A print at or below this value signals an extreme negative surprise in services activity, consistent with rapid deterioration in the business cycle.

pUSNPMI=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — the bull-case ceiling in the Reuters poll.
pUSNPMI=H.how_to_use: A print above this level indicates an exceptional beat; compare the range (H minus L) across months to track how uncertain forecasters are about services conditions.

pUSNPMI=T.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSNPMI=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI — a quantitative measure of forecast uncertainty.
pUSNPMI=T.how_to_use: Elevated dispersion implies higher implied vol is warranted for rates and equity products sensitive to the services PMI release.

pUSNPMI=C.description: ISM N-Mfg PMI — Number of Forecasters
pUSNPMI=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI in the current Reuters poll.
pUSNPMI=C.how_to_use: Validates consensus reliability; a large, stable panel count increases confidence in the median as a clean market signal.

USIPI=ECI.meaning: Actual year-over-year change in US Import Prices from the BLS, the 12-month cumulative view of import inflation that smooths monthly volatility from energy price swings.
USIPI=ECI.how_to_use: The YoY rate is more relevant for trend-inflation monitoring and TIPS breakeven analysis; compare with the MoM actual (USIMP=ECI) to distinguish trend from noise and assess tariff pass-through over time.

USIP=ECI.meaning: Actual month-on-month change in the Federal Reserve's Industrial Production Index, covering manufacturing, mining, and utilities output — released mid-month for the prior month.
USIP=ECI.how_to_use: Broader than ISM surveys as it measures actual output volume; compare to ISM Manufacturing PMI (USPMI=ECI) to reconcile hard vs. soft data. A negative print confirms factory contraction signaled by sub-50 PMI readings.

pUSIP=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for Industrial Production MM from the Reuters economist poll, compiled ahead of the Fed's mid-month release.
pUSIP=M.how_to_use: Benchmark for expected factory output; the actual-vs-median surprise is market-moving for industrials equities, USD, and rate expectations.

pUSIP=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for Industrial Production MM, incorporating energy output, manufacturing hours, and utility consumption signals.
pUSIP=F.how_to_use: A model forecast diverging from street median (pUSIP=M) flags potential for an outsized Industrial Production surprise.

pUSIP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for Industrial Production MM — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will beat or miss the street consensus.
pUSIP=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise is bullish for manufacturing-sector equities, commodities, and cyclical currencies; use alongside ISM surprises for macro consistency checks.

pUSIP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for Industrial Production MM across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSIP=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect skew; a mean below median implies tail risk of a larger-than-expected output decline, consistent with energy or utility drag scenarios.

pUSIP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for Industrial Production MM — the most frequently submitted individual estimate in the Reuters poll.
pUSIP=O.how_to_use: Identifies the modal output growth scenario; useful when energy-sector surprises create a bimodal distribution in forecaster estimates.

pUSIP=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for Industrial Production MM — the most pessimistic output view in the Reuters poll.
pUSIP=L.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk for output; a print at or below this level implies a significant industrial recession signal, likely to weigh on cyclical assets.

pUSIP=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for Industrial Production MM — the most optimistic output view in the Reuters poll.
pUSIP=H.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk; a print above this level would be a strong beat on hard industrial data, supporting broader cyclical equity rotation.

pUSIP=T.description: Industrial Production MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSIP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for Industrial Production MM — measures disagreement on the pace of output growth.
pUSIP=T.how_to_use: High dispersion before the release suggests elevated uncertainty — often tied to energy sector volatility or weather distortions in utilities output.

pUSIP=C.description: Industrial Production MM — Number of Forecasters
pUSIP=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for Industrial Production MM in the current Reuters poll.
pUSIP=C.how_to_use: A large, stable panel count confirms the median as a reliable consensus signal for this important hard-data release.

USTBAL=ECI.meaning: Actual monthly US International Trade Balance (goods + services) from Census/BEA, released ~5-7th of the following month. A negative value indicates a deficit; readings typically run -$60B to -$100B.
USTBAL=ECI.how_to_use: Compare against the Reuters poll median (pUSTBAL=M) to gauge the surprise; a miss wider than $5B can move USD, equity futures, and GDP nowcast models that treat net exports as a direct component.

pUSTBAL=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for the US International Trade Balance from the Reuters economist poll, collected ~1 week before release. The median is the most widely cited benchmark for market expectations.
pUSTBAL=M.how_to_use: Plot alongside USTBAL=ECI to track revision history and surprise magnitude; persistent deficit misses vs consensus signal structural import demand shifts or export softness relevant for USD and sector ETFs.

pUSTBAL=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for the US Trade Balance, derived algorithmically from high-frequency data inputs rather than a human panel survey.
pUSTBAL=F.how_to_use: Compare to pUSTBAL=M to assess whether systematic models are more bullish or bearish on the deficit than human forecasters; divergences can signal that the model has captured recent import/export data not yet in consensus.

pUSTBAL=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the US Trade Balance — the systematic component of expected deviation between the actual release and the median poll forecast.
pUSTBAL=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise implies the actual print will likely beat (narrower deficit than) consensus; use alongside pUSTBAL=T to assess risk-reward for positioning around the release.

pUSTBAL=E.meaning: Mean (arithmetic average) forecast for the US Trade Balance from the Reuters panel, which unlike the median can be skewed by outlier forecasters with extreme deficit or surplus views.
pUSTBAL=E.how_to_use: When pUSTBAL=E diverges materially from pUSTBAL=M, the distribution of forecasts is skewed; a mean more negative than the median implies downside tail risk to the deficit that markets may be underpricing.

pUSTBAL=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the US Trade Balance — the single most frequently cited estimate among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSTBAL=O.how_to_use: A mode well away from the median indicates a bimodal or multi-clustered distribution of forecaster views, often reflecting genuine uncertainty around trade policy; use alongside pUSTBAL=L/H to map the full range.

pUSTBAL=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic / widest-deficit) forecast for the US Trade Balance in the Reuters poll, representing the most bearish economist estimate.
pUSTBAL=L.how_to_use: Use with pUSTBAL=H to define the full forecast range; if the actual print falls outside this range it is a major surprise that will drive outsized USD and equity moves.

pUSTBAL=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic / narrowest-deficit) forecast for the US Trade Balance in the Reuters poll, representing the most bullish economist estimate.
pUSTBAL=H.how_to_use: The H-L range together with pUSTBAL=T quantifies consensus uncertainty ahead of the release; use to size option structures or set stop levels around the trade data event.

pUSTBAL=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts in the Reuters US Trade Balance poll, measuring the degree of disagreement among economists ahead of the release.
pUSTBAL=T.how_to_use: Elevated standard deviation (relative to recent history) warns of high event risk; combine with pUSTBAL=M to construct an implied confidence interval and calibrate position sizing for the release.

pUSTBAL=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting forecasts in the Reuters US Trade Balance poll for the current release cycle.
pUSTBAL=C.how_to_use: A low forecaster count (fewer than ~15) reduces reliability of the median and standard deviation; track over time to ensure sample size is sufficient before relying on consensus statistics.

USKCCI=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the Kansas City Fed Composite Activity Index, combining current conditions and future expectations of business activity across the 10th Fed District.
USKCCI=ECI.how_to_use: The composite blends current activity with a forward-looking expectations component; use alongside the manufacturing sub-index (USKCMF=ECI) to distinguish momentum from direction.

USKCMF=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the Kansas City Fed Manufacturing Activity Index, a diffusion index of factory conditions across the 10th Federal Reserve District (Kansas, Colorado, Nebraska, and surrounding states).
USKCMF=ECI.how_to_use: Regional Fed surveys supplement the national ISM; a consistent divergence between KC Fed and ISM Manufacturing (USPMI=ECI) highlights geographic variation in the industrial cycle.

USFOUT=ECI.meaning: Actual month-on-month change in the manufacturing-only component of the Federal Reserve's Industrial Production Index, stripping out mining and utilities.
USFOUT=ECI.how_to_use: Provides a cleaner read on factory sector health than total Industrial Production (USIP=ECI); compare to ISM Manufacturing PMI (USPMI=ECI) to reconcile survey vs. hard output data.

pUSFOUT=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for Manufacturing Output MM from the Reuters economist poll.
pUSFOUT=M.how_to_use: Benchmark for expected factory output growth; a beat vs. consensus provides hard confirmation of what ISM surveys have been signaling about manufacturing conditions.

pUSFOUT=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for Manufacturing Output MM.
pUSFOUT=F.how_to_use: Use model divergence from street median (pUSFOUT=M) to identify potential hard-data surprises in the factory sector, particularly when ISM surveys diverge from output trends.

pUSFOUT=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for Manufacturing Output MM — SmartEconomics' estimate of the likely deviation from street consensus at release.
pUSFOUT=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise strengthens the bullish manufacturing narrative; use in conjunction with ISM PMI surprises for a consistent cyclical sector view.

pUSFOUT=E.meaning: Mean forecast for Manufacturing Output MM across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSFOUT=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect distributional skew; a lower mean relative to median implies downside tail risk to factory output growth.

pUSFOUT=O.meaning: Mode forecast for Manufacturing Output MM — the most frequently submitted individual estimate in the poll.
pUSFOUT=O.how_to_use: Reveals the modal factory output scenario; useful when auto-sector or supply-chain distortions create a bimodal forecast distribution.

pUSFOUT=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for Manufacturing Output MM — the most pessimistic factory output view in the Reuters poll.
pUSFOUT=L.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk for manufacturing output; a print at or below this level confirms a severe factory contraction consistent with the bearish tail scenario.

pUSFOUT=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for Manufacturing Output MM — the most optimistic factory output view in the Reuters poll.
pUSFOUT=H.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk boundary; a print above this level confirms strong manufacturing momentum and supports cyclical equity and commodity positions.

pUSFOUT=T.description: Manuf Output MM — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSFOUT=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for Manufacturing Output MM — measures forecast uncertainty around factory production.
pUSFOUT=T.how_to_use: High dispersion suggests uncertainty about supply-chain and production conditions; use to calibrate width of confidence bands in manufacturing output models.

pUSFOUT=C.description: Manuf Output MM — Number of Forecasters
pUSFOUT=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for Manufacturing Output MM in the current Reuters poll.
pUSFOUT=C.how_to_use: Validates the reliability of the consensus; a declining participant count may reflect reduced forecaster coverage of this sub-component relative to headline Industrial Production.

USNAHB=ECI.meaning: Actual release of the NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index — a monthly survey of home builder sentiment scored 0-100, with 50 as the expansion/contraction threshold. Released mid-month, one day before Housing Starts.
USNAHB=ECI.how_to_use: Leads housing starts by 1-2 months and is the primary real-time gauge of new residential construction demand; a sustained move below 50 signals housing sector weakness with implications for consumer spending and GDP.

pUSNAHB=M.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Median Consensus
pUSNAHB=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index from the Reuters economist poll.
pUSNAHB=M.how_to_use: Sets the expected builder-sentiment baseline. A beat vs. consensus (USNAHB=ECI above pUSNAHB=M) is bullish for homebuilder equities and residential REITs.

pUSNAHB=F.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — SmartEconomics Forecast
pUSNAHB=F.meaning: SmartEconomics machine-learning forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index, incorporating mortgage rate trends and permit data.
pUSNAHB=F.how_to_use: Model forecast vs. street median (pUSNAHB=M) divergence can signal unusual rate-sensitivity risk in builder sentiment ahead of the release.

pUSNAHB=P.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Predicted Surprise
pUSNAHB=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the NAHB Housing Market Index — SmartEconomics' estimate of whether the actual will beat or miss the street consensus.
pUSNAHB=P.how_to_use: A positive predicted surprise implies stronger builder sentiment than expected; bullish for housing-related equities and mortgage-backed securities.

pUSNAHB=E.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Mean Forecast
pUSNAHB=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index across all Reuters poll contributors.
pUSNAHB=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to detect distributional skew in housing sentiment expectations; a mean below median implies tail risk of a sharp builder confidence drop.

pUSNAHB=O.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Mode Forecast
pUSNAHB=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index — the most frequently submitted estimate in the Reuters poll.
pUSNAHB=O.how_to_use: Identifies the most common builder-sentiment scenario among forecasters; useful when mean and median are pulled apart by outlier estimates.

pUSNAHB=L.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Min Forecast
pUSNAHB=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index — the most pessimistic builder-sentiment view in the poll.
pUSNAHB=L.how_to_use: Defines the downside risk for housing activity; a print at or below this level signals an outsized deterioration in builder confidence, bearish for homebuilder stocks.

pUSNAHB=H.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Max Forecast
pUSNAHB=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index — the most optimistic builder-sentiment view in the poll.
pUSNAHB=H.how_to_use: Defines the upside risk; a print above this level represents a significant beat in housing conditions, likely to lift homebuilder equities sharply.

pUSNAHB=T.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSNAHB=T.meaning: Standard deviation of all individual forecasts for the NAHB Housing Market Index — a direct measure of forecast uncertainty.
pUSNAHB=T.how_to_use: High dispersion signals elevated uncertainty about housing conditions — typically linked to sharp swings in mortgage rates; use to calibrate risk around the mid-month housing release.

pUSNAHB=C.description: NAHB Housing Market Indx — Number of Forecasters
pUSNAHB=C.meaning: Number of economists who submitted a forecast for the NAHB Housing Market Index in the current Reuters poll.
pUSNAHB=C.how_to_use: Higher participation validates the median as a robust consensus signal; a low count may reflect limited coverage of this housing indicator among poll participants.

USNDXA=ECI.meaning: Actual MoM percent change in US nondefense capital goods orders excluding aircraft — the 'core capex' proxy — from Census Bureau.
USNDXA=ECI.how_to_use: Best single indicator for US business investment intentions; leads Industrial Production by 1-3 months. Sustained positive trend supports GDP upgrades and equity risk appetite.

pUSNDXA=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for nondefense capital goods ex-aircraft (core capex) MoM change from the Reuters pre-release poll.
pUSNDXA=M.how_to_use: Benchmark for capex surprise; positive print vs median supports business investment narrative and leads Industrial Production revisions upward.

pUSNDXA=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for core capex (nondefense cap goods ex-air) MoM change.
pUSNDXA=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median to detect model-driven capex signal; macro model inputs (ISM Capital Goods, PPI metals) often lead analyst surveys on this series.

pUSNDXA=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for core capex (nondefense capital goods ex-air) MoM change.
pUSNDXA=P.how_to_use: Key pre-release risk gauge for business investment tone; strong positive predicted surprise alongside rising ISM Capex is a GDP growth signal.

pUSNDXA=E.meaning: Mean forecast for core capex MoM change across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSNDXA=E.how_to_use: Compare with median; outlier bullish capex views (M&A-driven equipment orders) can pull mean above median.

pUSNDXA=O.meaning: Mode forecast for core capex MoM change among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSNDXA=O.how_to_use: Tight mode-median alignment confirms consensus on business investment trend; wide gap flags analyst disagreement about capex cycle phase.

pUSNDXA=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for core capex MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSNDXA=L.how_to_use: Defines bearish capex scenario; print below min signals capex contraction that may prompt downward GDP tracking revisions.

pUSNDXA=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for core capex MoM change in the Reuters poll.
pUSNDXA=H.how_to_use: Defines bullish capex scenario; print above max indicates broad investment acceleration, typically supportive of industrial and tech equities.

pUSNDXA=T.description: Nondefe Cap Ex-Air — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSNDXA=T.meaning: Standard deviation of core capex MoM forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSNDXA=T.how_to_use: Elevated StdDev preceding a cycle turn (recession or recovery) is typical; monitor alongside GDPNow capex tracker for consistency.

pUSNDXA=C.description: Nondefe Cap Ex-Air — Number of Forecasters
pUSNDXA=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting a core capex forecast in the current Reuters poll.
pUSNDXA=C.how_to_use: Core capex typically draws fewer respondents than headline durables; low count reduces statistical reliability of median and mean.

USPROP=ECI.meaning: Actual release of US Non-farm Business Sector Labor Productivity (Preliminary Estimate) — the BLS measure of output per hour worked, released ~60 days after quarter-end.
USPROP=ECI.how_to_use: Productivity is the key long-run driver of non-inflationary growth. A beat versus pUSPROP=M is bullish for equities (more output per worker) and lowers unit labor cost, reducing Fed concern about wage-driven inflation.

pUSPROP=M.meaning: Median Consensus forecast for the US Non-farm Business Sector Productivity Preliminary Estimate from the Reuters economist poll.
pUSPROP=M.how_to_use: The consensus median is the standard against which to measure the Productivity surprise. A productivity surprise changes the perceived non-inflationary speed limit of the economy and affects Fed forward guidance narratives.

pUSPROP=F.meaning: Refinitiv SmartEconomics model forecast for the Productivity Preliminary Estimate — an algorithmic nowcast blending output data (GDP) and hours-worked data from the BLS.
pUSPROP=F.how_to_use: SmartEconomics productivity forecast reflects a mechanical calculation from GDP growth (already known at Prelim stage) and hours worked. Divergence from pUSPROP=M may signal a specific hours-worked data source difference.

pUSPROP=P.meaning: Predicted Surprise for the Productivity Preliminary Estimate — Refinitiv's directional signal indicating whether the output-per-hour print will beat or miss consensus.
pUSPROP=P.how_to_use: An upside Productivity Predicted Surprise alongside a downside Unit Labor Cost expected surprise (if available) forms a powerful benign macro narrative for risk assets and duration.

pUSPROP=E.meaning: Mean forecast for the Productivity Preliminary Estimate across all economists in the Reuters poll — arithmetic average of output-per-hour forecasts.
pUSPROP=E.how_to_use: Mean-median divergence for Productivity reflects outlier views on hours worked or output. A mean significantly above median suggests some economists expect a surge in output relative to labor input.

pUSPROP=O.meaning: Mode forecast for the Productivity Preliminary Estimate — the single most commonly submitted point estimate by economists in the Reuters survey.
pUSPROP=O.how_to_use: For Productivity, the mode often clusters at a round number near consensus trend (historically ~2%). A mode far from the median indicates the distribution is bimodal — some economists expect a structural shift.

pUSPROP=L.meaning: Minimum (most pessimistic) forecast for the Productivity Preliminary Estimate — the bear case for labor efficiency in the quarter.
pUSPROP=L.how_to_use: A print at or below the Productivity Min implies output per worker came in below all surveyed economists' expectations, which raises unit labor costs and is a potential inflationary catalyst.

pUSPROP=H.meaning: Maximum (most optimistic) forecast for the Productivity Preliminary Estimate — the bull case for labor efficiency in the Reuters economist survey.
pUSPROP=H.how_to_use: A print above the Productivity Max signals an exceptional output-per-hour surge, potentially driven by technology adoption or unusual hours data. Such a print is structurally bullish for potential GDP estimates.

pUSPROP=T.meaning: Standard deviation of forecasts for the Productivity Preliminary Estimate — measures analyst disagreement about quarterly output-per-hour growth.
pUSPROP=T.how_to_use: High Productivity StdDev often reflects uncertainty about hours-worked data (which feeds directly into the calculation). Rising StdDev over time may signal increased structural uncertainty about labor market efficiency trends.

pUSPROP=C.meaning: Number of economists submitting Productivity Preliminary forecasts in the Reuters poll — the sample size for this consensus.
pUSPROP=C.how_to_use: Productivity is a less heavily polled indicator than GDP; a count below 30 means the consensus statistics should be treated with caution. Monitor for declining participation over time as a sign of reduced institutional coverage.

USSSQ=ECI.meaning: Actual USDA quarterly US soybean stocks (on-farm + off-farm), released four times per year in the Grain Stocks report.
USSSQ=ECI.how_to_use: Major price-moving report for CBOT soybeans (ZS); stocks below consensus trigger limit-up moves. December 1 stocks are especially critical for new-crop supply outlook.

pUSSSQ=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for USDA quarterly soybean stocks from the Reuters pre-release poll.
pUSSSQ=M.how_to_use: Primary benchmark for CBOT ZS surprise; actual below median is strongly bullish for soybeans — these quarterly reports drive multi-cent daily moves in futures.

pUSSSQ=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for USDA quarterly soybean stocks.
pUSSSQ=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median; model incorporates crush pace, export inspections, and USDA supply/use balance adjustments to estimate residual stocks.

pUSSSQ=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for USDA quarterly soybean stocks — directional estimate of actual vs consensus deviation.
pUSSSQ=P.how_to_use: High-value pre-release signal for CBOT soy positioning; a strongly negative predicted surprise (tighter stocks) ahead of Dec 1 or Mar 1 stocks supports aggressive long ZS trades.

pUSSSQ=E.meaning: Mean forecast for USDA quarterly soybean stocks across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSSSQ=E.how_to_use: Compare with median to assess distribution skew; large crop years may generate outlier high-stocks forecasts pulling mean above median.

pUSSSQ=O.meaning: Mode forecast for USDA quarterly soybean stocks among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSSSQ=O.how_to_use: Mode near median confirms tight analyst consensus; mode far from median indicates split views on on-farm vs commercial storage allocation.

pUSSSQ=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for USDA quarterly soybean stocks in the Reuters poll.
pUSSSQ=L.how_to_use: Defines the most bullish (tightest supply) analyst scenario; actual below min triggers strongest soybean futures buying as all scenarios are exceeded.

pUSSSQ=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for USDA quarterly soybean stocks in the Reuters poll.
pUSSSQ=H.how_to_use: Defines the most bearish (most abundant supply) scenario; actual above max triggers downside ZS price pressure as supply exceeds all analyst estimates.

pUSSSQ=T.description: Qtrly Grain Stocks-Soy — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSSSQ=T.meaning: Standard deviation of USDA quarterly soybean stocks forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSSSQ=T.how_to_use: High StdDev ahead of the June stocks (new-crop transition) reflects maximum uncertainty in on-farm usage estimates; low StdDev in late-season indicates predictable drawdown.

pUSSSQ=C.description: Qtrly Grain Stocks-Soy — Number of Forecasters
pUSSSQ=C.meaning: Number of analysts submitting a quarterly soybean stocks forecast in the current Reuters poll.
pUSSSQ=C.how_to_use: Grain stocks polls attract a specialist agri panel; validate consensus reliability — low count near major USDA reports increases surprise risk.

USWSQ=ECI.meaning: Actual USDA quarterly US wheat stocks (all positions: on-farm + off-farm) released in the Grain Stocks report four times per year.
USWSQ=ECI.how_to_use: Price-moving report for CBOT wheat futures (ZW); tighter-than-expected stocks drive export premium and affect global flour/bread price chain.

pUSWSQ=M.meaning: Median consensus forecast for USDA quarterly wheat stocks from the Reuters pre-release poll.
pUSWSQ=M.how_to_use: Primary benchmark for CBOT ZW surprise; lower-than-expected stocks relative to median is bullish for wheat, especially when global supply is already tight.

pUSWSQ=F.meaning: SmartEconomics model-based forecast for USDA quarterly wheat stocks.
pUSWSQ=F.how_to_use: Compare vs median; model integrates USDA weekly export inspections, flour mill usage, and feed residual estimates to project stocks.

pUSWSQ=P.meaning: Predicted surprise for USDA quarterly wheat stocks — directional estimate of actual vs consensus deviation.
pUSWSQ=P.how_to_use: High-value pre-release signal for ZW futures; in low global stock environments (e.g., post-Ukraine supply shock), negative predicted surprise has outsized price impact.

pUSWSQ=E.meaning: Mean forecast for USDA quarterly wheat stocks across all Reuters poll respondents.
pUSWSQ=E.how_to_use: Compare mean vs median to assess distribution shape; large winter wheat crop estimates can produce outlier high-stock forecasts that pull mean above median.

pUSWSQ=O.meaning: Mode forecast for USDA quarterly wheat stocks among Reuters poll respondents.
pUSWSQ=O.how_to_use: Mode clustering near median confirms tight consensus on wheat supply-use balance; divergence signals uncertainty in feed-wheat usage or export pace.

pUSWSQ=L.meaning: Minimum individual forecast for USDA quarterly wheat stocks in the Reuters poll.
pUSWSQ=L.how_to_use: Defines the most bullish (tightest supply) analyst scenario for wheat; actual below min is a limit-up ZW signal in tight global markets.

pUSWSQ=H.meaning: Maximum individual forecast for USDA quarterly wheat stocks in the Reuters poll.
pUSWSQ=H.how_to_use: Defines the most bearish (most abundant supply) wheat scenario; actual above max is a negative price signal for ZW, especially in large domestic harvest years.

pUSWSQ=T.description: Qtrly Grain Stocks-Wheat — Forecast Standard Deviation
pUSWSQ=T.meaning: Standard deviation of USDA quarterly wheat stocks forecasts across Reuters poll respondents.
pUSWSQ=T.how_to_use: Elevated StdDev in the June stocks report reflects maximum uncertainty about winter-wheat harvest size; cross-check with USDA crop condition ratings.

pUSWSQ=C.description: Qtrly Grain Stocks-Wheat — Number of Forecasters
pUSWSQ=C.meaning: Number of analysts submitting a quarterly wheat stocks forecast in the current Reuters poll.
pUSWSQ=C.how_to_use: Agri specialist panel similar in size to soy stocks poll; low count increases noise in consensus estimates — validate with USDA export inspection data.
